Exploiting gateway rate-limit or routing-rule gaps to overwhelm backend capacity
scopeExcludes: Provider-wide shared-infrastructure attacks outside the organization's own resource (ITID-41611)
Cloud identity/authentication service disruption (ITID-41613)
ITID-41612.severity: High since the load balancer/gateway is typically the single entry point for all backend services.
ITID-41612.priority: P1 while the gateway is saturated and blocking legitimate traffic.
ITID-41612.escalation: Escalate to the cloud platform team immediately to apply auto-scaling, WAF rules, or provider-native DDoS protection.
indicators: Gateway/load-balancer request or connection metrics at configured capacity limits
5xx error rates spiking specifically at the gateway layer while backends remain healthy
Traffic concentrated on a narrow set of gateway endpoints from anomalous source patterns
vectors: HTTP request flood targeting a specific API gateway route
Connection-exhaustion attack against load-balancer listener capacity
Exploiting an unauthenticated or lightly-protected gateway endpoint as an amplification point
rootCauses: Gateway rate limiting not configured or set too permissively
No provider-native DDoS/WAF protection enabled on the gateway
Auto-scaling thresholds set too high to react before saturation occurs
mitreTechniques: T1499.002 Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
controls: Provider-native DDoS protection and WAF enabled on the gateway
Gateway-level rate limiting and request-size/complexity limits
Auto-scaling with aggressive thresholds tuned for burst absorption
ITID-41612.detection: Strong technical signal from gateway/load-balancer request, connection, and error-rate telemetry.
ITID-41612.response: Enable or tighten provider-native DDoS/WAF protection, apply emergency rate limits, and scale gateway capacity while identifying and blocking attack sources.
metrics: Peak gateway request/connection rate during incidents
Time to enable emergency DDoS/WAF protection
5xx error rate during and after mitigation
sops: Cloud Gateway/Load Balancer Incident Response SOP
ITID-41612.notes: Differentiator within Cloud Service Disruption: this leaf is a direct attack on the organization's own ingress resource, distinct from provider-wide outages (ITID-41611) or identity-service disruption (ITID-41613).

playbook.name: Cloud Load Balancer/API Gateway Overload Attack
playbook.description: An attack targeting the organization's cloud-hosted load balancer or API gateway is overwhelming its request-handling capacity, denying access to backend services.

steps.title: Confirm overload at the load balancer/API gateway layer
steps.desc: Review load balancer and API gateway metrics (connection counts, request rate, latency, error codes) to confirm the bottleneck is at this layer rather than backend compute.
steps.guidance: Look for 5xx/throttling errors originating at the gateway and elevated connection-table utilization; compare against provider service quotas/limits.
steps.outcome: Overload confirmed at the load balancer/API gateway layer with metrics documented.
steps.abort: If backend services show the primary resource exhaustion, redirect investigation to backend capacity rather than gateway.

steps.title: Open provider support ticket and request gateway quota/limit increase
steps.desc: Escalate to the cloud provider's support channel to report the overload and request an emergency increase to gateway connection/throughput quotas if the limit itself is the binding constraint.
steps.outcome: Support ticket filed; quota increase applied if available and appropriate.

steps.title: Sustain mitigation until attack traffic subsides
steps.desc: Continue monitoring and tuning gateway rules until the overload condition is fully resolved.
steps.outcome: Gateway operating within normal capacity thresholds.

steps.title: Validate backend service restoration and remove temporary limits
steps.desc: Confirm backend services are receiving normal traffic and roll back emergency rate limits/quota changes in a controlled manner.
steps.outcome: Full service restoration confirmed with normal performance baselines.

steps.title: Document incident and review gateway capacity/resilience design
steps.desc: Capture timeline and recommend gateway capacity headroom, multi-region redundancy, or provider quota adjustments to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Identify attack traffic pattern and source distribution
steps.desc: Analyze request logs to determine whether the overload is from a concentrated set of sources or widely distributed, and identify the specific request patterns causing overload.
steps.outcome: Attack pattern and source characteristics documented.

steps.title: Apply rate limiting and request filtering at the gateway
steps.desc: Configure or tighten rate-limiting rules, WAF policies, or IP/geo-based filtering directly on the load balancer/API gateway to shed attack traffic.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic reduced at the gateway; legitimate request success rate improves.

steps.title: Fail over to a secondary gateway/region if overload persists
steps.desc: If gateway-level mitigation is insufficient, evaluate routing traffic to a secondary gateway deployment or region.
steps.outcome: Traffic rerouted successfully where a secondary path exists.
steps.abort: If no secondary gateway path exists, continue with rate limiting and provider escalation only.

ITID-41613.def: A denial-of-service incident in which an adversary's attack against a cloud identity provider or authentication service (e.g., SSO, OAuth token issuance, MFA validation) causes widespread login failure, blocking legitimate users from accessing applications that depend on it even though those applications themselves remain otherwise healthy.
ITID-41613.purpose: Captures denial of service specifically affecting the cloud identity/authentication service, causing widespread login failure across dependent applications regardless of their individual health.
scopeIncludes: Attacks against SSO/IdP token-issuance or validation endpoints causing widespread authentication failure
MFA-validation-service overload preventing users from completing login
Credential-stuffing-scale traffic that saturates the authentication service's capacity (impact is availability, not the credential-theft outcome)
scopeExcludes: Attacks against the general API gateway or load balancer unrelated to authentication (ITID-41612)
Credential-stuffing/account-takeover attacks whose primary objective is unauthorized access rather than service disruption (tracked under the relevant identity-attack domain)
ITID-41613.severity: High since authentication is a single point of dependency for most or all downstream applications.
ITID-41613.priority: P1 while login failures are widespread across dependent applications.
ITID-41613.escalation: Escalate immediately to identity/platform engineering and communicate impact broadly, since the blast radius spans every application relying on the identity service.
indicators: Spike in authentication failures/timeouts across multiple unrelated applications simultaneously
Identity-provider capacity metrics (token issuance rate, MFA validation latency) at or near limits
Support/help-desk ticket surge specifically about login failures
vectors: Volumetric request flood against SSO/IdP endpoints
Large-scale automated login/MFA attempts saturating validation capacity
Exploiting an inefficient authentication code path (e.g., expensive password-hash verification) at scale
rootCauses: No rate limiting or anomaly-based throttling on authentication endpoints
Identity service sized without headroom for burst/attack traffic
Lack of provider-native DDoS protection specifically applied to the identity service
mitreTechniques: T1499.002 Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
controls: Rate limiting and anomaly-based throttling on authentication/MFA endpoints
Provider-native DDoS protection applied specifically to the identity service
Capacity headroom and auto-scaling sized for burst authentication traffic
ITID-41613.detection: Strong technical signal from authentication-failure-rate and identity-service capacity telemetry correlated across dependent applications.
ITID-41613.response: Apply emergency rate limiting on authentication endpoints, scale identity-service capacity, and communicate impact and workarounds to affected application owners and users.
metrics: Authentication failure rate during incidents
Number of dependent applications impacted
Time to restore normal login success rate
ITID-41613.notes: Differentiator within Cloud Service Disruption: this leaf isolates the identity/authentication dependency as the specific attack target, distinct from generic gateway attacks (ITID-41612).

playbook.name: Cloud Identity/Authentication Service Disruption (Widespread Login Failure)
playbook.description: A disruption to a cloud identity/authentication provider (e.g., SSO/IdP) is causing widespread login failures across organizational applications, denying user access.

steps.title: Confirm identity provider outage via provider status and internal auth logs
steps.desc: Check the identity provider's status dashboard and internal authentication/SSO logs to confirm the disruption is provider-side and quantify login failure rate.
steps.guidance: Correlate spike in authentication failures/timeouts with provider-reported incidents; rule out an internal misconfiguration (e.g., certificate expiry, SAML config change) as the cause first.
steps.outcome: Outage confirmed as identity-provider-side (attack or provider fault) with failure-rate metrics documented.
steps.abort: If internal SSO configuration (expired cert, metadata mismatch) is the cause, redirect to standard internal configuration-fix procedure.

steps.title: Open priority support ticket with the identity provider
steps.desc: File a severity-1 ticket with the IdP vendor referencing the outage, and monitor their public incident communications for updates.
steps.outcome: Support ticket opened; escalation contact engaged where available.

steps.title: Monitor provider remediation and validate authentication restoration
steps.desc: Track the provider's incident resolution status and independently verify successful login flows across affected applications.
steps.outcome: Authentication confirmed fully restored across all affected applications.

steps.title: Deactivate break-glass access and restore normal SSO flow
steps.desc: Revoke any break-glass credentials/accounts used during the outage and confirm all users are authenticating normally through SSO.
steps.outcome: Break-glass access fully revoked; normal SSO authentication confirmed for all users.

steps.title: Document incident and review identity resilience/break-glass procedures
steps.desc: Capture timeline, break-glass usage audit, and evaluate whether secondary/backup authentication paths or provider redundancy are warranted.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with resilience recommendations tracked.

steps.title: Assess which applications and user populations are affected
steps.desc: Determine which internal and customer-facing applications depend on the disrupted identity provider and the scope of affected users.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented to prioritize communication and any break-glass access decisions.

steps.title: Activate break-glass/emergency access procedures for critical systems
steps.desc: For business-critical systems where prolonged login failure is unacceptable, invoke pre-defined break-glass local-authentication procedures under change-controlled, logged conditions.
steps.guidance: Break-glass access must be tightly scoped, time-boxed, and fully logged for post-incident audit; only invoke for systems where the business impact justifies bypassing SSO.
steps.outcome: Critical-system access restored via break-glass where justified, with all use logged for audit.
steps.abort: If no critical system requires it, do not invoke break-glass procedures — wait for provider restoration.

ITID-41614.def: A cloud-service-disruption incident confirmed as an attack against cloud-hosted infrastructure, but not yet classified into a specific mechanism (provider-wide attack, gateway/load-balancer attack, identity-service attack) pending further investigation.
ITID-41614.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cloud service disruption attacks that do not yet fit provider-wide, gateway-targeted, or identity-service classifications.
scopeIncludes: Newly observed cloud-service-disruption techniques not yet mapped to an existing sibling leaf
Ambiguous cloud-availability incidents pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any incident later confirmed as provider-wide disruption (ITID-41611), gateway/load-balancer attack (ITID-41612), or identity-service disruption (ITID-41613) — reclassify once confirmed
ITID-41614.severity: Medium-High by default pending classification given cloud dependencies are often broad; adjust once the specific mechanism and business impact are confirmed.
ITID-41614.priority: P2 pending triage, escalating per standard severity guidance once root cause is identified.
ITID-41614.escalation: Escalate to the SOC classification lead for prompt re-tagging into a specific sibling leaf once the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Elevated cloud service unavailability with an unconfirmed cause
Analyst uncertainty about which cloud-disruption mechanism applies
vectors: Unclassified/novel cloud-service-disruption technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Root cause not yet determined
controls: Standard cloud service monitoring and alerting pending classification
ITID-41614.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual root cause; this bucket itself is detected via generic cloud-availability alerting.
ITID-41614.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism and reclassify to the appropriate sibling ITID as soon as possible; apply standard cloud-disruption containment in the interim.
metrics: Number of incidents parked in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
Average time to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf
ITID-41614.notes: Catch-all intake leaf; used only during initial triage. Analysts should reclassify into ITID-41611/41612/41613 as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud Service Disruption
playbook.description: A targeted attack against a cloud service provider used by the organization has caused a general service disruption not otherwise classified into a more specific sub-type.

steps.title: Confirm provider-side disruption via status dashboards and internal monitoring
steps.desc: Cross-check internal service alerts against the cloud provider's status dashboard and any security advisories to confirm the disruption is provider-side and attack-related.
steps.outcome: Disruption confirmed as provider-side with evidence timestamped.
steps.abort: If no provider incident is reported, treat as an internal fault.
steps.tool: Cloud provider status dashboard, internal APM

steps.title: Open priority support ticket with the cloud provider
steps.desc: File a severity-1 support ticket referencing the incident and request status updates and mitigation guidance.
steps.outcome: Support ticket opened and acknowledged.

steps.title: Monitor provider remediation and independently validate restoration
steps.desc: Track provider incident updates and confirm via internal monitoring that services are genuinely restored.
steps.outcome: Provider-side issue confirmed resolved and independently verified.
steps.tool: Cloud provider status dashboard, internal APM

steps.title: Confirm full service restoration and fail back if applicable
steps.desc: Verify all affected services meet normal baselines and execute controlled fail-back if a secondary provider/region was used.
steps.outcome: Services fully restored to normal operation.

steps.title: Document incident and review provider resilience posture
steps.desc: Capture timeline, provider communication quality, and business impact; recommend resilience improvements.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Assess scope of organizational impact
steps.desc: Determine which services, applications, and user populations are affected.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented for stakeholder communication.

steps.title: Evaluate failover to secondary provider/region
steps.desc: If a failover path exists, assess whether activating it is warranted given the outage severity and duration.
steps.outcome: Failover executed where viable, or decision documented not to fail over.
steps.abort: If no failover path exists, focus on provider engagement and communication.

ITID-41621.def: A denial-of-service incident in which an adversary directs volumetric or connection-based traffic at CDN edge nodes/points-of-presence themselves, exhausting their local compute, connection, or bandwidth capacity and degrading content delivery even for cacheable content that would not normally reach the origin.
ITID-41621.purpose: Captures denial of service caused by an adversary overwhelming CDN edge node compute/network capacity directly, distinct from attacks that pass through to the origin.
scopeIncludes: Volumetric floods against edge-node bandwidth or connection capacity
TLS-handshake exhaustion attacks targeting edge-node compute capacity
Attacks concentrated on specific edge locations/points-of-presence to degrade regional delivery
scopeExcludes: Attacks specifically engineered to bypass cache and force origin load (ITID-41622)
Attacks whose primary impact is inflated bandwidth billing rather than availability degradation (ITID-41623)
ITID-41621.severity: Medium-High; severity rises if edge saturation causes measurable content-delivery failures for end users rather than just elevated latency.
ITID-41621.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if end-user-facing content delivery is failing rather than merely slower.
ITID-41621.escalation: Escalate to the CDN provider and internal platform team to activate provider-side DDoS scrubbing/rate limiting at the edge.
indicators: Edge-node connection/bandwidth utilization at or near capacity in provider dashboards
Elevated error rates or latency concentrated on specific edge locations
Traffic volume far exceeding historical baseline with no corresponding legitimate demand driver
vectors: Volumetric traffic flood directed at specific CDN edge locations
TLS-handshake flood exhausting edge-node connection-establishment capacity
Botnet traffic distributed to concentrate load on regional points-of-presence
rootCauses: Insufficient edge-capacity headroom or auto-scaling for burst traffic
CDN-provider DDoS protection not enabled or under-configured
No geographic traffic-shaping/rate-limiting at the edge
controls: CDN provider-native DDoS scrubbing and rate limiting enabled at the edge
Edge-capacity auto-scaling with burst headroom
Geographic traffic-shaping and anomaly-based edge throttling
ITID-41621.detection: Strong technical signal from CDN provider dashboards showing per-edge-location connection/bandwidth utilization and error rates.
ITID-41621.response: Engage the CDN provider to activate scrubbing/rate limiting at affected edge locations and monitor for shift of attack traffic to other points-of-presence.
metrics: Peak edge-node utilization during incidents
Number of edge locations affected
Time to activate provider-side scrubbing
ITID-41621.notes: Differentiator within CDN Exhaustion: this leaf is a direct attack on edge-node capacity itself, distinct from cache-miss forcing that targets the origin (ITID-41622) or billing-focused abuse (ITID-41623).

playbook.name: CDN Edge Node Resource Exhaustion Attack
playbook.description: An attack is deliberately exhausting compute/connection resources on CDN edge nodes serving the organization's content, degrading delivery performance globally or regionally.

steps.title: Confirm edge node exhaustion via CDN provider dashboard and regional latency data
steps.desc: Review the CDN provider's edge health/status dashboard alongside internal regional latency/error monitoring to confirm specific edge nodes/PoPs are resource-exhausted.
steps.guidance: Look for elevated latency, cache-miss rates, or 5xx errors concentrated in specific geographic regions/PoPs correlating with an unusual request surge.
steps.outcome: Edge exhaustion confirmed with affected PoPs/regions and metrics documented.
steps.abort: If degradation is global and uniform rather than PoP-specific, consider origin-side or DNS-layer causes instead.
steps.tool: CDN provider dashboard, regional synthetic monitoring

steps.title: Open priority support ticket with the CDN provider
steps.desc: Escalate to the CDN provider's support/NOC channel, providing affected PoP/region details and requesting emergency capacity rebalancing or scrubbing.
steps.outcome: Support ticket opened; provider begins rebalancing traffic or applying edge-level mitigation.

steps.title: Monitor provider remediation until edge nodes stabilize
steps.desc: Track CDN provider mitigation progress and confirm affected edge nodes/PoPs return to normal operating parameters.
steps.outcome: Edge node performance confirmed restored to baseline.

steps.title: Validate global delivery performance and fail back if applicable
steps.desc: Confirm content delivery performance is normal across all regions and execute controlled fail-back if a secondary CDN was used.
steps.outcome: Global delivery performance confirmed within normal baselines.

steps.title: Document incident and review CDN capacity/multi-CDN resilience
steps.desc: Capture timeline and evaluate whether multi-CDN architecture, additional edge capacity, or provider SLA changes are warranted.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Assess customer-facing impact by region
steps.desc: Determine which regions/customer segments are experiencing degraded content delivery and the severity of impact.
steps.outcome: Impact-by-region documented to prioritize communication and mitigation.

steps.title: Apply CDN-level rate limiting and caching policy adjustments
steps.desc: Tighten rate-limiting rules and adjust caching behavior at the CDN edge to reduce per-node connection/compute load.
steps.outcome: Edge resource utilization reduced; delivery performance improves.

steps.title: Evaluate failover to a secondary CDN provider
steps.desc: If the primary CDN cannot stabilize affected regions in an acceptable timeframe and a secondary CDN is contracted, evaluate rerouting traffic via DNS/multi-CDN load balancing.
steps.outcome: Traffic rerouted to secondary CDN where viable, or decision documented not to.
steps.abort: If no secondary CDN exists, continue with primary provider engagement only.

ITID-41622.def: A denial-of-service incident in which an adversary crafts requests with randomized or unique query parameters, headers, or cache-busting values so that the CDN cannot serve them from cache, forcing every request to be forwarded to the origin server and exhausting origin capacity that the CDN was meant to shield.
ITID-41622.purpose: Captures denial of service caused by an adversary deliberately forcing cache misses at the CDN layer so that traffic passes through to overload the origin server.
scopeIncludes: Requests with randomized query strings/cache-busting parameters designed to defeat CDN caching
Targeting known-uncacheable or dynamic endpoints at high volume specifically because they bypass the CDN
Exploiting CDN cache-key configuration gaps that allow attacker-controlled values to force per-request cache misses
scopeExcludes: Direct volumetric attacks against edge-node capacity itself (ITID-41621)
Attacks whose primary measured impact is CDN billing cost rather than origin overload (ITID-41623)
ITID-41622.severity: High since the origin server is typically sized for cache-shielded traffic volume, not full-scale direct load.
ITID-41622.priority: P1 if origin capacity is saturated and the CDN cannot absorb the load; P2 if partial mitigations are containing impact.
ITID-41622.escalation: Escalate to the platform/CDN team immediately to tighten cache-key normalization and apply origin-shielding rate limits.
indicators: Cache hit ratio dropping sharply while request volume rises
Origin server load/error rate spiking in tandem with CDN cache-miss rate
High cardinality of near-identical request URLs differing only in cache-busting parameters
vectors: Automated requests appending randomized query parameters to bypass caching
Targeting endpoints already excluded from caching (e.g., search, personalized content) at attack volume
Exploiting overly broad cache-key configuration that includes attacker-controlled headers
rootCauses: Cache-key configuration includes unbounded or attacker-controllable parameters
No origin-shielding rate limit independent of CDN cache status
Dynamic/uncacheable endpoints exposed without additional protection
mitreTechniques: T1499.002 Endpoint Denial of Service: Service Exhaustion Flood
controls: Cache-key normalization to exclude attacker-controllable cache-busting parameters
Origin-shielding rate limits independent of cache status
Dedicated protection/rate limiting for known-uncacheable dynamic endpoints
ITID-41622.detection: Strong technical signal from cache-hit-ratio and origin-load telemetry correlated in real time.
ITID-41622.response: Tighten cache-key normalization, apply emergency origin-shielding rate limits, and block the source pattern generating cache-busting requests.
metrics: Cache hit ratio during incidents
Origin server load/error rate during incidents
Time to restore normal cache hit ratio
ITID-41622.notes: Differentiator within CDN Exhaustion: this leaf is specifically about defeating caching to overload the origin, distinct from direct edge-capacity attacks (ITID-41621) or billing abuse (ITID-41623).

playbook.name: CDN Origin Server Overload via Cache-Miss Forcing
playbook.description: An attacker is deliberately crafting requests (e.g., cache-busting query strings) to force CDN cache misses, driving excessive load directly to origin servers.

steps.title: Confirm cache-miss forcing pattern in CDN and origin logs
steps.desc: Analyze CDN logs for an abnormal rise in cache-miss ratio correlated with a surge in origin server load, and inspect request patterns for cache-busting techniques (randomized query strings, headers).
steps.guidance: Look for high-volume requests to otherwise-cacheable URLs with unique/randomized parameters designed to bypass the CDN cache layer.
steps.outcome: Cache-miss-forcing attack confirmed with representative malicious request samples documented.
steps.abort: If cache-miss rise correlates with a legitimate content update/cache purge, treat as operational, not an attack.
steps.tool: CDN access logs, origin server metrics

steps.title: Deploy CDN rules to normalize or strip cache-busting parameters
steps.desc: Configure CDN cache-key normalization rules to ignore or strip the query parameters/headers being used to force cache misses, restoring cache-hit ratio.
steps.outcome: Cache-hit ratio recovers; origin load drops correspondingly.

steps.title: Verify sustained cache-hit ratio recovery and origin load normalization
steps.desc: Confirm cache-hit ratio and origin load remain stable over a sustained window, indicating the attack technique is no longer effective.
steps.outcome: Cache-hit ratio and origin load confirmed stable at baseline.
steps.tool: CDN access logs, origin server monitoring

steps.title: Remove temporary rate limits and confirm normal service performance
steps.desc: Roll back emergency rate limits once cache-key fix is confirmed effective and verify origin performance remains normal.
steps.outcome: Normal service performance confirmed without emergency controls.

steps.title: Document incident and implement standing cache-key hardening
steps.desc: Capture timeline and recommend permanent cache-key normalization policies and origin-shield capacity review to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Assess origin server load and risk of exhaustion
steps.desc: Determine current origin CPU/connection/database load and estimate time-to-exhaustion if the pattern continues.
steps.outcome: Origin risk level documented to prioritize response urgency.

steps.title: Apply rate limiting on the identified malicious request pattern
steps.desc: Rate-limit or block the specific request pattern/source at the CDN or WAF layer while the cache-key fix propagates.
steps.outcome: Malicious request volume reduced immediately.

ITID-41623.def: A resource-depletion attack in which an adversary generates sustained, large-volume traffic against CDN-served content (e.g., repeatedly downloading large files or media) specifically to inflate the organization's usage-based CDN bandwidth billing, with financial cost as the primary impact rather than service unavailability.
ITID-41623.purpose: Captures denial-of-wallet incidents in which an adversary deliberately drives up CDN bandwidth consumption to inflate billing costs, even when availability is not materially degraded.
scopeIncludes: Automated repeated downloads of large cacheable assets to maximize billed bandwidth
Exploiting freely accessible large media/file assets with no download rate limiting
Sustained low-and-slow bandwidth abuse designed to stay under availability-impact thresholds while accumulating cost
scopeExcludes: Attacks whose primary impact is edge-node availability degradation (ITID-41621)
Cache-miss forcing whose primary impact is origin overload rather than billing cost (ITID-41622)
ITID-41623.severity: Medium; severity is driven by financial impact and budget-threshold breach rather than availability, though sustained abuse can still degrade service for others.
ITID-41623.priority: P2, escalating if billing anomaly detection shows cost trending to breach a defined budget-alert threshold within the billing cycle.
ITID-41623.escalation: Escalate to finance/platform stakeholders once projected cost impact is quantified; engage the CDN provider for abuse mitigation and possible billing adjustment.
indicators: CDN bandwidth billing metrics trending sharply above historical baseline
Download volume for a specific asset or set of assets far exceeding normal demand
A small number of source IPs/accounts responsible for a disproportionate share of bandwidth consumption
vectors: Automated scripts repeatedly downloading large publicly accessible files
Hotlinking of large media assets embedded on third-party sites to drive unexpected traffic
Distributed download requests designed to evade simple per-IP rate limiting
rootCauses: No per-asset or per-account download-rate limiting
Large assets served without hotlink protection or signed-URL controls
No billing-anomaly alerting tied to CDN usage
controls: Download-rate limiting and hotlink protection on large assets
Signed URLs/tokenized access for high-cost content
Billing-anomaly alerting with defined budget thresholds
ITID-41623.detection: Strong technical signal from CDN billing/usage telemetry correlated with per-asset and per-source download volume.
ITID-41623.response: Apply download-rate limiting or hotlink protection to the targeted asset(s), engage the CDN provider on abuse mitigation, and reconcile billing impact with finance.
metrics: Projected/actual bandwidth cost impact per incident
Download volume anomaly magnitude
Time to apply rate limiting/hotlink protection
ITID-41623.notes: Differentiator within CDN Exhaustion: this leaf is specifically a denial-of-wallet/cost-driven abuse, distinct from availability-focused edge attacks (ITID-41621) or origin-overload cache-miss forcing (ITID-41622).

playbook.name: CDN Bandwidth Cost Exhaustion Attack (Denial-of-Wallet via CDN Billing)
playbook.description: An attacker is deliberately driving high-volume content requests through the organization's CDN to inflate bandwidth billing costs (denial-of-wallet), rather than degrading availability directly.

steps.title: Detect abnormal CDN bandwidth/billing trajectory
steps.desc: Correlate CDN billing anomaly alerts with request/bandwidth logs to confirm a deliberate cost-driving attack versus organic traffic growth.
steps.guidance: Look for sustained high-volume requests to large cacheable assets (video, large downloads) from a broad or suspicious source set, with a spend-rate spike well above historical norms.
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed as denial-of-wallet via CDN bandwidth abuse, with cost trajectory and traffic evidence documented.
steps.abort: If bandwidth growth correlates with a legitimate viral content event, treat as capacity planning, not an incident.
steps.tool: CDN billing anomaly detection, access logs

steps.title: Set or verify hard billing alerts and spend caps on the CDN account
steps.desc: Immediately verify or configure hard spend caps/budget alerts on the CDN account to bound further financial exposure while investigation continues.
steps.outcome: Spend caps and alerts confirmed active.

steps.title: Block or challenge confirmed abusive sources
steps.desc: Apply sustained blocking or bot-management challenges against confirmed abusive sources to eliminate remaining cost-driving traffic.
steps.outcome: Abusive traffic eliminated; bandwidth and spend return to baseline.

steps.title: Reconcile CDN costs and confirm normal access patterns restored
steps.desc: Reconcile incurred CDN bandwidth costs for the incident window with finance and confirm legitimate user access to protected assets remains unaffected.
steps.outcome: Cost impact quantified and reported; legitimate access confirmed unaffected.

steps.title: Document incident and implement standing cost-anomaly guardrails
steps.desc: Capture timeline, financial impact, and recommend permanent hotlink protection, signed-URL policy, and cost-anomaly alerting for high-value assets.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with prioritized guardrail follow-ups assigned.

steps.title: Identify specific assets and sources driving cost
steps.desc: Pinpoint which URLs/assets and source IP ranges are responsible for the disproportionate bandwidth consumption.
steps.outcome: Specific abusive assets and sources identified.

steps.title: Apply rate limiting, hotlink protection, or token-authenticated URLs on abused assets
steps.desc: Restrict access to the abused assets via rate limiting, referrer/hotlink protection, or signed/token-authenticated URLs to eliminate unauthorized bulk access.
steps.outcome: Bandwidth consumption from abusive sources drops sharply.

ITID-41624.def: A CDN-resource-exhaustion incident confirmed as an attack against CDN-delivered infrastructure, but not yet classified into a specific mechanism (edge-node capacity, cache-miss forcing, billing/denial-of-wallet abuse) pending further investigation.
ITID-41624.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for CDN exhaustion attacks that do not yet fit edge-node, cache-miss-forcing, or billing-abuse classifications.
scopeIncludes: Newly observed CDN-exhaustion techniques not yet mapped to an existing sibling leaf
Ambiguous CDN-related incidents pending root-cause confirmation
scopeExcludes: Any incident later confirmed as edge-node exhaustion (ITID-41621), cache-miss forcing (ITID-41622), or billing/denial-of-wallet abuse (ITID-41623) — reclassify once confirmed
ITID-41624.severity: Medium by default pending classification; adjust once the specific mechanism and business impact are confirmed.
ITID-41624.priority: P3 pending triage, escalating per standard severity guidance once root cause is identified.
ITID-41624.escalation: Escalate to the SOC classification lead for prompt re-tagging into a specific sibling leaf once the mechanism is understood.
indicators: Elevated CDN-related resource consumption with an unconfirmed cause
Analyst uncertainty about which CDN-exhaustion mechanism applies
vectors: Unclassified/novel CDN-exhaustion technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Root cause not yet determined
controls: Standard CDN monitoring and alerting pending classification
ITID-41624.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual root cause; this bucket itself is detected via generic CDN-usage anomaly alerting.
ITID-41624.response: Investigate to determine the specific mechanism and reclassify to the appropriate sibling ITID as soon as possible; apply standard CDN-exhaustion containment in the interim.
metrics: Number of incidents parked in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
Average time to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf
ITID-41624.notes: Catch-all intake leaf; used only during initial triage. Analysts should reclassify into ITID-41621/41622/41623 as soon as the mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General CDN Exhaustion Attack
playbook.description: An attack targeting the organization's CDN infrastructure is causing resource exhaustion or degraded content delivery, not otherwise classified into a more specific sub-type.

steps.title: Confirm CDN-layer degradation via provider dashboard and internal monitoring
steps.desc: Review CDN provider health dashboards and internal real-user monitoring to confirm degradation is occurring at the CDN layer and characterize the pattern.
steps.outcome: CDN-layer issue confirmed with affected regions/PoPs and metrics documented.
steps.abort: If degradation is not CDN-specific, redirect investigation to origin or network layer.

steps.title: Open priority support ticket with the CDN provider
steps.desc: Escalate to the CDN provider's support channel with affected region/PoP details and request mitigation.
steps.outcome: Support ticket opened; provider begins remediation.

steps.title: Monitor provider remediation until CDN performance stabilizes
steps.desc: Track provider mitigation progress and confirm CDN performance returns to baseline.
steps.outcome: CDN performance confirmed restored.

steps.title: Validate global delivery performance
steps.desc: Confirm content delivery performance is normal across all regions before relaxing any temporary controls.
steps.outcome: Global delivery performance confirmed within normal baselines.

steps.title: Document incident and review CDN resilience posture
steps.desc: Capture timeline and recommend CDN capacity, configuration, or multi-CDN resilience improvements.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Assess customer-facing impact
steps.desc: Determine which regions/services are affected and the severity of degraded content delivery.
steps.outcome: Impact documented to prioritize response.

steps.title: Apply CDN-level rate limiting and caching adjustments
steps.desc: Tighten rate limiting and caching configuration at the CDN edge to reduce load and mitigate the exhaustion condition.
steps.outcome: Resource utilization reduced; delivery performance improves.

ITID-41711.def: The receipt of an extortion email or message threatening a future distributed denial-of-service attack unless a ransom (typically cryptocurrency) is paid by a stated deadline, sent before any actual attack traffic has been observed against the organization.
ITID-41711.purpose: Captures the initial extortion communication in a Ransom DoS campaign, where a threat actor emails a demand for payment under threat of a future DDoS attack, before any attack has occurred.
scopeIncludes: Unsolicited extortion emails threatening a future DDoS attack with a payment deadline
Threats referencing the organization's specific domains/IPs to establish credibility, received with no attack traffic yet observed
Mass-mailed extortion campaigns targeting many organizations with the same template
scopeExcludes: Ransom demands sent after a demonstration attack has already occurred (ITID-41712)
The actual DDoS attack itself, once launched (tracked under the relevant network/application flooding ITIDs, cross-referenced from this incident)
Extortion tied to data theft/encryption rather than a DDoS threat (ITID-23611/23615/31xxx ransomware-extortion leaves — no DDoS-as-leverage mechanism)
ITID-41711.severity: Low-Medium at receipt since no attack has occurred; do not treat as a technical incident requiring infrastructure response until/unless an attack materializes.
ITID-41711.priority: P3 for triage and threat-intelligence logging; do not pay and do not escalate to P1/P2 based on the threat alone.
ITID-41711.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence for actor/campaign attribution and to leadership for awareness; pre-stage DDoS mitigation readiness (scrubbing, rate limits) without paying.
indicators: Extortion email referencing the organization's actual domains/IPs and a specific cryptocurrency payment deadline
Email matching known RDoS extortion-group templates (e.g., threat-actor-brand language)
No corresponding attack traffic observed at time of receipt
vectors: Mass-mailed extortion email to published corporate/security contact addresses
Targeted extortion email to executives or the SOC identified via reconnaissance
rootCauses: Publicly listed contact addresses/security.txt harvested by extortion groups
Prior data breach or leak exposing organizational contact details used to target the extortion email
controls: DDoS mitigation/scrubbing service pre-staged and readiness-tested
Threat-intelligence tracking of known RDoS extortion groups and their campaign indicators
No-payment policy documented and communicated to relevant stakeholders
ITID-41711.detection: Limited technical signal at this stage; detection is primarily via email/communication review and threat-intelligence correlation rather than network telemetry.
ITID-41711.response: Do not pay; log and analyze the threat for actor attribution, verify DDoS mitigation readiness, and monitor closely for any follow-on attack traffic.
metrics: Number of RDoS extortion threats received per quarter
Percentage of threats followed by an actual attack
Mitigation readiness verification completion rate
detections: Email threat-intelligence matching against known RDoS campaign templates
ITID-41711.notes: Differentiator within Ransom Note Threats: this leaf is the pre-attack threat with zero demonstrated capability, distinct from a demand sent after a demonstration attack (ITID-41712) or one using a named threat-actor brand (ITID-41713). Scoped strictly to the DDoS-as-leverage mechanism; cross-reference ITID-23611/23615/23621 and ITID-31xxx for encryption/data-extortion ransom notes with no DDoS component.

playbook.name: Pre-Attack Extortion Email Threatening DDoS Unless Paid
playbook.description: The organization has received an extortion email threatening a DDoS attack against its infrastructure unless a ransom is paid by a stated deadline, with no attack yet demonstrated.

steps.title: Preserve the extortion email and assess sender/threat authenticity
steps.desc: Preserve the full email (headers, body, payment demand) as evidence and assess whether the threat actor brand/identity matches known active RDoS campaigns.
steps.guidance: Do not reply to the sender. Capture full email headers for origin analysis and cross-reference the named actor/brand and wallet address against threat intel trackers of active RDoS campaigns.
steps.outcome: Extortion email preserved as evidence with an initial credibility assessment documented.
steps.tool: Email security gateway, threat intel platform

steps.title: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; do not engage or pay
steps.desc: Escalate the extortion email to Legal counsel and relevant law enforcement per organizational ransom policy. Do not respond to or negotiate with the threat actor.
steps.guidance: Follow established non-payment policy consistent with prior ransomware incident handling; payment does not guarantee the attack will not occur and may invite repeat targeting.
steps.outcome: Legal and Law Enforcement formally notified; no payment or engagement made.
steps.abort: If leadership/Legal determine engagement is warranted, route all communication through Legal only.

steps.title: Monitor for attack onset through and beyond the stated deadline
steps.desc: Maintain heightened traffic monitoring through the threatened deadline and for a reasonable period after, ready to escalate to active DDoS mitigation immediately if an attack begins.
steps.outcome: No attack materializes, or an attack is detected and mitigated promptly per the DDoS playbook.
steps.abort: If an attack begins, transition immediately to the active DDoS mitigation playbook (containment/eradication steps).

steps.title: Stand down heightened monitoring once deadline risk window passes
steps.desc: Once the threat window has passed without incident (or the resulting attack has been resolved), return mitigation posture to standard operating levels.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored with lessons captured.

steps.title: Document the extortion attempt and response effectiveness
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline, Legal/Law Enforcement coordination, and proactive mitigation readiness; recommend any policy or readiness improvements for future RDoS threats.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Baseline current network/service capacity and DDoS mitigation readiness
steps.desc: Review current DDoS mitigation coverage (always-on vs on-demand), scrubbing provider contract status, and edge capacity ahead of the stated deadline.
steps.outcome: Readiness gaps identified and addressed proactively before the threatened deadline.

steps.title: Pre-position DDoS mitigation ahead of the threatened deadline
steps.desc: Proactively engage the scrubbing provider to place mitigation on heightened alert or pre-emptively activate always-on protection ahead of the stated deadline.
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture strengthened before the threatened attack window.

ITID-41712.def: An extortion communication demanding payment to prevent further DDoS attacks, sent after the threat actor has already launched a short demonstration attack against the target to prove capability, materially raising the credibility and urgency of the threat compared to a threat sent with no prior demonstration.
ITID-41712.purpose: Captures the ransom demand communication that follows an initial demonstration DDoS attack, where the threat actor has proven capability before making the payment demand.
scopeIncludes: Ransom email/message referencing a specific recent attack against the organization's own infrastructure as proof of capability
Demand received within a short window following a confirmed demonstration attack (ITID-41721/41722)
Escalating demand language tied explicitly to the just-completed demonstration
scopeExcludes: The demonstration attack itself, tracked separately under Demonstration Attack leaves (ITID-41721/41722/41723)
Initial threats with no prior attack (ITID-41711)
Recurring attacks after non-payment, once the campaign has moved past the initial demand phase (ITID-41731)
ITID-41712.severity: Medium-High given demonstrated capability materially increases the likelihood of a follow-on sustained attack.
ITID-41712.priority: P2, treated as an active campaign requiring mitigation readiness rather than a routine threat log entry.
ITID-41712.escalation: Escalate immediately to DDoS mitigation/network operations and leadership given a demonstrated capability has just been confirmed; activate heightened monitoring.
indicators: Ransom demand received within hours/days of a confirmed short-duration DDoS attack against the organization
Demand explicitly referencing attack details (timing, targeted service) only the attacker would know
Deadline for payment tied to threat of a larger follow-on attack
vectors: Follow-up extortion email sent after a demonstration attack recorded by the organization's own monitoring
Demand delivered via the same channel (email, chat) used for the pre-attack threat if one existed
rootCauses: Successful demonstration attack against an under-protected internet-facing service
Lack of DDoS mitigation capacity revealed by the demonstration, encouraging further extortion
controls: Emergency activation of DDoS scrubbing/mitigation capacity following any demonstration attack
No-payment policy documented and communicated to relevant stakeholders
Post-demonstration heightened monitoring window
ITID-41712.detection: Moderate-to-strong technical signal by combining the confirmed demonstration-attack telemetry with the extortion communication content.
ITID-41712.response: Do not pay; correlate the demand with the demonstration attack for attribution, harden and verify DDoS mitigation capacity, and maintain heightened monitoring through the stated deadline.
metrics: Time between demonstration attack and ransom demand receipt
Percentage of demand-following-demonstration cases that escalate to sustained attack
detections: Correlation alerting linking recent DDoS events to subsequent extortion communications
ITID-41712.notes: Differentiator within Ransom Note Threats: distinguished from ITID-41711 by the presence of a prior demonstration attack, which materially changes response urgency.

playbook.name: Ransom Demand Sent After Initial Demonstration Attack
playbook.description: The organization has experienced a short demonstration DDoS attack, followed by a ransom demand referencing that attack and threatening a larger follow-on campaign unless paid.

steps.title: Confirm the demonstration attack and preserve the ransom communication
steps.desc: Verify the demonstration DDoS occurred via traffic analysis and preserve the ransom note/email in full as evidence, noting any specific claims tying it to the demonstrated attack.
steps.outcome: Demonstration attack confirmed and ransom communication preserved with chain of custody.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; do not engage or pay
steps.desc: Escalate the ransom demand to Legal counsel and law enforcement per organizational non-payment policy.
steps.outcome: Legal and Law Enforcement formally notified; no payment or engagement made.
steps.abort: If leadership/Legal determine engagement is warranted, route all communication through Legal only.

steps.title: Monitor for follow-on attack and respond per active DDoS mitigation procedure
steps.desc: Maintain heightened monitoring through the threatened window; if the follow-on attack materializes, execute active DDoS containment/eradication steps immediately.
steps.outcome: Follow-on attack, if it occurs, is mitigated promptly with minimal impact.

steps.title: Stand down heightened posture once threat window passes
steps.desc: Return mitigation posture to standard levels once the threatened window has passed or the follow-on attack has been resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and mitigation scaling decision effectiveness
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline, Legal/Law Enforcement coordination, and the effectiveness of the proactive scaling decision; recommend readiness improvements.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Assess demonstrated attack capability and follow-on threat credibility
steps.desc: Analyze the demonstration attack's scale/vector to estimate the actor's real capability and cross-reference the actor brand against known RDoS campaign trackers.
steps.outcome: Credibility and capability assessment documented to inform mitigation scaling.

steps.title: Scale up DDoS mitigation ahead of the threatened follow-on campaign
steps.desc: Given the demonstrated capability, decide whether to proactively scale mitigation (activate always-on scrubbing, increase edge capacity) ahead of the threatened larger attack.
steps.guidance: Weigh the cost of proactive scaling against the demonstrated severity and credibility of the threat; err toward scaling up given a confirmed demonstration attack already occurred.
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture scaled appropriately, decision documented.
steps.abort: If the demonstration attack was trivial and actor credibility is low, standard readiness may suffice without full scale-up.

ITID-41713.def: An extortion communication demanding payment to prevent a DDoS attack, in which the sender claims to be (or be affiliated with) a publicly known RDoS threat-actor brand, using that brand's reputation and cryptocurrency payment conventions to increase perceived credibility, regardless of whether the sender has any actual connection to the named group.
ITID-41713.purpose: Captures ransom demands in which the threat actor impersonates or claims affiliation with a known, named RDoS threat-actor brand to borrow that brand's reputation for credibility.
scopeIncludes: Demand explicitly naming a known/publicized RDoS extortion group brand
Copycat or impersonation demands using a known brand's template/wording with no verified affiliation
Demands using a named brand's known cryptocurrency wallet conventions or messaging style
scopeExcludes: Generic, unbranded threats with no named group reference (ITID-41711)

Demands following a confirmed demonstration attack where brand naming is not the primary distinguishing feature (ITID-41712, unless brand impersonation is also present, in which case log under both facets with this ITID as primary)
ITID-41713.severity: Medium; brand naming alone does not confirm actual capability, but known-brand campaigns have historically shown higher follow-through rates and warrant proportionate caution.
ITID-41713.priority: P2 pending threat-intelligence verification of whether the named brand is actively campaigning; adjust once attribution confidence is established.
ITID-41713.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence to verify whether the named brand matches current campaign indicators/infrastructure, and to leadership for awareness given brand-name threats can affect stakeholder confidence.
indicators: Extortion communication explicitly naming a known RDoS threat-actor brand
Message template/wording matching prior publicized campaigns from the named or copycat group
Payment wallet address reused from or mimicking known campaign infrastructure
vectors: Mass-mailed extortion email using a well-known brand name to maximize perceived credibility
Targeted extortion email referencing the named brand's known prior victims for social proof
rootCauses: High public visibility of certain RDoS brands' past campaigns, making them attractive for impersonation
Reuse of leaked or previously published campaign templates by unaffiliated copycat actors
controls: Threat-intelligence subscription/feed tracking known RDoS brand campaign indicators
No-payment policy documented and communicated to relevant stakeholders
DDoS mitigation readiness verification triggered by any named-brand threat
ITID-41713.detection: Limited direct technical signal; detection relies on threat-intelligence correlation of the named brand against current campaign activity and wallet/infrastructure indicators.
ITID-41713.response: Do not pay; engage threat intelligence to assess whether the named brand is genuinely active, verify DDoS mitigation readiness, and monitor for attack traffic through the stated deadline.
metrics: Number of named-brand extortion threats received per quarter
Attribution-confirmation rate (verified brand activity vs. copycat)
detections: Threat-intelligence matching against known RDoS brand indicators
ITID-41713.notes: Differentiator within Ransom Note Threats: the axis here is brand impersonation/claimed affiliation, independent of whether a demonstration attack has occurred.

playbook.name: Anonymous Cryptocurrency Ransom Demand with Named Threat-Actor-Brand Impersonation
playbook.description: The organization has received an extortion demand invoking a well-known RDoS threat-actor brand (e.g., a Fancy Bear/Lazarus-style impersonation) with a cryptocurrency payment demand, whose authenticity as the named actor is uncertain.

steps.title: Preserve the communication and assess brand-impersonation authenticity
steps.desc: Preserve the extortion communication in full and research whether the claimed threat-actor brand's tactics, wallet reuse patterns, and historical behavior match this demand, since brand impersonation by unrelated copycat actors is common.
steps.guidance: Check threat intel trackers for the cryptocurrency wallet address against known campaign wallets; genuine campaigns from major brands often reuse infrastructure/wallets across victims.
steps.outcome: Authenticity assessment documented — genuine, copycat, or indeterminate — informing response posture.
steps.tool: Threat intel platform, blockchain analysis tool

steps.title: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; do not engage or pay
steps.desc: Escalate the extortion demand to Legal counsel and law enforcement, noting the brand-impersonation uncertainty, per organizational non-payment policy.
steps.outcome: Legal and Law Enforcement formally notified; no payment or engagement made.
steps.abort: If leadership/Legal determine engagement is warranted, route all communication through Legal only.

steps.title: Monitor for attack onset and respond per active DDoS mitigation procedure
steps.desc: Maintain heightened monitoring; if an attack materializes, execute active DDoS containment/eradication steps immediately regardless of the actor's claimed identity.
steps.outcome: Any resulting attack is mitigated promptly with minimal impact.

steps.title: Stand down heightened posture once threat window passes
steps.desc: Return mitigation posture to standard levels once the threat window has passed without incident or the resulting attack has been resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored.

steps.title: Document the incident including brand-impersonation findings
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline, authenticity assessment findings, and recommend threat-intel process improvements for evaluating brand-impersonation extortion claims.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Assess current attack status and organizational readiness
steps.desc: Confirm whether any attack traffic has yet been observed and review current DDoS mitigation readiness regardless of the actor's true identity.
steps.guidance: Treat the threat as credible for readiness purposes regardless of brand-authenticity uncertainty.
steps.outcome: Readiness status documented and any gaps addressed.

steps.title: Pre-position DDoS mitigation regardless of actor-brand authenticity
steps.desc: Proactively engage the scrubbing provider to elevate mitigation readiness, since the threat must be treated as credible until disproven by an actual attack (or lack thereof).
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture strengthened ahead of any potential attack.

ITID-41714.def: A received RDoS extortion communication confirmed as a ransom threat, but not yet classified into a specific mechanism (pre-attack threat, post-demonstration demand, brand-impersonation demand) pending further investigation.
ITID-41714.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for RDoS ransom note threats that do not yet fit the pre-attack, post-demonstration, or brand-impersonation classifications.
scopeIncludes: Newly observed RDoS threat communication patterns not yet mapped to an existing sibling leaf
Ambiguous extortion communications pending classification
scopeExcludes: Any incident later confirmed as a pre-attack threat (ITID-41711), post-demonstration demand (ITID-41712), or brand-impersonation demand (ITID-41713) — reclassify once confirmed
ITID-41714.severity: Low-Medium by default pending classification; adjust once the specific circumstances are confirmed.
ITID-41714.priority: P3 pending triage, escalating per standard severity guidance once classified.
ITID-41714.escalation: Escalate to the SOC classification lead for prompt re-tagging into a specific sibling leaf once the circumstances are understood.
indicators: Extortion communication threatening DDoS with an unconfirmed classification
Analyst uncertainty about which ransom-note-threat category applies
vectors: Unclassified/novel RDoS threat communication pending investigation
rootCauses: Root cause/classification not yet determined
controls: Standard RDoS threat triage and mitigation-readiness process pending classification
ITID-41714.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual classification; this bucket itself is logged via standard threat-communication intake.
ITID-41714.response: Do not pay; investigate to determine the specific category and reclassify to the appropriate sibling ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Number of incidents parked in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
Average time to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf
ITID-41714.notes: Catch-all intake leaf; used only during initial triage. Analysts should reclassify into ITID-41711/41712/41713 as soon as the circumstances are confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General RDoS Ransom Note Threat
playbook.description: The organization has received a ransom note threatening a DDoS attack unless payment is made, not otherwise classified into a more specific sub-type.

steps.title: Preserve the ransom communication and assess credibility
steps.desc: Preserve the full ransom communication as evidence and assess threat credibility against known RDoS campaign intelligence.
steps.outcome: Communication preserved and credibility assessment documented.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement; do not engage or pay
steps.desc: Escalate the ransom demand to Legal counsel and law enforcement per organizational non-payment policy.
steps.outcome: Legal and Law Enforcement formally notified; no payment or engagement made.
steps.abort: If leadership/Legal determine engagement is warranted, route all communication through Legal only.

steps.title: Monitor for attack onset and respond per active DDoS mitigation procedure
steps.desc: Maintain heightened monitoring; if an attack materializes, execute active DDoS containment/eradication steps immediately.
steps.outcome: Any resulting attack is mitigated promptly.

steps.title: Stand down heightened posture once threat window passes
steps.desc: Return mitigation posture to standard levels once the threat has passed or been resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and response effectiveness
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline and recommend readiness or policy improvements for future RDoS threats.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Review current DDoS mitigation readiness
steps.desc: Assess current mitigation coverage and identify any gaps ahead of a potential attack.
steps.outcome: Readiness gaps identified and addressed.

steps.title: Pre-position DDoS mitigation ahead of any potential attack
steps.desc: Proactively engage the scrubbing provider to elevate mitigation readiness ahead of any stated or implied deadline.
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture strengthened.

ITID-41721.def: A brief, intentionally limited denial-of-service attack (minutes rather than hours) launched by a threat actor to demonstrate genuine attack capability against the target's general infrastructure, intended to lend credibility to an accompanying or forthcoming ransom demand rather than to cause sustained business impact.
ITID-41721.purpose: Captures the short-duration, low-volume DDoS burst a threat actor launches purely to prove attack capability, typically as a precursor to or alongside a ransom demand.
scopeIncludes: Short-duration (typically under an hour) volumetric or application-layer attack bursts against general internet-facing infrastructure
Attacks that stop on their own without further action, consistent with a proof-of-capability pattern
Bursts occurring in temporal proximity to an extortion communication
scopeExcludes: A demonstration attack focused specifically on a single named critical service to maximize demonstrated leverage (ITID-41722)
Sustained, recurring attacks following a missed payment deadline (ITID-41731/41732)
ITID-41721.severity: Medium; brief duration limits direct business impact, but confirms genuine capability and materially raises the credibility/likelihood of a larger follow-on campaign.
ITID-41721.priority: P2, treated as high-signal threat intelligence requiring immediate mitigation-readiness verification.
ITID-41721.escalation: Escalate to network operations/DDoS mitigation and threat intelligence immediately upon detection to correlate with any received or forthcoming ransom communication.
indicators: Sudden, short-lived spike in inbound traffic volume or malicious request rate against general infrastructure
Attack stopping abruptly without any mitigation action having taken effect
Attack occurring within a short window of an extortion email/message
vectors: Brief volumetric flood via a rented/booter DDoS-for-hire service
Short application-layer request flood against a public-facing endpoint
rootCauses: Insufficient DDoS mitigation capacity/readiness that the demonstration is designed to expose
Public-facing infrastructure with no baseline traffic anomaly alerting
controls: DDoS mitigation/scrubbing service capable of rapid activation
Traffic-anomaly alerting tuned to detect short-duration bursts
Correlation process linking detected bursts to threat-intelligence extortion indicators
ITID-41721.detection: Strong technical signal from traffic-volume/anomaly telemetry; correlating timing with any extortion communication confirms the RDoS context.
ITID-41721.response: Verify and, if needed, activate DDoS mitigation capacity, log full attack characteristics for attribution, and correlate with any extortion communication received.
metrics: Duration and peak volume of demonstration bursts
Time to correlate a demonstration attack with an extortion communication
Mitigation-readiness activation time
ITID-41721.notes: Differentiator within Demonstration Attack: this leaf is a general-infrastructure capability-proof burst, distinct from a single-critical-service-targeted demonstration (ITID-41722).

playbook.name: Short-Duration Proof-of-Capability DDoS Burst
playbook.description: A brief, deliberately short DDoS burst has hit organizational infrastructure, apparently intended to demonstrate attacker capability ahead of an anticipated ransom demand or larger campaign.

steps.title: Confirm the burst attack and characterize its scale/vector
steps.desc: Analyze traffic telemetry to confirm the short-duration DDoS burst occurred, capturing its vector, peak volume, and duration precisely.
steps.guidance: Proof-of-capability bursts are typically brief (minutes) but can reveal significant attacker resources; capture full telemetry even though the burst may have already ended by the time analysis begins.
steps.outcome: Burst attack confirmed with vector, scale, and duration documented.

steps.title: Decide on proactive mitigation scaling ahead of an anticipated full campaign
steps.desc: Given the demonstrated capability, decide whether to proactively scale DDoS mitigation (activate always-on scrubbing, increase edge capacity) ahead of an anticipated larger follow-on attack.
steps.guidance: Weigh the burst's demonstrated scale and vector sophistication against the cost of scaling up; err toward proactive scaling given a real attack has already been observed.
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture scaled appropriately with the decision and rationale documented.
steps.abort: If the burst was trivial in scale and no ransom communication follows within a reasonable window, standard readiness may suffice.

steps.title: Monitor for the anticipated full-scale follow-on campaign
steps.desc: Maintain heightened monitoring through the period during which a full campaign is anticipated; execute active DDoS containment/eradication steps immediately if it materializes.
steps.outcome: Follow-on campaign, if it occurs, is mitigated promptly given the pre-scaled posture.

steps.title: Stand down heightened posture once anticipated campaign window passes
steps.desc: Return mitigation posture to standard levels once the anticipated attack window passes without a full campaign, or once a follow-on campaign has been resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored.

steps.title: Document the demonstration burst and scaling decision effectiveness
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline, the proactive scaling decision and rationale, and any follow-on campaign outcome; recommend readiness improvements.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Monitor for accompanying or imminent ransom communication
steps.desc: Check email security gateway and relevant inboxes for a ransom note referencing the demonstration burst, which often follows within hours.
steps.outcome: Any accompanying ransom communication identified and preserved.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement if a ransom demand is received
steps.desc: If a ransom communication accompanies or follows the burst, escalate to Legal counsel and law enforcement per organizational non-payment policy.
steps.outcome: Legal and Law Enforcement notified where applicable; no payment or engagement made.
steps.abort: If no ransom communication is received, this step is not applicable.

ITID-41722.def: A brief denial-of-service attack in which the threat actor deliberately selects and targets one specific business-critical service (e.g., the primary customer-facing application, payment gateway, or a named subsidiary) to demonstrate that they have identified and can disrupt exactly what matters most to the organization, maximizing psychological leverage ahead of a full extortion campaign.
ITID-41722.purpose: Captures a demonstration attack deliberately targeted at a single, specifically chosen critical service (rather than general infrastructure) to maximize the perceived leverage of the threat before a full campaign.
scopeIncludes: Short attack precisely targeting a named critical service identified in advance by the threat actor
Demonstration attacks referencing the specific targeted service by name in an accompanying communication
Attacks that demonstrate reconnaissance of which service matters most to the business
scopeExcludes: Demonstration bursts against general/undifferentiated infrastructure with no specific critical-service targeting (ITID-41721)
Full-scale persistent attacks following non-payment (ITID-41731/41732/41733)
ITID-41722.severity: High given the deliberate targeting indicates reconnaissance and intent to maximize business disruption in any follow-on campaign.
ITID-41722.priority: P1 given the specific critical service is now a confirmed target requiring immediate protective action.
ITID-41722.escalation: Escalate immediately to the business owner of the targeted critical service, network operations, and leadership given the deliberate targeting signals a credible, informed threat.
indicators: Short attack burst precisely aligned to a single named critical service's infrastructure
Extortion communication explicitly naming the targeted service
Evidence of prior reconnaissance (e.g., probing) against the specific service preceding the burst
vectors: Targeted volumetric or application-layer burst against the specific critical service's known endpoints
Attack timed to a period of known business criticality for the targeted service (e.g., a peak sales period)
rootCauses: Publicly discoverable information revealing which service is most business-critical
Insufficient dedicated DDoS protection on the specific critical service compared to general infrastructure
controls: Dedicated, prioritized DDoS mitigation for identified business-critical services
Business-impact-based prioritization in the DDoS mitigation readiness plan
Rapid cross-functional escalation path to the critical service's business owner
ITID-41722.detection: Strong technical signal from traffic telemetry against the specific critical service, combined with content analysis of any accompanying extortion communication naming the target.
ITID-41722.response: Immediately harden and prioritize mitigation for the targeted critical service, brief its business owner, and treat as a credible precursor to a full campaign.
metrics: Time to prioritize mitigation for the named critical service
Business impact duration/cost of the demonstration burst
ITID-41722.notes: Differentiator within Demonstration Attack: the axis is deliberate single-critical-service targeting versus general-infrastructure bursts (ITID-41721).

playbook.name: Demonstration Attack Targeting a Single Critical Service Before Full Campaign
playbook.description: A demonstration DDoS attack has targeted one specific critical service (rather than broad infrastructure), apparently to prove the actor can disrupt a high-value target before threatening a wider campaign.

steps.title: Confirm the targeted demonstration attack and assess why this service was chosen
steps.desc: Verify the attack via traffic analysis and assess why the specific critical service was targeted (e.g., high business value, known fragility, public visibility).
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed with targeting rationale assessed to inform which other services may be at risk.

steps.title: Decide on proactive mitigation scaling across critical services ahead of a full campaign
steps.desc: Given the targeted demonstration, decide whether to proactively extend DDoS mitigation coverage to the affected service and other similarly exposed critical services ahead of an anticipated wider campaign.
steps.guidance: Prioritize scaling for services identified in the prior step as sharing exposure with the demonstrated target.
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture scaled across at-risk critical services with the decision documented.
steps.abort: If the targeted service is isolated and no other critical services share its exposure, scope scaling to that service alone.

steps.title: Monitor for the anticipated full-scale campaign across all at-risk services
steps.desc: Maintain heightened monitoring across the originally targeted service and other at-risk critical services; execute active DDoS containment/eradication immediately if the campaign materializes.
steps.outcome: Any full campaign is mitigated promptly given the pre-scaled posture.

steps.title: Stand down heightened posture once anticipated campaign window passes
steps.desc: Return mitigation posture to standard levels once the anticipated wider campaign window passes without materializing, or once resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and cross-service exposure findings
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline, the exposure assessment across critical services, and recommend architectural or mitigation-coverage improvements to reduce shared exposure.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Identify other critical services with similar exposure
steps.desc: Assess whether other business-critical services share the same architectural weaknesses or public exposure that made the targeted service vulnerable.
steps.outcome: A list of similarly exposed services identified for inclusion in proactive mitigation scaling.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Law Enforcement if a ransom demand follows
steps.desc: If a ransom communication follows the demonstration attack, escalate to Legal counsel and law enforcement per organizational non-payment policy.
steps.outcome: Legal and Law Enforcement notified where applicable; no payment or engagement made.
steps.abort: If no ransom communication is received, this step is not applicable.

ITID-41723.def: A brief denial-of-service attack confirmed as an RDoS demonstration/proof-of-capability event, but not yet classified into a specific mechanism (general-infrastructure burst, critical-service-targeted burst) pending further investigation.
ITID-41723.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for RDoS demonstration attacks that do not yet fit general-infrastructure or critical-service-targeted classifications.
scopeIncludes: Newly observed demonstration-attack patterns not yet mapped to an existing sibling leaf
Ambiguous short-duration attacks pending confirmation of RDoS context and targeting intent
scopeExcludes: Any incident later confirmed as a general-infrastructure demonstration (ITID-41721) or a critical-service-targeted demonstration (ITID-41722) — reclassify once confirmed
ITID-41723.severity: Medium by default pending classification; adjust once targeting intent and business impact are confirmed.
ITID-41723.priority: P2 pending triage, escalating per standard severity guidance once root cause and targeting intent are identified.
ITID-41723.escalation: Escalate to the SOC classification lead for prompt re-tagging into a specific sibling leaf once the targeting pattern is understood.
indicators: Short-duration attack burst with an unconfirmed targeting rationale
Analyst uncertainty about whether targeting was general or deliberately critical-service-specific
vectors: Unclassified/novel demonstration-attack pattern pending investigation
rootCauses: Root cause/classification not yet determined
controls: Standard DDoS mitigation readiness and threat-intelligence correlation pending classification
ITID-41723.detection: Coverage depends on the eventual classification; this bucket itself is detected via generic short-duration traffic-burst alerting.
ITID-41723.response: Investigate to determine targeting intent and reclassify to the appropriate sibling ITID as soon as possible; apply standard demonstration-attack containment in the interim.
metrics: Number of incidents parked in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
Average time to reclassify into a specific sibling leaf
ITID-41723.notes: Catch-all intake leaf; used only during initial triage. Analysts should reclassify into ITID-41721/41722 as soon as targeting intent is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General RDoS Demonstration Attack
playbook.description: A demonstration DDoS attack apparently intended to prove capability ahead of a ransom demand or larger campaign has occurred, not otherwise classified into a more specific sub-type.

steps.title: Confirm the demonstration attack and characterize its scale/vector
steps.desc: Analyze traffic telemetry to confirm the demonstration attack occurred and document its vector, scale, and duration.
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed with vector, scale, and duration documented.

steps.title: Decide on proactive mitigation scaling ahead of an anticipated full campaign
steps.desc: Given the demonstrated capability, decide whether to proactively scale DDoS mitigation ahead of an anticipated larger follow-on attack.
steps.outcome: Mitigation posture scaled appropriately with the decision documented.
steps.abort: If the demonstration was trivial and no ransom communication follows, standard readiness may suffice.

steps.title: Monitor for the anticipated full-scale follow-on campaign
steps.desc: Maintain heightened monitoring through the period during which a full campaign is anticipated.
steps.outcome: Follow-on campaign, if it occurs, is mitigated promptly.

steps.title: Stand down heightened posture once anticipated campaign window passes
steps.desc: Return mitigation posture to standard levels once the anticipated window passes or a follow-on campaign is resolved.
steps.outcome: Normal operating posture restored.

steps.title: Document the demonstration attack and response effectiveness
steps.desc: Capture the full timeline and recommend readiness improvements.
steps.outcome: Report finalized with follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Monitor for accompanying or imminent ransom communication
