steps.desc: Continue elevated monitoring/alerting on the previously scanned hosts beyond immediate containment.
steps.guidance: Configure a time-boxed heightened-alert rule in the SIEM.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring window completed with no follow-on attack activity, or follow-on activity caught and handled.

steps.title: Document scan activity and reinforce stealth-scan detection capability
steps.desc: Record the scan details and recommend improvements to detection tooling/thresholds for stealth scanning techniques.
steps.outcome: Report filed; detection improvements tracked for implementation.

steps.title: Check source IP against threat intelligence
steps.desc: Determine whether the scanning source is known-malicious infrastructure or a known internet-wide scanning service.
steps.guidance: Query threat intel feeds for source IP reputation and prior activity.
steps.outcome: Source classification established to inform response severity.

steps.title: Tune IDS/IPS and firewall to detect and rate-limit stealth scan patterns
steps.desc: Enable or tune signatures/thresholds specifically for half-open/SYN scan detection to improve future detection speed and consider connection rate-limiting at the perimeter.
steps.guidance: Enable relevant IDS/IPS signature categories and configure SYN-flood/rate-limiting protections if not already active.
steps.outcome: Improved detection and rate-limiting for future stealth scan attempts.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent activity given recon-precedes-attack pattern
steps.desc: Because stealth scanning often indicates a more deliberate/sophisticated actor preparing for further attack, set heightened monitoring and correlate any follow-on connection attempts against the discovered open ports rather than closing the incident once scanning stops.
steps.guidance: Configure a monitoring watch for a defined follow-up period on the scanned hosts/ports.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether follow-on exploitation occurred, with heightened monitoring in place regardless.

ITID-42313.def: A distributed and/or low-and-slow port scan in which probes are spread across many source IPs, extended time windows, or both, specifically to remain under the volume/rate thresholds that trigger standard scan-detection alerting.
ITID-42313.purpose: Captures reconnaissance activity deliberately spread across time and/or source IPs to stay below rate- and threshold-based detection.
scopeIncludes: Scans using a botnet or distributed infrastructure to probe from many different source IPs
Scans deliberately paced (e.g., one probe per host per hour) to stay under rate-based alert thresholds
Aggregated analysis across a wide time window revealing a coordinated scan otherwise invisible to real-time thresholds
scopeExcludes: Standard full-connect scans from a single source in a short window (ITID-42311)
Standard SYN scans from a single source in a short window (ITID-42312)
ITID-42313.severity: Medium-High — the deliberate evasion effort indicates a more sophisticated and likely persistent adversary.
ITID-42313.priority: P2 upon detection via retrospective/aggregated analysis; P1 if correlated with a broader active campaign.
ITID-42313.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence/IR for campaign correlation; standard per-source blocking is insufficient given the distributed nature.
indicators: Long-window aggregated log analysis revealing a coordinated low-rate scan pattern across many source IPs
Threat intelligence correlation linking disparate low-volume probes to a single known scanning campaign or infrastructure cluster
SIEM long-baseline analytics flagging a slow accumulation of port-touch events against the same target set
vectors: Botnet-distributed scanning infrastructure
Deliberately rate-limited scanning tooling configured to evade per-source thresholds
rootCauses: Detection tuned only for short-window, high-rate scan patterns
Insufficient log retention/aggregation window to correlate low-and-slow activity retrospectively
mitreTechniques: T1595.001 Active Scanning: Scanning IP Blocks
controls: Long-window SIEM analytics/UEBA capable of correlating low-rate distributed activity
Threat intelligence feeds identifying known distributed scanning infrastructure
Extended log retention to support retrospective correlation
ITID-42313.detection: Weak in real time; moderate-to-strong only with long-window aggregated analytics and threat intelligence correlation.
ITID-42313.response: Correlate across the full distributed source set, block/monitor the identified infrastructure cluster, and assess for a broader coordinated campaign.
metrics: Count of distributed/low-and-slow scan campaigns identified per period
Mean time to correlate a distributed scan retrospectively
ITID-42313.notes: This leaf exists specifically because standard real-time thresholds miss this pattern by design; detection here depends on retrospective and cross-source correlation capability.

playbook.name: Distributed/Low-and-Slow Scan Evading Detection Thresholds
playbook.description: An external actor conducted a distributed scan across multiple source IPs, or a low-and-slow scan spread over an extended time period, specifically to stay below per-source rate-based detection thresholds while enumerating the perimeter.

steps.title: Aggregate and correlate distributed low-volume scan traffic across a wide time window
steps.desc: Because per-source volume stays below normal alert thresholds, aggregate flow/firewall logs over an extended window (days to weeks) and correlate scanning patterns across multiple source IPs to detect the distributed/low-and-slow campaign as a whole.
steps.guidance: Use SIEM correlation rules or manual analysis grouping connections by targeted port sequence, timing pattern, or shared destination set across many distinct low-volume sources; check for common ASN/infrastructure ownership among sources.
steps.outcome: Confirmed coordinated distributed/low-and-slow scan campaign identified, with the full set of source IPs and scanned scope documented.
steps.abort: If the aggregated pattern does not show coordination and is consistent with unrelated background internet noise, close as low-priority background scanning.

steps.title: Block identified source IPs/infrastructure at the perimeter firewall
steps.desc: Add deny rules for all confirmed sources in the distributed campaign, potentially at a broader ASN/range level given the distributed nature.
steps.guidance: Balance blocking scope against risk of impacting shared/legitimate infrastructure; consider geo-fencing or ASN-level blocking where the campaign is clearly concentrated.
steps.outcome: Identified distributed scanning sources blocked from further reconnaissance.

steps.title: Reduce unnecessary exposed attack surface identified by the campaign
steps.desc: Review the ports/services found reachable across the full campaign and close or restrict any not business-justified for external exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with service owners to confirm business need for each exposed port.
steps.outcome: External attack surface reduced.

steps.title: Maintain extended heightened monitoring on scanned hosts
steps.desc: Continue elevated monitoring/alerting on the previously scanned hosts for an extended follow-up period given the actor's demonstrated evasion sophistication.
steps.guidance: Configure an extended time-boxed heightened-alert rule in the SIEM.
steps.outcome: Extended monitoring window completed with no follow-on attack activity, or follow-on activity caught and handled.

steps.title: Document campaign and reinforce long-window detection capability
steps.desc: Record the full campaign details and recommend permanent implementation of long-window correlation rules to catch future distributed/low-and-slow reconnaissance earlier.
steps.outcome: Report filed; detection improvements tracked for implementation.

steps.title: Check aggregated source infrastructure against threat intelligence
steps.desc: Determine whether the distributed source IPs share infrastructure, proxy/VPN services, or botnet characteristics indicating a coordinated, evasion-focused actor.
steps.guidance: Query threat intel feeds for each source IP and look for shared hosting providers, known scanning botnets, or anonymization services.
steps.outcome: Source infrastructure characterized, informing actor sophistication assessment.

steps.title: Tune detection thresholds to catch low-and-slow patterns going forward
steps.desc: Adjust SIEM/IDS correlation rules to detect low-volume, extended-duration scanning patterns rather than relying solely on short-window volume thresholds.
steps.guidance: Implement or tune a long-window aggregation rule specifically designed to catch distributed/low-and-slow reconnaissance.
steps.outcome: Improved detection capability for future evasive scanning campaigns.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent activity given heightened sophistication indicates deliberate attack preparation
steps.desc: Given the deliberate evasion effort indicates a more sophisticated and likely persistent actor, establish extended heightened monitoring and correlate any follow-on activity against the discovered open ports/services rather than treating the incident as closed once scanning activity subsides.
steps.guidance: Configure an extended monitoring watch (longer than a standard scan follow-up window, given the low-and-slow nature of the actor) on the scanned hosts/ports.
steps.outcome: Extended heightened monitoring in place with any follow-on exploitation attempts flagged for immediate escalation.

ITID-42314.def: General/unclassified port scanning activity that cannot yet be attributed to a full-connect scan, a SYN/stealth scan, or a distributed/low-and-slow scan.
ITID-42314.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for port scanning activity that does not yet fit a more specific sibling leaf.
scopeIncludes: Any confirmed port scan activity pending technique classification
Scan activity where the specific technique cannot be determined from available telemetry
scopeExcludes: Cases root-caused to full-connect scanning (ITID-42311)
Cases root-caused to SYN/stealth scanning (ITID-42312)
Cases root-caused to distributed/low-and-slow scanning (ITID-42313)
ITID-42314.severity: Default Low-Medium pending triage; reassess once technique is determined.
ITID-42314.priority: P3 pending triage, escalating if follow-up exploitation is observed.
ITID-42314.escalation: Escalate to SOC for triage; reclassify once the specific scan technique is established.
indicators: Perimeter or internal scan alerting not yet matched to a specific known technique
vectors: Varies — captured here only until technique is determined
rootCauses: To be determined via investigation
controls: Standard incident triage workflow
Perimeter IDS/IPS scan detection
ITID-42314.detection: Varies by underlying technique; general scan detection provides the initial signal.
ITID-42314.response: Triage promptly, block/monitor the source, and reclassify the record once the specific technique is established.
metrics: Count of records held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to reclassification
ITID-42314.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; analysts should actively work to reclassify records out of it wherever a specific technique can be established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Port Scanning
playbook.description: Port scanning activity against the organization's network was detected that does not match a more specific known scan technique, requiring general investigation to characterize the scan and assess risk of a follow-on attack.

steps.title: Detect and characterize the scan via IDS/IPS and flow logs
steps.desc: Review IDS/IPS alerts and firewall/flow logs to confirm scanning activity, source IP(s), scanned port range, and targeted hosts.
steps.guidance: Determine scan technique characteristics (connect vs. SYN vs. UDP, scope, timing) to the extent possible from available logs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scan activity with source, scope, and targeted hosts documented.
steps.abort: If source is a known/authorized scanning service, close as expected activity.

steps.title: Block the scanning source IP(s) at the perimeter firewall
steps.desc: Add a deny rule for the confirmed unauthorized scanning source at the perimeter firewall.
steps.guidance: Verify the block does not impact legitimate business traffic before applying.
steps.outcome: Scanning source blocked from further reconnaissance.
steps.abort: Skip if source is confirmed authorized.

steps.title: Reduce unnecessary exposed attack surface identified by the scan
steps.desc: Review ports/services found reachable during the scan and close or restrict any not business-justified for external exposure.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with system/service owners to confirm business need for each exposed port.
steps.outcome: External attack surface reduced.

steps.title: Maintain heightened monitoring on scanned hosts for a defined follow-up period
steps.desc: Continue elevated monitoring/alerting on the previously scanned hosts beyond immediate containment.
steps.guidance: Configure a time-boxed heightened-alert rule in the SIEM.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring window completed with no follow-on attack activity, or follow-on activity caught and handled.

steps.title: Document scan activity and reinforce perimeter monitoring
steps.desc: Record the scan details and recommend periodic external attack-surface reviews and detection tuning as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Report filed; follow-up actions tracked.

steps.title: Check source IP against threat intelligence
steps.desc: Determine whether the scanning source is known-malicious infrastructure or previously unseen.
steps.guidance: Query threat intel feeds for source IP reputation and prior activity.
steps.outcome: Source classification established to inform response severity.

steps.title: Correlate scan activity with any subsequent exploitation attempts
steps.desc: Because reconnaissance often precedes a larger attack, monitor for and correlate any follow-on activity against the scanned hosts/ports rather than treating the incident as closed once scanning stops.
steps.guidance: Set a monitoring watch on the scanned hosts/ports for a defined follow-up period.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether follow-on exploitation occurred, with heightened monitoring in place regardless.

ITID-42321.def: Enumeration technique in which an adversary connects to open ports and captures service banners (software name, version, configuration hints) returned during connection setup, used to fingerprint exploitable software versions before targeting an attack.
ITID-42321.purpose: Captures reconnaissance activity that connects to exposed services specifically to read version/software banners for fingerprinting.
scopeIncludes: Connections to open ports that solicit and record service banner responses
Fingerprinting activity following a port scan to identify software versions on discovered open ports
Use of banner data to select a subsequent exploitation attempt
scopeExcludes: The initial port discovery scan itself (ITID-4231x family)
SNMP/network-device-specific enumeration (ITID-42322)
Automated vulnerability-scanner-driven enumeration (ITID-42323)
ITID-42321.severity: Medium — indicates the adversary has moved from broad discovery to targeted fingerprinting, a precursor to exploitation.
ITID-42321.priority: P2 for confirmed banner-grabbing activity; P1 if followed by an exploitation attempt matching the fingerprinted software/version.
ITID-42321.escalation: Escalate to SOC to check the fingerprinted software for known vulnerabilities and patch status before an exploitation attempt occurs.
indicators: Connections to open ports followed immediately by disconnection with no further protocol interaction, consistent with banner-only probing
IDS signatures for known banner-grabbing tools (e.g., Netcat banner grabs, Nmap version detection)
Source correlating banner-grab activity with subsequent targeted exploitation attempts
vectors: Nmap version detection (-sV) or similar tooling
Manual banner grabbing via Netcat/Telnet against identified open ports
rootCauses: Services configured to return verbose version banners unnecessarily
No suppression/normalization of banner information at the network edge
mitreTechniques: T1592.002 Gather Victim Host Information: Software
controls: Banner suppression/minimization on externally-facing services
Prompt patching of fingerprinted services
IDS signatures for known banner-grabbing tooling
ITID-42321.detection: Moderate — detectable via IDS signatures and connection-pattern analysis, though a single low-volume banner grab can blend into normal traffic.
ITID-42321.response: Identify the fingerprinted service/version, confirm patch status, and monitor for follow-up exploitation attempts.
metrics: Count of banner-grabbing events detected per period
Percentage of externally-facing services with banner suppression applied
ITID-42321.notes: The differentiator from other enumeration siblings is the specific technique (banner text capture) rather than protocol-specific enumeration (SNMP) or automated scanning tools.

playbook.name: Service Banner Grabbing for Version Fingerprinting
playbook.description: An external actor performed service banner grabbing against exposed hosts to fingerprint software versions running on open ports, a reconnaissance precursor activity used to identify exploitable, version-specific vulnerabilities.

steps.title: Detect banner-grabbing activity via IDS/IPS and application/service logs
steps.desc: Review IDS/IPS alerts and service-level logs (web server, SSH, FTP, mail, etc.) for connection patterns consistent with automated banner-grabbing tools (e.g., rapid connect-and-disconnect across multiple services without further protocol interaction).
steps.guidance: Correlate connection attempts across multiple distinct services on the same host(s) from the same source in a short window, with minimal or no follow-through protocol handshake beyond the initial banner exchange.
steps.outcome: Confirmed banner-grabbing activity with source IP, targeted hosts/services, and versions potentially disclosed documented.
steps.abort: If the source is a known/authorized scanning vendor, close as expected activity.

steps.title: Block the source IP performing the banner grabbing
steps.desc: Add a deny rule for the confirmed unauthorized source at the perimeter firewall.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further reconnaissance.
steps.abort: Skip if source is confirmed authorized.

steps.title: Patch or upgrade fingerprinted services with known vulnerabilities
steps.desc: Prioritize patching/upgrading any service versions identified as having known, exploitable vulnerabilities disclosed by the banner grab.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with system owners for emergency or expedited patching where a critical vulnerability was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable service versions patched or upgraded.

steps.title: Verify patched services and confirm no follow-on exploitation
steps.desc: Confirm all identified vulnerable services are patched and no follow-on exploitation attempts succeeded during the monitoring window.
steps.guidance: Run a vulnerability rescan on the affected hosts.
steps.outcome: Services confirmed patched; no successful exploitation observed.

steps.title: Document findings and reinforce patch management and banner hardening practices
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend routine banner-suppression hardening as part of the standard external service deployment baseline.
steps.outcome: Report filed; hardening baseline updated as appropriate.

steps.title: Determine which software versions were disclosed and their known vulnerabilities
steps.desc: Identify exactly what version information was exposed via the banners and cross-reference against known CVEs for those versions.
steps.guidance: Check the actual banner strings returned by the affected services and search vulnerability databases for known exploits against those specific versions.
steps.outcome: List of disclosed software versions and any associated known vulnerabilities that could be targeted next.

steps.title: Suppress or obfuscate version banners where feasible
steps.desc: Configure exposed services to suppress or generalize version information in their banners to reduce the value of future fingerprinting attempts.
steps.guidance: Apply server configuration hardening (e.g., disable verbose version strings on web servers, SSH, mail servers) per vendor-recommended hardening guides.
steps.outcome: Reduced information disclosure via service banners.
steps.abort: Skip if banner suppression is not supported by the service or would break monitoring/compatibility needs, and rely on patching as the primary control.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent exploitation attempts against fingerprinted services
steps.desc: Because banner grabbing is a direct precursor to targeted exploitation, establish heightened monitoring specifically on the fingerprinted services for exploitation attempts matching the disclosed version's known vulnerabilities.
steps.guidance: Configure targeted detection rules/signatures for known exploits against the specific disclosed versions.
steps.outcome: Heightened, vulnerability-specific monitoring in place on the fingerprinted services.

ITID-42322.def: Enumeration of network infrastructure devices (routers, switches, and similar) via SNMP or other device-management protocols to extract configuration, topology, and software version information, typically exploiting weak or default community strings.
ITID-42322.purpose: Captures reconnaissance activity that queries SNMP or other network-device-specific protocols to enumerate infrastructure details.
scopeIncludes: SNMP walk/get operations against network devices using default or weak community strings
Enumeration of device configuration, routing tables, or interface details via SNMP or similar management protocols
Use of extracted device information to plan further reconnaissance or targeted exploitation
scopeExcludes: General service banner grabbing on non-network-device services (ITID-42321)
Automated vulnerability-scanner-driven enumeration (ITID-42323)
ITID-42322.severity: Medium-High — successful SNMP enumeration can reveal detailed network topology and device configuration directly useful for follow-on attacks.
ITID-42322.priority: P2 for confirmed enumeration activity; P1 if default/weak community strings are confirmed successfully exploited.
ITID-42322.escalation: Escalate to network engineering to rotate SNMP community strings/credentials and restrict SNMP access immediately.
indicators: SNMP GET/WALK requests from unexpected source IPs against network devices
Successful SNMP queries using default community strings (e.g., 'public', 'private')
Network device logs showing management-protocol queries outside the designated management network
vectors: Default or weak SNMP community strings left unchanged from vendor defaults
SNMP left reachable outside the dedicated management network
rootCauses: Network devices deployed without rotating default SNMP community strings
SNMP not restricted to the management network via ACL
No periodic audit of SNMP configuration across the device fleet
controls: Rotate default SNMP community strings to strong, unique values (or migrate to SNMPv3)
Restrict SNMP access to the dedicated management network
Periodic SNMP configuration audit across network devices
ITID-42322.detection: Moderate — requires monitoring on network devices or management-network boundary for SNMP query patterns from unexpected sources.
ITID-42322.response: Rotate community strings/credentials, restrict SNMP reachability, and review what configuration data may have been disclosed.
metrics: Count of devices found with default/weak SNMP strings per audit
Count of SNMP enumeration attempts detected per period
detections: SNMP enumeration attempt alert from outside the management network
ITID-42322.notes: The differentiator from ITID-42321 is the protocol-specific target: network infrastructure device management protocols rather than general application/service banners.

playbook.name: SNMP/Network Device Service Enumeration
playbook.description: An actor enumerated network device services via SNMP (e.g., querying community strings, MIB walking) to gather configuration and topology information about network infrastructure devices.

steps.title: Detect SNMP enumeration activity via network device and IDS logs
steps.desc: Review network device logs and IDS/IPS alerts for repeated SNMP GET/GETBULK/walk requests from an unexpected source, including failed community-string attempts (indicating brute-forcing) or successful queries from an unrecognized management station.
steps.guidance: Check SNMP access logs on routers/switches/firewalls for source IP and queried OIDs; look for community-string guessing patterns (e.g., 'public'/'private' attempts).
steps.outcome: Confirmed SNMP enumeration activity with source, targeted devices, and information queried documented.
steps.abort: If source is an authorized network monitoring system, close as expected activity.

steps.title: Block the source performing SNMP enumeration
steps.desc: Add a deny rule for the confirmed unauthorized source at the perimeter/internal firewall, and restrict SNMP access to only authorized management station IPs.
steps.guidance: Apply an ACL on network devices restricting SNMP queries to the authorized network management subnet only.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized SNMP access blocked.

steps.title: Harden SNMP configuration organization-wide
steps.desc: Audit all network devices for SNMP exposure, disable SNMP where not needed, migrate to SNMPv3, and enforce source-IP restriction for all remaining SNMP access.
steps.guidance: Use network configuration management tooling to audit and enforce the SNMP hardening baseline across all devices.
steps.outcome: SNMP hardened/disabled across the environment per the updated baseline.

steps.title: Verify network device configuration integrity and monitoring
steps.desc: Confirm no unauthorized configuration changes were made to the affected devices and that heightened monitoring shows no follow-on activity.
steps.guidance: Compare current device configurations against last-known-good backups.
steps.outcome: Device configurations confirmed intact; no follow-on activity observed.

steps.title: Document incident and update network device hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record findings and formalize SNMPv3-only/source-restricted SNMP as a mandatory item in the network device hardening standard.
steps.outcome: Hardening standard updated and communicated to network operations.

steps.title: Determine what configuration/topology information was disclosed
steps.desc: Identify what MIB data was successfully queried (device configuration, routing tables, interface details, community strings) to assess exposure.
steps.guidance: Review the specific OIDs/queries that returned successful responses.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of information disclosed to the actor.

steps.title: Rotate SNMP community strings/credentials
steps.desc: Change SNMP community strings (v1/v2c) or credentials (v3) on all affected devices in case default or weak strings were exploited.
steps.guidance: Migrate to SNMPv3 with authentication/encryption where feasible rather than reusing v1/v2c community strings.
steps.outcome: SNMP credentials rotated and hardened.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent reconnaissance or exploitation attempts against network devices
steps.desc: Because SNMP enumeration often precedes targeted attacks against network infrastructure, establish heightened monitoring on the queried devices for follow-on configuration-change attempts or exploitation.
steps.guidance: Configure alerting on the affected devices for unauthorized configuration change attempts or additional SNMP write (SET) attempts.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place on the affected network devices.

ITID-42323.def: Enumeration performed by an automated vulnerability scanner (commercial, open-source, or adversary-operated) that systematically probes hosts and services for known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations as part of reconnaissance, distinguished by its automated, signature-driven, and comprehensive scan pattern.
ITID-42323.purpose: Captures reconnaissance conducted through automated vulnerability scanning tools rather than manual/targeted enumeration.
scopeIncludes: Third-party/adversary use of automated vulnerability scanning tools against the organization's exposed infrastructure
Scan traffic exhibiting characteristic signatures of known scanner products/frameworks
Enumeration output used to plan or select subsequent exploitation attempts
scopeExcludes: Manual/targeted banner grabbing (ITID-42321)
SNMP-specific device enumeration (ITID-42322)
The organization's own authorized/internal vulnerability scanning activity, which is not an incident
ITID-42323.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the scan identifies and is followed by exploitation of a genuine unpatched vulnerability.
ITID-42323.priority: P2 for confirmed unauthorized scanner activity; P1 if a vulnerability is confirmed exploited following the scan.
ITID-42323.escalation: Escalate to vulnerability management to prioritize patching of any genuinely vulnerable service identified; escalate to IR if exploitation follows.
indicators: Traffic matching known vulnerability scanner signatures (e.g., Nessus, OpenVAS, Nuclei templates) from an unauthorized source
High-volume, systematic probing across many services and known CVE checks from a single source in a short window
Source IP not matching the organization's authorized internal scanning infrastructure
vectors: Adversary use of commercial or open-source vulnerability scanners against internet-facing assets
Automated scan-and-exploit frameworks chaining enumeration directly into exploitation
rootCauses: Unpatched or misconfigured services discoverable by automated scanning
No allowlisting distinguishing authorized internal scans from unauthorized external ones
controls: Vulnerability management program to remediate discoverable weaknesses proactively
IDS/IPS signatures for known vulnerability scanner tooling
Allowlisting of authorized internal scanning source IPs
ITID-42323.detection: Strong — automated scanners generate distinctive, high-volume, signature-matched traffic that is well-suited to IDS/IPS detection.
ITID-42323.response: Confirm whether any identified vulnerability is genuinely exploitable and unpatched, prioritize remediation, and block the scanning source.
metrics: Count of unauthorized scanner detections per period
Time to remediate vulnerabilities confirmed discoverable by the scan
ITID-42323.notes: The differentiator from ITID-42321/42322 is the automated, tool-driven nature of the enumeration rather than manual/targeted probing.

playbook.name: Automated Vulnerability-Scanner-Driven Service Enumeration
playbook.description: An external actor ran an automated vulnerability scanning tool against exposed services to enumerate versions and identify known exploitable vulnerabilities, a reconnaissance activity typically preceding a targeted exploitation attempt.

steps.title: Detect automated scanner activity via IDS/IPS signatures and traffic pattern
steps.desc: Review IDS/IPS alerts for signatures matching known vulnerability scanning tools (e.g., Nessus, OpenVAS, Nikto, Qualys) and confirm the pattern of systematic, high-volume probing across many vulnerability checks against exposed services.
steps.guidance: Look for IDS/IPS signature hits tied to specific scanner tool fingerprints, plus a high volume of distinct probe types against the same hosts in a short window.
steps.outcome: Confirmed automated vulnerability scan activity with source, tool signature (if identifiable), and targeted hosts/services documented.
steps.abort: If source is a known/authorized vulnerability assessment vendor or internal scanning schedule, close as expected activity.

steps.title: Block the scanning source at the perimeter firewall
steps.desc: Add a deny rule for the confirmed unauthorized scanning source.
steps.outcome: Scanning source blocked from further reconnaissance.
steps.abort: Skip if source is confirmed authorized.

steps.title: Emergency-patch confirmed exploitable vulnerabilities
steps.desc: Prioritize and apply emergency patches or compensating controls (WAF rules, service restriction) for any vulnerabilities the scan likely confirmed as present and exploitable.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with system owners for expedited patching given the elevated risk of imminent targeted exploitation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitable vulnerabilities patched or mitigated.

steps.title: Verify remediation and confirm no follow-on exploitation
steps.desc: Run a vulnerability rescan to confirm the identified issues are resolved and review monitoring for any successful follow-on exploitation.
steps.outcome: Vulnerabilities confirmed remediated; no successful exploitation observed.

steps.title: Document incident and reinforce proactive vulnerability management cadence
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend increasing internal vulnerability scanning/patching cadence for externally exposed services to close gaps before external actors find them.
steps.outcome: Report filed; vulnerability management cadence reviewed.

steps.title: Determine which vulnerabilities the scan may have confirmed as present
steps.desc: Review which specific vulnerability checks returned indicators of a positive match (e.g., service responded in a way consistent with a vulnerable version) to assess what the actor now knows about exploitable weaknesses.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the specific probes/responses against the organization's own vulnerability scan results for the same hosts, if available, to estimate what the actor likely confirmed.
steps.outcome: List of vulnerabilities the actor likely confirmed as exploitable, prioritizing those for urgent remediation.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent targeted exploitation attempts
steps.desc: Because automated vulnerability scanning is a strong precursor to a targeted exploit attempt against a confirmed weakness, establish heightened, vulnerability-specific monitoring on the affected hosts rather than treating the incident as closed once scanning stops.
steps.guidance: Configure targeted detection rules for exploitation of the specific vulnerabilities likely confirmed by the scan.
steps.outcome: Heightened, vulnerability-specific monitoring in place on the affected hosts.

ITID-42324.def: General/unclassified service enumeration activity that cannot yet be attributed to banner grabbing, SNMP/device enumeration, or automated vulnerability-scanner-driven enumeration.
ITID-42324.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for service enumeration activity that does not yet fit a more specific sibling leaf.
scopeIncludes: Any confirmed service enumeration activity pending technique classification
scopeExcludes: Cases root-caused to banner grabbing (ITID-42321)
Cases root-caused to SNMP/device enumeration (ITID-42322)
Cases root-caused to automated vulnerability scanning (ITID-42323)
ITID-42324.severity: Default Medium pending triage; reassess once technique is determined.
ITID-42324.priority: P2 pending triage, escalating if follow-up exploitation is observed.
ITID-42324.escalation: Escalate to SOC for triage; reclassify once the specific technique is established.
indicators: Enumeration activity not yet matched to a specific known technique
vectors: Varies — captured here only until technique is determined
rootCauses: To be determined via investigation
controls: Standard incident triage workflow
ITID-42324.detection: Varies by underlying technique; general enumeration detection provides the initial signal.
ITID-42324.response: Triage promptly and reclassify the record once the specific technique is established.
metrics: Count of records held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to reclassification
ITID-42324.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; analysts should actively work to reclassify records out of it wherever a specific technique can be established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Service Enumeration
playbook.description: Service enumeration activity against exposed hosts was detected that does not match a more specific known technique, requiring general investigation to characterize the enumeration and assess risk of follow-on attack.

steps.title: Detect and characterize the enumeration activity via IDS/IPS and service logs
steps.desc: Review IDS/IPS alerts and service-level logs to confirm enumeration activity, source, targeted hosts/services, and what was likely disclosed.
steps.guidance: Look for systematic probing patterns across services beyond simple port scanning, indicating an attempt to identify service types/versions.
steps.outcome: Confirmed enumeration activity with source, scope, and disclosed information documented.
steps.abort: If source is a known/authorized scanning vendor, close as expected activity.

steps.title: Block the source performing enumeration
steps.desc: Add a deny rule for the confirmed unauthorized source at the perimeter firewall.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further reconnaissance.
steps.abort: Skip if source is confirmed authorized.

steps.title: Remediate any exposed weaknesses identified during enumeration
steps.desc: Patch, upgrade, or restrict access to any services found to disclose exploitable information during the enumeration.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with system owners for remediation prioritized by exposure severity.
steps.outcome: Identified weaknesses remediated.

steps.title: Verify remediation and confirm no follow-on exploitation
steps.desc: Confirm remediated services are secure and no follow-on exploitation succeeded during the monitoring window.
steps.guidance: Run a vulnerability rescan on the affected hosts.
steps.outcome: Services confirmed secure; no exploitation observed.

steps.title: Document findings and reinforce external service hardening review
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend periodic review of externally exposed service configurations.
steps.outcome: Report filed; review scheduled as appropriate.

steps.title: Check source against threat intelligence
steps.desc: Determine whether the source is known-malicious infrastructure or previously unseen.
steps.guidance: Query threat intel feeds for source IP reputation.
steps.outcome: Source classification established.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent exploitation attempts
steps.desc: Because enumeration often precedes a larger attack, establish heightened monitoring on the affected hosts/services rather than treating the incident as closed once enumeration stops.
steps.guidance: Configure a monitoring watch on the affected hosts/services for a defined follow-up period.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place; follow-on activity, if any, identified and handled.

ITID-42331.def: Active network topology discovery in which an adversary sends probes (ICMP echo requests, traceroute packets, TCP/UDP probes) across a range of addresses to determine which hosts are alive and how network paths/hops are structured, generating visible traffic in the process.
ITID-42331.purpose: Captures reconnaissance that actively probes the network to build a map of its topology, using techniques such as traceroute and ping sweeps.
scopeIncludes: Ping sweeps across a subnet or address range to identify live hosts
Traceroute-style probing to map network paths and hop topology
Active probing generating detectable ICMP/TCP/UDP traffic patterns
scopeExcludes: Passive topology discovery via traffic observation only (ITID-42332)
Cloud API-based asset enumeration (ITID-42333)
Port/service-level scanning once hosts are already identified (Port Scanning and Service Enumeration Tier-4 categories)
ITID-42331.severity: Low-Medium standalone; escalate if it precedes targeted scanning or exploitation of discovered live hosts.
ITID-42331.priority: P3 for isolated mapping activity; P2 if followed by targeted scanning of discovered hosts.
ITID-42331.escalation: Escalate to SOC for source tracking; escalate further only if mapping is followed by scanning/exploitation against discovered assets.
indicators: Sequential ICMP echo requests across a contiguous address range
Traceroute-pattern traffic (incrementing TTL probes) from a single source
IDS alerts for ping sweep/network mapping tool signatures
vectors: Commodity network mapping tools (e.g., Nmap ping sweep, fping) run against internal or external ranges
Traceroute used to infer network segmentation and routing structure
rootCauses: ICMP not restricted at network/segment boundaries
No rate-limiting or alerting on high-volume ping sweep patterns
mitreTechniques: T1595.001 Active Scanning: Scanning IP Blocks
controls: ICMP rate-limiting/restriction at network boundaries
IDS/IPS detection for ping sweep and traceroute patterns
Network segmentation limiting the address space reachable from any single point
ITID-42331.detection: Strong — active probing generates clear, high-volume, easily-signatured traffic patterns.
ITID-42331.response: Block or rate-limit the source, and monitor discovered live hosts for follow-up scanning or exploitation attempts.
metrics: Count of active mapping/ping sweep events detected per period
ITID-42331.notes: Differentiates from ITID-42332 by being an active, detectable probing technique rather than passive observation.

playbook.name: Active Network Topology Mapping (Traceroute/Ping Sweep)
playbook.description: An actor performed active network topology mapping using techniques such as ICMP ping sweeps and traceroute against the organization's network to identify live hosts and infer network structure/segmentation.

steps.title: Detect ping sweep/traceroute activity via IDS/IPS and flow logs
steps.desc: Review IDS/IPS alerts and firewall/flow logs for a pattern of ICMP echo requests across a broad address range, or incrementing-TTL traceroute traffic, from a source attempting to map the network.
steps.guidance: Look for ICMP sweep patterns (sequential or ranged destination addresses) or characteristic traceroute TTL-increment patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed topology-mapping activity with source, scope of addresses probed, and inferred information documented.
steps.abort: If source is a known/authorized network monitoring or scanning tool, close as expected activity.

steps.title: Block the source performing the mapping activity
steps.desc: Add a deny rule for the confirmed unauthorized source at the perimeter firewall.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further reconnaissance.
steps.abort: Skip if source is confirmed authorized.

steps.title: Review network segmentation exposed by the mapping
steps.desc: Assess whether the mapping revealed unintended network segmentation weaknesses (e.g., internal hosts reachable that should be isolated) and remediate.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference discovered live hosts against intended segmentation design; correct any unintended reachability.
steps.outcome: Unintended segmentation exposure remediated.

steps.title: Maintain heightened monitoring on discovered hosts
steps.desc: Continue elevated monitoring on the hosts discovered during the mapping activity for a defined follow-up period.
steps.guidance: Configure a time-boxed heightened-alert rule in the SIEM.
steps.outcome: Monitoring window completed with no follow-on attack activity, or follow-on activity caught and handled.

steps.title: Document activity and reinforce network exposure reduction practices
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend ICMP/traceroute exposure reduction as part of standard perimeter hardening review.
steps.outcome: Report filed; hardening review scheduled as appropriate.

steps.title: Determine what topology/segmentation information was likely inferred
steps.desc: Assess what live hosts and network path information the actor likely derived from the sweep/traceroute results, informing the scope of subsequent risk.
steps.guidance: Reconstruct the probed address ranges and correlate against actual live-host and network segment layout to estimate what the actor learned.
steps.outcome: Documented estimate of topology information disclosed.

steps.title: Restrict ICMP and traceroute responsiveness where not operationally required
steps.desc: Reduce the network's responsiveness to unsolicited ICMP echo requests and traceroute probes from untrusted sources to limit future topology disclosure.
steps.guidance: Apply firewall rules to rate-limit or block inbound ICMP echo from untrusted zones where not needed for legitimate diagnostics, and consider filtering ICMP TTL-exceeded responses at the perimeter.
steps.outcome: Reduced topology information leakage via ICMP-based probing.
steps.abort: Skip if ICMP responsiveness is required for legitimate external diagnostics/monitoring partners, and rely on monitoring instead.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent scanning or exploitation attempts against discovered live hosts
steps.desc: Because topology mapping often precedes targeted port scanning or exploitation of specific discovered hosts, establish heightened monitoring on the identified live hosts rather than treating the incident as closed once the mapping activity stops.
steps.guidance: Configure a monitoring watch on hosts confirmed as discovered/live during the mapping activity.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place on the discovered hosts.

ITID-42332.def: Passive network topology discovery in which an adversary who already has visibility into network traffic (via a compromised host, tap, or sniffing position) infers segment structure, routing, and device relationships from observed traffic patterns without sending any active probes of their own.
ITID-42332.purpose: Captures reconnaissance that infers network topology by passively observing traffic rather than generating active probes.
scopeIncludes: Inference of network topology from ARP tables, routing announcements, or observed broadcast/multicast traffic
Passive analysis of captured traffic to map segment boundaries and device roles
Topology discovery performed from a position already gained via packet sniffing (ITID-4234x)
scopeExcludes: Active probing such as ping sweeps/traceroute (ITID-42331)
Cloud API-based asset enumeration (ITID-42333)
The initial sniffing/capture technique used to gain visibility, which is covered under the Packet Sniffing Tier-4 category
ITID-42332.severity: Medium — indicates the adversary already has a foothold with network visibility, since passive mapping requires an existing vantage point.
ITID-42332.priority: P2 upon confirmation of a foothold being used for passive topology inference; escalate to P1 if paired with active lateral movement.
ITID-42332.escalation: Escalate to IR — passive mapping implies a prior compromise granting traffic visibility, which itself needs investigation and containment.
indicators: Evidence of a compromised host or device running passive capture/analysis tooling
Traffic analysis logs on a compromised endpoint referencing ARP table or routing data collection
No corresponding active-scan traffic despite evidence of topology knowledge being used by the adversary
vectors: Malware or implant on a compromised host passively cataloguing network structure
A rogue device or tap positioned to observe traffic and build a topology map without generating probes
rootCauses: Prior compromise granting the adversary a passive traffic-visibility position
Insufficient network segmentation limiting how much topology is visible from any single vantage point
controls: Network segmentation limiting topology visibility from any single compromised point
Host-based detection for passive capture/analysis tooling
Encrypted routing/management protocols limiting passively observable topology data
ITID-42332.detection: Weak — passive techniques generate no distinguishing network traffic; detection depends on identifying the underlying compromise/foothold.
ITID-42332.response: Investigate and remediate the underlying foothold granting traffic visibility; assess what topology information may have been inferred.
metrics: Count of confirmed passive mapping incidents tied to an identified foothold per period
ITID-42332.notes: Differentiates from ITID-42331 by requiring no active probing; the security signal here is the underlying foothold, not the mapping itself.

playbook.name: Passive Network Topology Discovery via Traffic Analysis
playbook.description: An actor with access to a network segment passively analyzed observed traffic (broadcast/multicast protocols, routing advertisements, DHCP/ARP chatter) to infer network topology and segmentation without generating active probe traffic, making the activity harder to detect than active scanning.

steps.title: Identify the vantage point and indicators of passive monitoring
steps.desc: Because passive discovery generates no active probe traffic, focus identification on identifying an unauthorized listening presence — an unexpected device in promiscuous/monitor mode, an unauthorized SPAN/mirror port configuration, or a compromised host running packet-capture tooling.
steps.guidance: Review switch port security/CAM table anomalies, NAC logs for unrecognized devices, and EDR telemetry for packet-capture tool execution (e.g., tcpdump, Wireshark) on hosts without an authorized business need.
steps.outcome: Identified vantage point or device responsible for passive traffic analysis, if determinable.
steps.abort: If no vantage point or supporting evidence can be identified and the alert is based on weak circumstantial indicators, document as a low-confidence finding and proceed to hardening steps rather than active containment.

steps.title: Remove the unauthorized monitoring presence and secure switch port configuration
steps.desc: If an unauthorized device, SPAN/mirror port, or compromised host performing the capture was identified, disconnect/remediate it and correct any switch mirroring misconfiguration.
steps.guidance: Physically or logically disconnect the offending device; review and correct any switch SPAN/mirror port configuration that inadvertently exposed traffic.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized passive monitoring presence removed.
steps.abort: Skip if no specific device/configuration could be conclusively identified; proceed directly to broader switch-security hardening instead.

steps.title: Implement switch port security controls to prevent future unauthorized monitoring access
steps.desc: Deploy port security (limiting MAC addresses per port), disable unused switch ports, and enforce NAC-based authentication for any device connecting to the segment.
steps.guidance: Apply 802.1X or MAC-based NAC enforcement and port-security violation actions (shutdown/restrict) on switch ports in the affected segment.
steps.outcome: Switch port security controls in place preventing unauthorized device connection for future passive monitoring.

steps.title: Verify segment security posture and maintain heightened monitoring
steps.desc: Confirm switch port security and broadcast-reduction controls are functioning and continue heightened monitoring on high-value systems for a defined follow-up period.
steps.guidance: Spot-check port security enforcement and confirm no unauthorized devices remain connected.
steps.outcome: Segment confirmed secured; heightened monitoring window completed with no follow-on activity.

steps.title: Document findings and update switch security baseline
steps.desc: Record findings and formalize port security, NAC enforcement, and broadcast-protocol restriction as mandatory items in the network switch hardening baseline.
steps.outcome: Hardening baseline updated and communicated to network operations.

steps.title: Assess what topology information was likely exposed via observable broadcast/routing traffic
steps.desc: Review what broadcast, multicast, routing-protocol, and DHCP/ARP traffic was present on the segment the actor had access to, to estimate what topology information could have been passively inferred.
steps.guidance: Inventory the protocols broadcasting on the segment (e.g., CDP/LLDP, OSPF/EIGRP hellos, DHCP, ARP) and assess what network structure they would reveal to a passive observer.
steps.outcome: Documented estimate of topology information likely exposed.

steps.title: Reduce broadcast/routing information leakage on the segment
steps.desc: Restrict or disable unnecessary broadcast/discovery protocols (e.g., CDP/LLDP on user-facing ports) that reveal topology information to anyone with segment access.
steps.guidance: Disable CDP/LLDP on access ports where not required for legitimate device discovery (e.g., VoIP phones); confirm routing protocol authentication is enabled to prevent unauthorized routing-advertisement snooping abuse.
steps.outcome: Reduced passive topology information leakage on the segment.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent active reconnaissance or targeted access attempts
steps.desc: Because passive mapping often precedes a targeted active attack once the actor has topology knowledge, establish heightened monitoring across the segment and any high-value systems the traffic analysis would have revealed.
steps.guidance: Configure a monitoring watch for subsequent active scanning or access attempts against systems that would have been identifiable from the observed traffic.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place across the affected segment and likely-identified high-value systems.

ITID-42333.def: Enumeration of cloud environment assets and network structure (VPCs/VNets, subnets, security groups, instances, load balancers) via cloud provider management APIs, typically using leaked or compromised cloud credentials rather than traditional network-layer probing.
ITID-42333.purpose: Captures reconnaissance conducted against cloud provider APIs to enumerate the organization's cloud-hosted network assets and topology.
scopeIncludes: API calls enumerating VPC/VNet structure, subnets, security groups, and instance inventories
Use of compromised or overly permissive cloud IAM credentials to enumerate network configuration
Reconnaissance conducted entirely through the cloud control plane rather than the data plane
scopeExcludes: Traditional active network probing (ITID-42331)
Passive traffic-based topology inference (ITID-42332)
Exploitation of a discovered cloud misconfiguration itself (covered under the relevant cloud-specific ITIDs elsewhere in the taxonomy)
ITID-42333.severity: Medium-High — successful cloud API enumeration can reveal the entire network architecture in a single set of API calls, far more efficiently than traditional scanning.
ITID-42333.priority: P2 for confirmed unauthorized enumeration; P1 if paired with evidence of a compromised cloud credential being actively used for further access.
ITID-42333.escalation: Escalate to cloud security/IR to rotate the credential used and review IAM permissions that allowed such broad enumeration.
indicators: Cloud audit logs (e.g., CloudTrail, Azure Activity Log) showing a burst of read-only network/describe API calls from an unfamiliar identity or location
API calls enumerating security groups, subnets, and instances outside normal operational patterns
Cloud IAM credential usage inconsistent with its typical usage baseline
vectors: Leaked or phished cloud API credentials used to call describe/list network APIs
Overly permissive IAM roles allowing broad read access to network configuration
Compromised CI/CD pipeline credentials with cloud network read access
rootCauses: IAM roles granted broader network-read permissions than required (violation of least privilege)
No anomaly detection on cloud API call volume/pattern for network-enumeration-related actions
Cloud credentials not rotated or scoped tightly enough
controls: Least-privilege IAM scoping for network-read permissions
Cloud audit log monitoring/UEBA for anomalous enumeration API call patterns
Credential rotation and short-lived/temporary credential use
ITID-42333.detection: Strong when cloud audit logging (e.g., CloudTrail) is enabled and monitored; absent without centralized cloud API log analysis.
ITID-42333.response: Rotate the credential used, review and tighten the IAM permissions that enabled the enumeration, and assess what was exposed.
metrics: Count of anomalous cloud network-enumeration API call bursts detected per period
Percentage of IAM roles scoped to least privilege for network-read actions
detections: Cloud API anomalous enumeration burst alert
ITID-42333.notes: This leaf captures the cloud-native reconnaissance angle, distinguishing it from traditional on-premises active/passive network mapping techniques.

playbook.name: Cloud Environment Asset/Network Mapping via API Enumeration
playbook.description: An actor with valid or stolen cloud credentials used cloud provider APIs (e.g., describe/list calls across compute, networking, and IAM services) to enumerate cloud assets, network configuration, and security groups to map the cloud environment for further attack planning.

steps.title: Detect anomalous cloud API enumeration activity via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud provider audit logs (e.g., CloudTrail, Azure Activity Log, GCP Audit Logs) for a high volume of read-only describe/list/get API calls across multiple services in a short window, especially from an unusual identity, source IP, or region.
steps.guidance: Look for enumeration-characteristic API call sequences (e.g., DescribeInstances, ListBuckets, DescribeSecurityGroups, GetIAMPolicy) from a single principal at a rate or breadth inconsistent with normal administrative behavior.
steps.outcome: Confirmed cloud API enumeration activity with the identity/credential used, source, and scope of services queried documented.
steps.abort: If the activity matches an authorized security tool (e.g., CSPM scanner) or known administrative behavior, close as expected activity.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs (CloudTrail/Activity Log/Audit Logs) / SIEM

steps.title: Disable or rotate the compromised cloud credential immediately
steps.desc: Disable the compromised IAM user/role/access key and rotate any associated credentials to prevent further use.
steps.guidance: Deactivate the access key/service principal and revoke active sessions/tokens via the cloud IAM console.
steps.outcome: Compromised credential invalidated; no further API calls possible under it.

steps.title: Remediate the credential exposure root cause and enforce least-privilege IAM policy
steps.desc: Close the specific exposure vector (rotate leaked keys, remove hardcoded credentials from code, fix over-privileged role) and rebuild the affected identity's permissions under a least-privilege model.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with development/platform teams to remove any hardcoded credentials, implement short-lived credentials (e.g., workload identity federation) where possible, and scope IAM policies to only required actions/resources.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure vector closed; least-privilege IAM policy enforced for the affected identity.
steps.tool: Cloud IAM console / CI/CD pipeline configuration

steps.title: Verify no unauthorized resource changes occurred and restore normal operations
steps.desc: Confirm no cloud resources were modified or accessed without authorization following the enumeration, and restore legitimate access for the affected identity under corrected permissions.
steps.guidance: Review cloud configuration change history and compare against expected baseline (e.g., via infrastructure-as-code drift detection).
steps.outcome: No unauthorized changes confirmed; legitimate access restored under least-privilege policy.
steps.tool: Cloud configuration drift detection / IaC tooling

steps.title: Document incident and enhance cloud API activity monitoring
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend enabling or tuning cloud-native anomaly detection (e.g., GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud) to catch future enumeration patterns proactively, plus a broader credential-hygiene review (secret scanning, key rotation policy).
steps.outcome: Report filed; monitoring and credential-hygiene improvements tracked for implementation.

steps.title: Determine how the cloud credential/identity was obtained
steps.desc: Investigate whether the identity used for enumeration is a compromised human user, a leaked service account/access key, or an over-privileged workload identity, to determine root cause.
steps.guidance: Review the credential's authentication history, check for leaked-key indicators (e.g., key found in a public code repository via secret-scanning alerts), and review IAM policy attached to the identity.
steps.outcome: Root cause of credential exposure identified.

steps.title: Apply an emergency deny policy or restrict the identity's permissions scope
steps.desc: If immediate credential disablement is not feasible due to a critical dependency, apply a restrictive IAM policy limiting the identity to only essential actions while investigation continues.
steps.guidance: Attach an explicit deny policy for sensitive/high-risk API actions to the affected identity as an interim measure.
steps.outcome: Identity's blast radius reduced pending full remediation.
steps.abort: Skip if the credential was fully disabled in the prior step.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent resource-modification or data-access attempts
steps.desc: Because cloud API enumeration typically precedes a targeted attempt to access or modify a specific discovered resource (e.g., an exposed storage bucket or a misconfigured security group), establish heightened monitoring on resources identified during the enumeration.
steps.guidance: Configure cloud-native alerting (e.g., GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud) or SIEM correlation for write/modify API calls following the enumeration from the same identity or related identities.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place on enumerated resources; any follow-on access/modification attempts identified.

ITID-42334.def: General/unclassified network topology mapping activity that cannot yet be attributed to active probing, passive observation, or cloud API enumeration.
ITID-42334.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for network mapping activity that does not yet fit a more specific sibling leaf.
scopeIncludes: Any confirmed network mapping activity pending technique classification
scopeExcludes: Cases root-caused to active probing (ITID-42331)
Cases root-caused to passive observation (ITID-42332)
Cases root-caused to cloud API enumeration (ITID-42333)
ITID-42334.severity: Default Low-Medium pending triage; reassess once technique is determined.
ITID-42334.priority: P3 pending triage, escalating if follow-up activity is observed.
ITID-42334.escalation: Escalate to SOC for triage; reclassify once the specific technique is established.
indicators: Mapping/topology-discovery activity not yet matched to a specific known technique
vectors: Varies — captured here only until technique is determined
rootCauses: To be determined via investigation
controls: Standard incident triage workflow
ITID-42334.response: Triage promptly and reclassify the record once the specific technique is established.
metrics: Count of records held in unclassified status beyond SLA
Time to reclassification
ITID-42334.notes: This is a catch-all/intake leaf; analysts should actively work to reclassify records out of it wherever a specific technique can be established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Network Mapping
playbook.description: Network mapping activity was detected that does not match a more specific known technique, requiring general investigation to characterize the mapping method and assess risk of follow-on attack.

steps.title: Detect and characterize the mapping activity via available logs
steps.desc: Review IDS/IPS, firewall/flow logs, and relevant infrastructure logs (cloud audit logs, NAC, or wireless controller logs as applicable) to confirm mapping activity, source, and scope of the network/assets probed.
steps.guidance: Determine whether the activity is active (probing) or passive (traffic analysis), and identify the environment involved (on-premises network vs. cloud).
steps.outcome: Confirmed mapping activity with source, scope, and technique documented.
steps.abort: If source is a known/authorized scanning or monitoring tool, close as expected activity.
steps.tool: IDS/IPS / firewall flow logs / relevant infrastructure logs

steps.title: Block or restrict the source performing the mapping activity
steps.desc: Add a deny rule or access restriction for the confirmed unauthorized source at the appropriate control point (firewall, cloud IAM, NAC).
steps.guidance: Select the containment mechanism appropriate to the environment where mapping was detected.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further reconnaissance.
steps.abort: Skip if source is confirmed authorized.

steps.title: Remediate exposure that enabled the mapping activity
steps.desc: Close the specific gap that allowed the mapping (excessive permissions, unnecessary broadcast/response services, unrestricted API access) based on root cause identified.
steps.guidance: Tailor remediation to the specific environment and technique identified during investigation.
steps.outcome: Root-cause exposure closed.

steps.title: Maintain heightened monitoring and verify remediation
steps.desc: Confirm the exposure is remediated and continue elevated monitoring on discovered assets for a defined follow-up period.
steps.outcome: Monitoring window completed with no follow-on attack activity, or follow-on activity caught and handled.

steps.title: Document findings and reinforce exposure-reduction practices
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend periodic review of network/asset exposure appropriate to the environment involved.
steps.outcome: Report filed; review scheduled as appropriate.

steps.title: Determine what topology/asset information was likely disclosed
steps.desc: Assess what information about the network or asset inventory the actor likely gained from the mapping activity.
steps.guidance: Reconstruct the scope of hosts/services/resources probed and compare against actual environment layout.
steps.outcome: Documented estimate of information disclosed.

steps.title: Correlate with subsequent scanning or exploitation attempts
steps.desc: Because network mapping often precedes a larger attack, establish heightened monitoring on discovered assets rather than treating the incident as closed once mapping activity stops.
steps.guidance: Configure a monitoring watch for a defined follow-up period on assets confirmed as discovered during the mapping.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place; follow-on activity, if any, identified and handled.

ITID-42341.def: Passive capture of unencrypted or partially-visible network traffic from an already-accessible vantage point (e.g., a compromised host, a shared broadcast segment, or a network tap) for reconnaissance purposes such as harvesting credentials, session tokens, or topology data.
ITID-42341.purpose: Captures reconnaissance that captures network traffic from a vantage point without needing to manipulate the network path to obtain it.
scopeIncludes: Packet capture from a compromised host's own network interface
Capture on a hub-based or misconfigured switch segment where traffic is broadcast
Reconnaissance-focused capture and analysis of unencrypted protocol traffic (e.g., plaintext credentials, DNS, HTTP)
scopeExcludes: ARP spoofing used to actively redirect traffic to the capture point (ITID-42342)
Wireless-specific packet capture (ITID-42343)
Passive topology inference as the primary objective (ITID-42332, a closely related but topology-focused use of similar techniques)
ITID-42341.severity: Medium-High — successful capture of unencrypted traffic can directly yield credentials or sensitive data.
ITID-42341.priority: P2 upon confirmation of capture tooling on a host or segment; P1 if credentials or sensitive data are confirmed harvested from the capture.
ITID-42341.escalation: Escalate to IR to remediate the underlying foothold and assess what data was exposed via the capture.
indicators: Host-based detection of packet capture tooling (e.g., tcpdump, Wireshark, raw socket libraries) running without authorization
Network interface placed in promiscuous mode unexpectedly
Evidence of harvested plaintext credentials being used elsewhere shortly after capture activity
vectors: Malware or implant on a compromised host running a packet capture utility
Legacy hub-based network segments or misconfigured switch port mirroring exposing traffic broadly
rootCauses: Sensitive protocols still transmitted in cleartext internally
Switched network not fully eliminating broadcast-domain exposure on legacy segments
No host-based monitoring for unauthorized promiscuous-mode network interfaces
controls: Encrypt sensitive protocols end-to-end (eliminate cleartext credential transmission)
Host-based detection of promiscuous-mode network interfaces and capture tooling
Elimination of legacy hub/broadcast-exposed network segments
ITID-42341.detection: Moderate — host-based EDR can detect promiscuous mode and capture tooling; network-layer detection of passive listening itself is inherently difficult.
ITID-42341.response: Remediate the underlying foothold, rotate any credentials potentially exposed in cleartext, and move affected protocols to encrypted alternatives.
metrics: Count of confirmed unauthorized capture tooling detections per period
Percentage of internal protocols still transmitted in cleartext
ITID-42341.notes: Differentiates from ITID-42342 by requiring no active traffic redirection — the adversary already has a vantage point where traffic is naturally visible.

playbook.name: Passive Network Traffic Capture for Reconnaissance
playbook.description: An actor with access to a wired network segment passively captured network traffic (e.g., via a compromised host, rogue tap, or misconfigured mirror port) to harvest credentials, session data, or reconnaissance information without generating active probe traffic.

steps.title: Identify the packet-capture vantage point
steps.desc: Because passive sniffing generates no active probe traffic, detection is harder — focus on identifying an unauthorized listening presence: a host running packet-capture tooling without business justification, an unauthorized physical tap, or a misconfigured SPAN/mirror port.
steps.guidance: Review EDR telemetry for packet-capture tool execution (tcpdump, Wireshark, tshark) on hosts lacking authorized business need, and audit switch SPAN/mirror port configurations for unexpected entries.
steps.outcome: Identified vantage point/device responsible for the packet capture, if determinable.
steps.abort: If no vantage point or supporting evidence can be identified beyond a weak circumstantial indicator, document as a low-confidence finding and proceed directly to switch-security hardening steps.

steps.title: Remove the unauthorized capture presence and secure switch port configuration
steps.desc: Disconnect/remediate the identified device or host performing the capture, and correct any switch port security or SPAN/mirror misconfiguration that enabled it.
steps.guidance: Use switch port security (limit MAC addresses per port), disable unused switch ports, and enable Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) and DHCP snooping to prevent related MITM positioning.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized capture presence removed; switch security controls tightened.
steps.abort: Skip if no specific device could be conclusively identified; proceed directly to broader switch-security hardening instead.

steps.title: Eliminate unencrypted protocol usage on the affected segment
steps.desc: Migrate any remaining unencrypted/legacy protocols in use on the segment to encrypted equivalents to remove the underlying data-exposure risk from passive sniffing.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with system/application owners to disable legacy protocols (e.g., LDAP without TLS, Telnet, SMBv1) and enforce encrypted alternatives.
steps.outcome: Segment no longer transmits sensitive data in cleartext.

steps.title: Verify segment security posture and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Confirm switch security controls are functioning and monitor the segment for any recurrence of unauthorized capture activity.
steps.guidance: Spot-check port security enforcement and review switch logs for a defined follow-up period.
steps.outcome: Segment confirmed secured; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document findings and update switch/network hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record findings and formalize port security, DHCP snooping, DAI, and encrypted-protocol-only requirements in the network hardening baseline.
steps.outcome: Hardening baseline updated and communicated to network operations.

steps.title: Assess what sensitive data (credentials, session tokens) may have been exposed in captured traffic
steps.desc: Review what protocols were in use on the affected segment during the capture window to determine what sensitive information (e.g., unencrypted credentials, session cookies) may have been exposed.
steps.guidance: Inventory unencrypted or weakly-encrypted protocols in use on the segment (e.g., legacy LDAP, HTTP, Telnet, SMBv1) during the relevant timeframe.
steps.outcome: Documented estimate of sensitive data exposure risk from the capture.

steps.title: Force credential resets for accounts potentially exposed via captured traffic
steps.desc: If unencrypted credential transmission was likely captured, force a password reset for the affected accounts as a precaution.
steps.guidance: Identify accounts that authenticated over the affected segment using unencrypted protocols during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.
steps.abort: Skip if no unencrypted credential transmission was in use on the segment during the exposure window.

steps.title: Deploy switch port security and network access control on the affected segment
steps.desc: Implement port security, DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, and 802.1X/NAC enforcement on the affected segment to prevent unauthorized devices from gaining passive-capture positioning in the future.
steps.guidance: Apply these controls consistently across the segment, not just on the specific port where the incident occurred.
steps.outcome: Switch-level controls in place preventing future unauthorized capture access.

ITID-42342.def: Use of ARP spoofing/cache poisoning to redirect traffic between two or more hosts through an adversary-controlled position on the local network segment, enabling on-path (man-in-the-middle) interception and capture of traffic that would not otherwise be visible from the adversary's actual network location.
ITID-42342.purpose: Captures reconnaissance that actively manipulates the local network path (via ARP spoofing) to position itself as an on-path interceptor before capturing traffic.
scopeIncludes: ARP cache poisoning used to redirect victim-to-gateway or victim-to-victim traffic through an attacker-controlled host
On-path positioning achieved specifically via Layer 2 ARP manipulation
Traffic capture/manipulation performed after successful ARP spoofing is established
scopeExcludes: Passive capture from a naturally-visible vantage point requiring no traffic redirection (ITID-42341)
Wireless-specific packet capture (ITID-42343)
ITID-42342.severity: High — active on-path positioning enables both interception and potential manipulation of traffic, a materially more capable position than passive capture.
ITID-42342.priority: P1 upon confirmed ARP spoofing activity, given the active manipulation of network traffic paths.
ITID-42342.escalation: Escalate immediately to network security and IR; ARP spoofing indicates an adversary already has a foothold on the local segment and is actively escalating capability.
indicators: Duplicate or conflicting ARP replies for the same IP address mapping to different MAC addresses
Switch/network monitoring showing MAC address flapping inconsistent with normal device behavior
Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) or similar control triggering violations
vectors: Commodity ARP spoofing tooling (e.g., Ettercap, Bettercap) run from a compromised host on the local segment
Physical access to the network segment enabling direct ARP poisoning
rootCauses: No Dynamic ARP Inspection or equivalent Layer 2 protection deployed on switches
Flat network segments with no port security limiting who can send ARP traffic
Lack of static ARP entries or equivalent hardening for critical Layer 2 paths
controls: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) on managed switches
Port security limiting MAC/ARP behavior per switch port
Network segmentation reducing the population reachable via Layer 2 ARP manipulation
ITID-42342.detection: Strong where DAI or equivalent switch-level Layer 2 monitoring is deployed; weak on flat, unmonitored segments.
ITID-42342.response: Isolate the offending host/port immediately, restore correct ARP mappings, and investigate what traffic was intercepted during the spoofing window.
metrics: Count of ARP spoofing/DAI violation alerts per period
Percentage of switches with DAI or equivalent enabled
ITID-42342.notes: This is the active-MITM-positioning sibling; the differentiator from ITID-42341 is deliberate traffic redirection rather than capture from an already-visible vantage point.

playbook.name: ARP Spoofing-Enabled Packet Sniffing (Active MITM Positioning)
playbook.description: An actor on the local network segment performed ARP spoofing/cache poisoning to position themselves as a man-in-the-middle, redirecting and capturing traffic between victim hosts and the gateway for reconnaissance or credential harvesting.

steps.title: Detect ARP spoofing activity via switch and endpoint indicators
steps.desc: Review switch logs (Dynamic ARP Inspection violations, if enabled) and endpoint/EDR telemetry for ARP cache anomalies (duplicate/conflicting MAC-to-IP mappings, gratuitous ARP floods) indicating spoofing.
steps.guidance: Look for DAI drop/violation logs on switches, or ARP table inconsistencies reported by endpoint security tooling across multiple hosts on the same segment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed ARP spoofing activity with the attacking device's MAC/IP and affected victim hosts identified.
steps.abort: If no ARP anomaly evidence is found, verify whether the alert was triggered by a legitimate network change (e.g., failover/HSRP).

steps.title: Disconnect the attacking device from the network
steps.desc: Identify the physical/logical switch port associated with the spoofing device's MAC address and disable it, or quarantine the device via NAC.
steps.guidance: Use switch CAM table lookup to locate the port, then administratively shut it down or apply a NAC quarantine VLAN.
steps.outcome: Attacking device disconnected; ARP spoofing activity halted.

steps.title: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection and DHCP snooping on the affected segment
steps.desc: Deploy DAI (validating ARP packets against the DHCP snooping binding table) and DHCP snooping on all switches serving the affected segment to prevent future ARP spoofing.
steps.guidance: Configure DHCP snooping first to build a trusted binding table, then enable DAI referencing that table; apply consistently across all access switches on the segment, not just the affected port.
steps.outcome: ARP spoofing prevented at the switch level going forward on the affected segment.
