ITID-43321.severity: High — successful positioning allows full visibility and potential manipulation of the RDP session, including credential capture.
ITID-43321.priority: P1 upon confirmed on-path positioning against an RDP session.
ITID-43321.escalation: Escalate to network engineering to remediate the positioning technique (e.g. dynamic ARP inspection) and to IR to assess session compromise.
indicators: ARP table anomalies (duplicate/conflicting MAC-to-IP mappings) on the segment
RDP client TLS/CredSSP warnings not normally seen
Unexpected additional hop or latency in RDP session path
vectors: ARP spoofing tools used to redirect RDP traffic through an attacker-controlled host
Rogue switch/access point positioned on the RDP client's network segment
rootCauses: No dynamic ARP inspection or port security on network switches
RDP sessions traversing untrusted or shared network segments without a VPN
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
controls: Dynamic ARP inspection and port security on switches
Network Level Authentication (NLA) enforcement
VPN/tunnel requirement for RDP over untrusted segments
ITID-43321.detection: Moderate — network monitoring for ARP anomalies catches this reliably where deployed; otherwise relies on client-side TLS warning reports.
ITID-43321.response: Remediate the ARP/positioning vector, force password reset for any account whose session was intercepted, and validate NLA/TLS enforcement.
metrics: ARP anomaly alerts investigated
Percentage of network segments with dynamic ARP inspection enabled
ITID-43321.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43322 by mechanism: network-layer positioning rather than certificate-validation failure.

playbook.name: RDP Session Hijacked via ARP Spoofing/On-Path Positioning
playbook.description: An attacker used ARP spoofing to position on-path between a client and RDP server, intercepting or hijacking the remote desktop session.

steps.title: Detect ARP spoofing enabling the on-path position
steps.desc: Review switch ARP/CAM tables and endpoint ARP caches for duplicate/conflicting MAC-to-IP bindings on the segment hosting the RDP client or server.
steps.guidance: Look for gratuitous ARP storms and a single MAC claiming multiple IPs including the RDP server's IP.
steps.outcome: On-path attacker device identified on the segment.

steps.title: Isolate the on-path attacking device
steps.desc: Shut down or NAC-quarantine the switch port of the device performing ARP spoofing.
steps.outcome: ARP spoofing traffic stops.

steps.title: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection and DHCP snooping on the segment
steps.desc: Configure DAI/DHCP snooping on affected switches to prevent future ARP-based on-path positioning against RDP or any protocol.
steps.outcome: DAI/DHCP snooping active and verified.

steps.title: Restore normal RDP access and monitor the segment
steps.desc: Confirm affected users can reconnect normally and monitor the segment for renewed ARP spoofing or certificate warnings.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 7-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and extend DAI/certificate hardening org-wide
steps.desc: Record the attack path and verify DAI and RDP certificate hardening are applied across all access-layer switches and RDP hosts, not just the affected segment.
steps.outcome: Hardening extended org-wide; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess RDP session integrity and certificate warnings
steps.desc: Review client-side RDP connection logs/event IDs for certificate mismatch warnings or unexpected reconnects that indicate the session was intercepted.
steps.guidance: Check Event ID 1024/1025 (RDP client) and TerminalServices-RemoteConnectionManager logs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed session interception evidence and affected user/session identified.

steps.title: Terminate and reset the hijacked RDP session
steps.desc: Force-terminate the active RDP session and require the user to re-authenticate over a verified clean path.
steps.outcome: Hijacked session terminated; attacker no longer has session control.

steps.title: Enforce RDP TLS/CredSSP with certificate validation
steps.desc: Ensure RDP is configured to require TLS-secured connections with a valid, trusted certificate and that clients are configured to reject invalid certificates, closing the interception path.
steps.outcome: RDP server enforces validated TLS; test on-path interception attempt now fails with a hard client-side rejection.

ITID-43322.def: An RDP client accepts a self-signed, expired, or otherwise invalid TLS certificate presented by an attacker impersonating the legitimate RDP server, enabling the attacker to decrypt and relay the session transparently.
ITID-43322.purpose: Captures RDP man-in-the-middle attacks enabled specifically by weak or bypassed certificate validation on the RDP client, allowing an attacker to present a forged certificate without detection.
scopeIncludes: Client configured to skip or ignore certificate validation warnings for RDP connections
Successful interception where the attacker's forged certificate was accepted without user scrutiny
scopeExcludes: Interception achieved through network-layer positioning alone with no certificate-validation weakness involved (ITID-43321)
Certificate forgery techniques documented generally under Cryptographic Protocol Exploitation (ITID-43631–43634)
ITID-43322.severity: High — bypassed certificate validation is the trust anchor for RDP's encryption; its failure enables full session interception.
ITID-43322.priority: P1 upon confirmed certificate-validation bypass exploited in an active session.
ITID-43322.escalation: Escalate to endpoint/security engineering to enforce strict certificate validation policy and to IR to assess session compromise.
indicators: RDP client logs showing certificate warnings dismissed or suppressed
Client group policy configured to accept any certificate for RDP
Certificate thumbprint mismatch between client cache and the legitimate server's known certificate
vectors: Attacker presents a self-signed certificate to a client configured to bypass validation warnings
Group Policy or registry setting disabling certificate validation prompts for RDP
rootCauses: Organizational policy or user habit of dismissing certificate warnings
RDP clients not configured to enforce and pin server certificates
No centralized certificate management for RDP hosts
mitreTechniques: T1553.004 Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate
controls: Strict RDP certificate validation enforcement (no warning-bypass allowed)
Centralized certificate deployment and pinning for internal RDP hosts
Network Level Authentication (NLA) requirement
ITID-43322.detection: Moderate — client-side certificate-validation-bypass configuration can be audited proactively; active exploitation is harder to see without endpoint telemetry on certificate acceptance events.
ITID-43322.response: Enforce certificate validation policy, reissue/verify the legitimate server certificate, and rotate credentials used during the intercepted session.
metrics: Percentage of endpoints enforcing strict RDP certificate validation
Confirmed certificate-bypass MITM incidents
ITID-43322.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43321 by mechanism: trust/certificate-validation failure rather than network-layer positioning. General certificate forgery techniques are documented separately under ITID-43631–43634.

playbook.name: RDP Certificate Validation Bypass Enabling MITM
playbook.description: Clients configured to ignore or bypass RDP server certificate validation allowed an attacker to interpose a rogue server and capture/manipulate a remote desktop session.

steps.title: Confirm certificate validation was bypassed on affected clients
steps.desc: Review RDP client group policy/registry settings (AuthenticationLevelOverride, certificate warning suppression) and connection logs to confirm clients were accepting untrusted/self-signed certificates without warning.
steps.outcome: Confirmed misconfiguration allowing certificate bypass on specific clients/hosts.

steps.title: Block the rogue RDP endpoint
steps.desc: Block network access to the identified rogue server IP at the firewall and isolate it if internal.
steps.outcome: Rogue endpoint no longer reachable.

steps.title: Enforce mandatory RDP certificate validation via policy
steps.desc: Remove any GPO/registry settings allowing certificate warning suppression and enforce that RDP clients must validate the server certificate against a trusted CA before connecting.
steps.outcome: Certificate validation enforced and verified via a test connection to an untrusted-cert host, which now fails/warns correctly.

steps.title: Validate enforcement and monitor for bypass attempts
steps.desc: Confirm policy enforcement across the fleet and monitor for any renewed attempts to disable certificate validation.
steps.outcome: No policy drift or MITM recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and codify certificate validation as baseline RDP control
steps.desc: Record the incident and formally add mandatory certificate validation to the RDP hardening baseline for all future deployments.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Identify the rogue server and any data exposed during the MITM window
steps.desc: Review network logs/packet captures to identify the rogue RDP endpoint the client connected to and determine what session data (credentials, clipboard, files) may have been exposed.
steps.outcome: Rogue endpoint identified and exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Reset credentials exposed during the MITM session
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation for any account whose credentials may have been captured during the bypassed-validation session.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Deploy trusted internal CA-issued certificates to RDP hosts
steps.desc: Replace self-signed RDP server certificates with certificates issued by the trusted internal CA and distributed via auto-enrollment, removing the incentive for users to bypass warnings.
steps.outcome: All RDP hosts present a trusted, valid certificate.

ITID-43323.def: General or as-yet-unclassified RDP man-in-the-middle activity, used during initial triage before the specific interception mechanism is determined.
ITID-43323.purpose: Intake bucket for RDP man-in-the-middle activity that has not yet been attributed to a specific mechanism (network positioning versus certificate-validation bypass).
scopeIncludes: Suspected RDP interception reported without a confirmed mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any RDP MITM incident once the mechanism is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43321 or ITID-43322 at that point
ITID-43323.severity: High pending triage, given the credential-exposure risk inherent to any successful RDP interception.
ITID-43323.priority: P1 while mechanism is being determined.
ITID-43323.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately in parallel with mechanism triage.
indicators: User-reported certificate warning or unexpected RDP session behavior, mechanism unconfirmed
vectors: Any RDP MITM technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient logging to determine the specific interception mechanism at time of detection
controls: RDP session and certificate-event logging
Incident triage workflow for suspected interception
ITID-43323.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43323.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43321 or ITID-43322; force credential rotation as a precaution.
metrics: Count of general RDP MITM reports pending reclassification
ITID-43323.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43321 or ITID-43322 once the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General RDP Man-in-the-Middle Attack
playbook.description: A generic RDP man-in-the-middle event of unspecified mechanism (ARP spoofing, certificate bypass, or other on-path technique) intercepted a remote desktop session.

steps.title: Confirm the MITM condition and identify the mechanism
steps.desc: Review network path, ARP tables, and RDP certificate validation logs to determine which on-path technique enabled the interception.
steps.outcome: MITM mechanism classified (ARP-based, certificate-bypass, or rogue-gateway) and affected session identified.
steps.abort: If evidence does not support MITM, close as benign.

steps.title: Terminate the affected session and isolate the on-path device
steps.desc: Force-terminate the compromised RDP session and isolate any identified on-path attacking device from the network.
steps.outcome: Interception stopped.

steps.title: Remediate the specific MITM enabling condition
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix based on root cause identified: DAI/DHCP snooping for ARP spoofing, certificate validation enforcement for bypass, or rogue-gateway removal.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified via testing.

steps.title: Restore normal RDP operation and monitor
steps.desc: Return service to normal and monitor for renewed MITM indicators.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document mechanism and refine detection/classification
steps.desc: Record the confirmed MITM mechanism to refine future classification and detection tuning.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed; detection guidance updated.

steps.title: Assess session data exposure
steps.desc: Determine what data (credentials, clipboard content, files transferred) may have been exposed or manipulated during the intercepted session.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Reset any exposed credentials
steps.desc: Reset passwords for accounts whose credentials may have transited the intercepted session.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Audit fleet-wide RDP hardening posture
steps.desc: Confirm DAI/DHCP snooping and RDP certificate validation enforcement extend across all segments and RDP hosts, not just the affected one.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide audit completed with gaps closed.

ITID-43331.def: An adversary scans public IP ranges to discover hosts with RDP (typically TCP/3389) exposed to the internet, then launches a direct, single-source automated password-guessing attack against the discovered host.
ITID-43331.purpose: Captures the common pattern of an internet-exposed RDP port being discovered by scanning and then subjected to a straightforward brute-force attempt from a single source.
scopeIncludes: Mass internet scanning identifying an exposed RDP port followed by brute-force attempts from the same or closely related source
Single-source automated credential-guessing tools targeting a discovered RDP host
scopeExcludes: Brute force distributed across many source IPs/botnet infrastructure (ITID-43332)
Deliberately throttled, low-and-slow attempts designed to evade lockout thresholds (ITID-43333)
ITID-43331.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High if any account shows signs of successful authentication.
ITID-43331.priority: P2 for attempts blocked by existing controls; P1 if any successful logon is observed.
ITID-43331.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately if any successful authentication is detected during the brute-force window.
indicators: High volume of failed RDP logon attempts from a single source IP in a short window
Source IP appearing in known internet-scanning/attack infrastructure lists
Sequential username guessing pattern
vectors: Automated scan-and-attack tooling (e.g. masscan combined with a credential-guessing tool)
Direct exposure of RDP to the internet with no gateway or VPN in front of it
rootCauses: RDP exposed directly to the internet
No rate limiting or geofencing on RDP connection attempts
No account lockout policy compounding the exposure
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
controls: Removal of direct internet exposure (VPN/bastion/gateway required)
Rate limiting and geofencing on RDP-facing infrastructure
Account lockout policy enforcement
ITID-43331.detection: Strong — high-volume single-source failed-logon patterns are among the most reliably detected RDP attack patterns.
ITID-43331.response: Block the source IP, confirm no successful authentication occurred, and remediate the internet exposure.
metrics: Blocked brute-force attempts per quarter
Internet-exposed RDP hosts remaining after remediation sweeps
detections: High-volume single-source failed RDP logon detection
ITID-43331.notes: Differentiated from siblings by being a single-source, undisguised, high-volume attack — the most common and most easily detected RDP brute-force pattern.

playbook.name: Internet-Exposed RDP Port Scanned and Brute-Forced
playbook.description: An internet-facing RDP endpoint was discovered via port scanning and subjected to a sustained single-source brute-force credential attack.

steps.title: Confirm brute-force pattern and source of the attack
steps.desc: Review 4625 failed logon events on the exposed host for a high-volume, single-source (or small set of sources) sequential credential-guessing pattern.
steps.guidance: Correlate with perimeter firewall/IDS logs showing the preceding port scan against 3389.
steps.outcome: Attack source IP(s) and targeted account list identified.

steps.title: Block the attacking source IP(s)
steps.desc: Block the identified source IP(s) at the perimeter firewall immediately.
steps.outcome: Brute-force traffic from the source stops.

steps.title: Remove RDP from direct internet exposure and require VPN/gateway access
steps.desc: Restrict RDP so it is only reachable via VPN or RD Gateway, never directly from the internet, closing the exposure that enabled the scan-and-brute-force chain.
steps.outcome: External scan confirms RDP no longer directly reachable.

steps.title: Validate exposure closure and monitor
steps.desc: Re-scan externally to confirm no exposure remains and monitor authentication logs for further brute-force attempts via the gateway.
steps.outcome: No exposure detected; no unmitigated brute-force activity over 14 days.

steps.title: Document and add to continuous attack-surface monitoring
steps.desc: Record the incident and ensure recurring external attack-surface scanning catches future accidental RDP exposure.
steps.outcome: Continuous monitoring in place; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine whether the brute force succeeded
steps.desc: Check for a successful 4624 logon following the failed-attempt sequence from the same source, indicating a successful compromise.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: If compromised, disable affected accounts and isolate the host
steps.desc: Disable any account confirmed compromised and network-isolate the host pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.
steps.abort: If not compromised, this step may be skipped.

steps.title: Enforce account lockout policy and NLA/MFA
steps.desc: Configure account lockout thresholds and require NLA plus MFA for any remaining RDP access path.
steps.outcome: Lockout/NLA/MFA enforced and verified.

ITID-43332.def: An adversary coordinates password-guessing attempts against an RDP host from a large number of distinct source IP addresses, typically via a botnet, so that no single source generates enough volume to trigger IP-based blocking.
ITID-43332.purpose: Captures RDP brute-force attacks distributed across a botnet or many source IPs, designed to evade simple source-IP-based blocking and rate limiting.
scopeIncludes: Failed RDP logon attempts against a single target correlated across many distinct source IPs in a coordinated pattern
Known botnet infrastructure identified as the source of distributed credential-guessing traffic
scopeExcludes: Single-source brute force from one scanning host (ITID-43331)
Low-and-slow attacks from a small number of sources specifically designed to stay under lockout thresholds (ITID-43333)
ITID-43332.severity: High — distributed attacks are explicitly designed to evade standard IP-based defenses and often indicate a well-resourced or rented attack infrastructure.
ITID-43332.priority: P1 given the evasion sophistication and difficulty of simple blocking.
ITID-43332.escalation: Escalate to network security engineering for coordinated blocking/geofencing response and to IR if any successful authentication is observed.
indicators: Failed RDP logon attempts against the same account(s) from dozens or hundreds of distinct source IPs
Source IPs matching known botnet/C2 infrastructure feeds
Aggregate attempt volume far exceeding what any single source generated
vectors: Botnet-as-a-service credential-guessing campaigns
Compromised IoT/consumer device networks used as distributed attack infrastructure
rootCauses: RDP exposed to the internet with only per-source-IP rate limiting (easily evaded by distribution)
No behavioral/aggregate anomaly detection across source IPs targeting the same account
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
controls: Aggregate/behavioral anomaly detection across source IPs targeting the same account
Threat-intelligence-based blocking of known botnet infrastructure
Removal of direct internet exposure in favor of VPN/bastion access
ITID-43332.detection: Moderate — requires aggregation/correlation across sources rather than simple per-IP thresholds; under-detected in environments lacking a SIEM correlation rule for this pattern.
ITID-43332.response: Block identified botnet infrastructure via threat intelligence feeds, confirm no successful authentication, and escalate exposure remediation.
metrics: Distributed brute-force campaigns identified per quarter
Coverage of aggregate cross-source correlation rules
ITID-43332.notes: Differentiated by distribution: many sources, coordinated, evading per-IP defenses — distinct from the single-source (ITID-43331) and deliberately-throttled (ITID-43333) patterns.

playbook.name: Distributed/Botnet-Driven RDP Brute Force
playbook.description: A large botnet distributed RDP credential-guessing attempts across many source IPs against one or more internet-facing RDP endpoints, evading single-source rate limiting.

steps.title: Identify distributed brute-force pattern across many source IPs
steps.desc: Analyze failed RDP logon events for a high volume of attempts spread across a large, geographically diverse set of source IPs targeting the same account(s), indicating botnet-driven credential stuffing/guessing.
steps.guidance: Use threat-intel IP reputation feeds to confirm sources are known botnet/proxy infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Botnet pattern confirmed with source IP range/ASN characteristics documented.

steps.title: Apply geo/reputation-based blocking at the perimeter
steps.desc: Block or rate-limit traffic from the identified botnet IP ranges/ASNs and enable geo-fencing where business rules allow.
steps.guidance: Single-IP blocking is insufficient against a distributed source; apply reputation/ASN-level blocks.
steps.outcome: Volume of brute-force attempts drops significantly.
steps.tool: Perimeter firewall / WAF with geo/reputation filtering

steps.title: Remove RDP from direct internet exposure
steps.desc: Restrict RDP to VPN/RD Gateway-only access so distributed source IPs can no longer reach the authentication endpoint at all.
steps.outcome: RDP confirmed unreachable directly from the internet.

steps.title: Validate exposure closure and monitor gateway logs
steps.desc: Confirm external unreachability and monitor gateway authentication logs for continued distributed attack attempts.
steps.outcome: No unmitigated brute-force activity over 14 days.

steps.title: Document and tune distributed-attack detection thresholds
steps.desc: Record the botnet characteristics and tune SIEM correlation rules to detect low-volume-per-source, high-aggregate-volume brute-force patterns going forward.
steps.outcome: Detection rule updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine if any distributed attempt succeeded
steps.desc: Cross-reference the failed-attempt flood with any successful logon from any of the botnet source IPs.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: If compromised, disable accounts and isolate affected hosts
steps.desc: Disable any account confirmed compromised and isolate affected hosts.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.
steps.abort: If not compromised, skip.

steps.title: Enforce NLA, MFA, and lockout policy on the gateway
steps.desc: Require Network Level Authentication, MFA, and account lockout thresholds on the RD Gateway/VPN to prevent brute force even from a distributed source.
steps.outcome: Enforced and verified.

ITID-43333.def: An adversary spaces out password-guessing attempts against an RDP account over an extended period, keeping the attempt rate below the account lockout and alerting thresholds, so the campaign can continue for days or weeks without triggering standard defenses.
ITID-43333.purpose: Captures RDP brute-force attempts deliberately throttled to stay under account-lockout and rate-limiting thresholds, trading speed for stealth.
scopeIncludes: Failed RDP logon attempts against the same account spaced at intervals designed to avoid lockout thresholds
Long-duration (multi-day/week) low-volume credential-guessing campaigns
scopeExcludes: High-volume single-source attacks (ITID-43331)
High-volume distributed/botnet attacks (ITID-43332)
ITID-43333.severity: Medium-High — individually quiet but often indicative of a patient, targeted adversary rather than opportunistic scanning.
ITID-43333.priority: P2 during active low-and-slow detection; P1 if any successful authentication is observed.
ITID-43333.escalation: Escalate to IR if the pattern correlates with a targeted campaign against a specific high-value account.
indicators: Failed RDP logon attempts against the same account at regular, sparse intervals over an extended period
Attempt rate consistently just below the configured lockout threshold
Long observation window required to distinguish this from normal user typo-driven failures
vectors: Deliberately scripted low-rate credential-guessing tools
Manual, patient guessing by a targeted adversary
rootCauses: Lockout/alerting thresholds set with no time-window correlation across long periods
No behavioral baselining of an account's normal failed-logon rate
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
controls: Long-window behavioral baselining of failed-logon rates per account
Multi-factor authentication on RDP regardless of password guess success
Adaptive lockout policies accounting for slow-rate patterns
ITID-43333.detection: Weak-Moderate — requires long-window log retention and correlation; frequently missed by tools tuned only for short-window volume spikes.
ITID-43333.response: Extend log retention/correlation windows to confirm the pattern, reset the targeted account's credential, and enforce MFA.
metrics: Low-and-slow brute-force campaigns identified per quarter
Log retention window sufficiency for slow-rate detection
detections: Long-window failed-logon rate baselining and anomaly detection
ITID-43333.notes: Differentiated by tempo: deliberately sub-threshold and long-duration, requiring detection logic distinct from the volume-based approaches used for ITID-43331/43332.

playbook.name: Low-and-Slow RDP Brute Force Evading Lockout Thresholds
playbook.description: An attacker deliberately paced RDP credential-guessing attempts below account lockout thresholds over an extended period to evade detection and lockout controls.

steps.title: Detect low-frequency, long-duration failed logon pattern
steps.desc: Use extended-window SIEM correlation (days to weeks) to identify accounts receiving a small, steady trickle of failed RDP logon attempts from one or more sources, staying just under the lockout threshold.
steps.guidance: Standard short-window brute-force alerting will miss this; require a long-baseline anomaly rule (e.g. failed attempts per account per week above historical norm).
steps.outcome: Targeted account(s) and pacing pattern identified.
steps.abort: If pattern matches a known misconfigured service retrying with a stale credential, close as benign.

steps.title: Block source IP(s) and disable targeted account if compromised
steps.desc: Block the identified source(s) at the perimeter and, if a successful logon occurred, disable the account and terminate any active session immediately.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic stopped and any active compromise contained.

steps.title: Remove RDP from direct internet exposure
steps.desc: Require VPN/RD Gateway for all RDP access so the slow-brute-force channel is eliminated entirely rather than merely rate-limited.
steps.outcome: RDP confirmed unreachable directly from the internet.

steps.title: Restore normal access and extend long-window monitoring
steps.desc: Return systems to normal operation and keep the long-window anomaly detection rule active to catch any resumption of low-and-slow attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 30-day extended monitoring window.

steps.title: Document evasion technique and update detection baselines
steps.desc: Record the low-and-slow evasion technique and ensure SIEM detection content includes long-window baselining, not just short-window volumetric rules.
steps.outcome: Detection content updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine whether the low-and-slow attempt succeeded
steps.desc: Check for any eventual successful logon amid the trickle of failures, which would indicate the attacker found the correct credential.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Isolate any host accessed via the compromised account
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host reached using the slowly-brute-forced credential pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further attacker activity halted.
steps.abort: If no compromise confirmed, skip.

steps.title: Deploy adaptive lockout/throttling and MFA
steps.desc: Implement progressive delay/throttling on repeated failures (not just a hard count-based lockout) and require MFA to make even a low-and-slow guess ineffective.
steps.outcome: Adaptive throttling and MFA enforced and verified.

ITID-43334.def: General or as-yet-unclassified RDP brute-force activity, used during initial triage before the specific pattern is determined.
ITID-43334.purpose: Intake bucket for RDP brute-force activity that has not yet been characterized by source pattern (single-source, distributed, or low-and-slow).
scopeIncludes: Suspected RDP brute force reported without a confirmed source/tempo pattern
scopeExcludes: Any RDP brute-force incident once the pattern is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43331, ITID-43332, or ITID-43333 at that point
ITID-43334.priority: P2 during triage; P1 if any successful authentication is observed.
ITID-43334.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately if any successful authentication is detected during triage.
indicators: Failed RDP logon volume flagged by alerting, pattern not yet characterized
vectors: Any RDP brute-force technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient telemetry to characterize source/tempo pattern at time of detection
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
controls: RDP authentication logging and alerting
Incident triage workflow for brute-force reports
ITID-43334.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43334.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into the specific sibling leaf; block the account/source in the interim if warranted.
metrics: Count of general RDP brute-force reports pending reclassification
ITID-43334.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43331, ITID-43332, or ITID-43333 once the pattern is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General RDP Brute Force
playbook.description: A generic RDP brute-force event of unspecified pattern (single-source, distributed, or low-and-slow) targeting one or more accounts.

steps.title: Confirm brute-force activity and classify its pattern
steps.desc: Review failed RDP logon events to confirm brute-force activity and determine whether it is single-source, distributed, or paced/low-and-slow.
steps.outcome: Pattern classified and source(s)/targeted account(s) identified.
steps.abort: If explained by a legitimate misconfigured client, close as benign.

steps.title: Block attacking source(s) at the perimeter
steps.desc: Block identified source IP(s)/ranges at the firewall.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic stopped.

steps.title: Remove RDP from direct internet exposure and enforce NLA/MFA/lockout
steps.desc: Require VPN/RD Gateway for RDP access and enforce Network Level Authentication, MFA, and account lockout policy.
steps.outcome: Controls enforced and verified.

steps.title: Validate closure and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm exposure is closed and monitor for recurrence.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document pattern and refine classification
steps.desc: Record the confirmed brute-force pattern to refine future classification and detection tuning.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine whether the attack succeeded
steps.desc: Check for a successful logon correlating with the brute-force attempt sequence.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: If compromised, disable account and isolate host
steps.desc: Disable the compromised account and isolate any accessed host.
steps.outcome: Attacker access contained.
steps.abort: If not compromised, skip.

steps.title: Deploy long-window anomaly detection alongside standard lockout controls
steps.desc: Add a long-baseline SIEM correlation rule to catch low-and-slow variants that could evade standard volumetric lockout/brute-force detection.
steps.outcome: Detection rule deployed and validated.

ITID-43411.def: The injection of attacker-controlled script into web content that is subsequently executed in another user's browser, exploiting the HTTP/HTML trust model in which content from a site is executed with that site's privileges.
ITID-43411.purpose: Provides a general, protocol-level definition of Cross-Site Scripting for use at the network-infrastructure/HTTP-protocol altitude, cross-referencing the taxonomy's detailed technique breakdown.
scopeIncludes: General XSS observations at the HTTP/HTTPS protocol-exploitation level before the specific variant (reflected, stored, DOM-based) is determined
Cross-references to the detailed variant-specific documentation
scopeExcludes: The detailed reflected (ITID-32431), stored/persistent (ITID-32432), DOM-based (ITID-32433) variant breakdowns, and the session-token-theft-outcome leaf (ITID-32434), all tracked under the Exploitation domain's Browser Exploits group
The general catch-all XSS leaf already maintained at ITID-32435
ITID-43411.severity: Medium-High, varying by variant and by whether session/credential theft is confirmed.
ITID-43411.priority: P2 initial triage; escalate per the specific variant once classified.
ITID-43411.escalation: Escalate to application security/web engineering for remediation and to IR if session hijacking or credential theft is confirmed.
indicators: Unexpected script execution in a web application context
Web application firewall alerts for script-injection payload patterns
User reports of unexpected pop-ups or redirects on a trusted site
vectors: Unsanitized user input reflected or stored in web page output
Client-side JavaScript improperly handling untrusted data (DOM-based)
rootCauses: Insufficient output encoding/input sanitization in web application code
No Content Security Policy (CSP) deployed
Lack of secure web application development training
controls: Web application firewall (WAF) with XSS signature coverage
Content Security Policy (CSP) enforcement
Secure coding practices with output encoding/input validation
ITID-43411.detection: Moderate-Strong where a WAF and CSP reporting are deployed; weak for DOM-based variants that never traverse the server.
ITID-43411.response: Confirm the variant, patch the vulnerable application code, and assess whether any session tokens or credentials were exposed.
metrics: General XSS detections pending variant classification
Mean time to reclassification and remediation
ITID-43411.notes: This is the general, protocol-exploitation-level definition of XSS. The taxonomy's detailed variant breakdowns (reflected, stored, DOM-based, session-theft outcome, and general) live at ITID-32431 through ITID-32435 under the Exploitation domain's Browser Exploits group — reclassify mature incidents there.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Exploit (HTTP/HTTPS Context)
playbook.description: An attacker injected malicious script into a web application (stored, reflected, or DOM-based, mechanism not yet classified) that executed in victim browsers.

steps.title: Review WAF/application logs for injected script payloads
steps.desc: Search WAF and application access logs for requests containing script tags, event-handler attributes, or encoded payloads (e.g. <script>, onerror=, javascript:) hitting input fields or URL parameters.
steps.guidance: Correlate with WAF XSS rule-set alerts and any user reports of unexpected pop-ups/redirects.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint(s), payload, and affected user sessions identified.
steps.abort: If payload was blocked by WAF with no successful execution, document and close as attempted-only.

steps.title: Remove or neutralize the stored malicious payload
steps.desc: If stored XSS, immediately remove or sanitize the malicious content from the database/CMS to stop further execution against new viewers.
steps.guidance: For reflected/DOM-based XSS, this step may not apply; proceed to WAF blocking instead.
steps.outcome: Malicious payload no longer served to users.
steps.abort: If reflected/DOM-based only, skip and note in the record.

steps.title: Open an AppSec remediation ticket for output encoding/input sanitization
steps.desc: File a developer/AppSec ticket to implement proper contextual output encoding and input validation at the vulnerable endpoint — the actual code fix, not just the compensating WAF control.
steps.guidance: Eradication here means development remediation; track to completion and require a fix verification test (e.g. re-run the payload against a patched build) before closing.
steps.outcome: Code fix deployed and verified via retest showing the payload is neutralized.

steps.title: Revoke sessions/tokens exposed by the XSS payload
steps.desc: Invalidate any session cookies or tokens that may have been exfiltrated via the malicious script and monitor for their reuse.
steps.outcome: Exposed sessions invalidated; no reuse observed.

steps.title: Document and add regression test to CI/CD pipeline
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add an automated regression test/DAST rule to the CI/CD pipeline to prevent reintroduction.
steps.outcome: Regression test added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine XSS type and confirm successful execution
steps.desc: Determine whether the payload was reflected (single-request), stored (persisted and served to other users), or DOM-based (client-side sink), and confirm via browser replay or session recording whether it actually executed.
steps.guidance: Stored XSS requires broader user-impact assessment since it affects all subsequent viewers, not just the original requester.
steps.outcome: XSS type confirmed and blast radius (number of affected users/sessions) established.

steps.title: Deploy a virtual patch via WAF rule
steps.desc: Add or tighten a WAF rule blocking the specific injection pattern on the vulnerable endpoint as an immediate compensating control while the code fix is developed.
steps.outcome: WAF confirmed blocking repeat/variant payloads against the endpoint.

steps.title: Apply a Content-Security-Policy to limit script execution impact
steps.desc: Deploy or tighten a Content-Security-Policy header restricting inline script execution and untrusted script sources as defense-in-depth alongside the code-level fix.
steps.outcome: CSP verified blocking a test inline-script payload.

ITID-43421.def: SQL injection in which the attacker deliberately triggers database error messages that are reflected back in the application's response, using the content of those errors to infer table names, column names, or data values.
ITID-43421.purpose: Captures SQL injection where the application's error messages directly reveal database structure or data, letting the attacker map and extract the schema through crafted errors.
scopeIncludes: Crafting input to trigger verbose SQL error messages reflected in the HTTP response
Iterative error-message-based schema/data extraction
scopeExcludes: Extraction via UNION-based query combination (ITID-43422)
Extraction via true/false boolean inference with no error messages involved (ITID-43423)
Extraction via response-time inference (ITID-43424)
ITID-43421.severity: High — verbose errors typically allow rapid, low-effort data extraction.
ITID-43421.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful data extraction; P2 for detected attempts blocked by a WAF.
ITID-43421.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately; escalate to IR/data-protection teams if sensitive data was confirmed extracted.
indicators: Application returning verbose SQL error messages containing schema details
Web server/application logs showing crafted quote/comment injection payloads triggering errors
WAF alerts for SQL error-message-based injection patterns
vectors: Injecting single quotes or malformed SQL syntax into input fields to trigger verbose errors
Automated tools (e.g. sqlmap) configured for error-based extraction techniques
rootCauses: Verbose database error messages exposed to end users instead of generic error pages
Lack of parameterized queries/prepared statements in application code
No WAF or input validation layer in front of the application
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements enforced in application code
Generic error pages with verbose errors suppressed in production
Web application firewall with SQL injection signature coverage
ITID-43421.detection: Strong — error-based injection patterns are among the most reliably signatured by WAFs and application logs.
ITID-43421.response: Patch the vulnerable query, suppress verbose error output, and assess the scope of data exposed via the error-based extraction.
metrics: Confirmed error-based SQLi incidents per quarter
Percentage of applications with verbose errors suppressed
ITID-43421.notes: Differentiated from sibling SQLi leaves by extraction mechanism: reliance on reflected database error content rather than UNION, boolean, or timing inference.

playbook.name: Error-Based SQL Injection
playbook.description: An attacker exploited a web application endpoint by injecting SQL that triggers verbose database error messages disclosing schema or data.

steps.title: Identify database error disclosure in application responses
steps.desc: Search WAF/application logs and response bodies for SQL syntax fragments, database error strings (e.g. ODBC/JDBC/ORA- error codes), or injected quote/comment characters in request parameters.
steps.guidance: Grep for classic error-based markers like extractvalue(), updatexml(), or CONVERT() error triggers, and correlate with the exact endpoint/parameter.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and injected payload identified.
steps.abort: If the error was a benign application bug with no injectable syntax, close as benign.

steps.title: Deploy a WAF virtual patch blocking the injection pattern
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking the specific error-based injection syntax on the vulnerable endpoint/parameter.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via parameterized queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to replace the vulnerable dynamic SQL with parameterized queries or an ORM, verified by retesting the original payload against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Payload retest confirms the injection point is closed.

steps.title: Assess and remediate downstream data exposure impact
steps.desc: If sensitive data (credentials, PII) was disclosed via the error-based extraction, force credential resets and notify affected data subjects per policy.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per data classification policy.
steps.abort: If no sensitive data confirmed disclosed, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for error-based patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add detection to the SAST/DAST pipeline for verbose-error-disclosure risks going forward.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what schema/data was disclosed via error messages
steps.desc: Reconstruct the sequence of error-triggering requests to determine what table/column names or data values the attacker extracted via error message content.
steps.outcome: Scope of information disclosure documented.

steps.title: Suppress verbose database error output
steps.desc: Configure the application/database to return generic error messages to clients instead of raw database error text, removing the immediate oracle.
steps.outcome: Verbose errors no longer returned to external requests.

steps.title: Apply least-privilege to the application database account
steps.desc: Restrict the application's database account to only the tables/operations it legitimately requires, limiting the damage of any future injection.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed scoped appropriately.

ITID-43422.def: SQL injection exploiting the ability to append a UNION SELECT statement to a vulnerable query, causing the application to display attacker-chosen data (e.g. from other tables) alongside or in place of the legitimate result set.
ITID-43422.purpose: Captures SQL injection where the attacker uses a UNION clause to append the results of an arbitrary query onto a legitimate one, directly returning extracted data in the application's normal output.
scopeIncludes: Crafting a UNION SELECT payload matching the original query's column count/types to extract arbitrary table data
Confirmed data extraction visible directly in the application's rendered output
scopeExcludes: Extraction via reflected error messages (ITID-43421)
Extraction via true/false boolean inference (ITID-43423)
Extraction via response-time inference (ITID-43424)
ITID-43422.severity: High — this technique typically allows direct, bulk extraction of arbitrary database content.
ITID-43422.escalation: Escalate to application security and data-protection teams immediately given the direct data-exposure risk.
indicators: Application output containing unexpected additional columns/rows not matching the legitimate query's data model
Logs showing UNION SELECT payloads with column-count probing sequences (ORDER BY enumeration)
WAF alerts for UNION-based injection patterns
vectors: Automated column-count probing followed by a UNION SELECT payload against a vulnerable parameter
Manual crafting of UNION-based payloads against a known vulnerable endpoint
rootCauses: Lack of parameterized queries/prepared statements
Application directly concatenating user input into SQL query strings
No WAF or input validation layer in front of the application
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements enforced in application code
Least-privilege database accounts limiting UNION-accessible table scope
Web application firewall with UNION-based SQL injection signature coverage
ITID-43422.detection: Strong — column-count probing and UNION SELECT patterns are well signatured by WAFs and application logs.
ITID-43422.response: Patch the vulnerable query, apply least-privilege to the database account used by the application, and assess the full scope of data exposed.
metrics: Confirmed UNION-based SQLi incidents per quarter
Database accounts remediated to least-privilege following an incident
ITID-43422.notes: Differentiated by extraction mechanism: direct UNION-based data return rather than error content, boolean inference, or timing.

playbook.name: Union-Based SQL Injection
playbook.description: An attacker used UNION SELECT statements injected into a vulnerable query to directly extract data from other tables within the application's response.

steps.title: Identify UNION-based injection payloads in request logs
steps.desc: Search WAF/application logs for UNION SELECT, ORDER BY column-count probing, or matching-column-count injection payloads targeting a specific endpoint.
steps.guidance: Look for sequential ORDER BY N requests (column enumeration) followed by a UNION SELECT with matching column count.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and full injected query sequence identified.
steps.abort: If pattern is a false positive from a legitimate reporting query builder, close as benign.

steps.title: Deploy WAF virtual patch blocking UNION-based syntax
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking UNION SELECT and ORDER BY probing patterns on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via parameterized queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to replace the vulnerable dynamic SQL with parameterized queries, verified by retesting the original UNION payload against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms the injection point is closed.

steps.title: Notify affected data subjects and reset exposed credentials
steps.desc: Given union-based extraction directly discloses data, notify affected individuals per breach-notification policy and reset any exposed credentials.
steps.outcome: Notification and credential reset completed per policy.
steps.abort: If no sensitive data confirmed in the extracted dataset, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for UNION-based patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and least-privilege gap, and add detection/regression coverage going forward.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine exactly what data was extracted via the response-diffing technique
steps.desc: Reconstruct the response content returned for each UNION SELECT request to determine which tables/columns/rows were exfiltrated directly into the application response.
steps.guidance: Union-based extraction returns data inline in the page, unlike blind techniques — response bodies from the logged requests should directly reveal what was taken.
steps.outcome: Exact dataset exfiltrated documented for breach-scope determination.

steps.title: Restrict database account privileges used by the application
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege to the application's database service account so even a successful UNION injection cannot read tables outside its intended scope.
steps.outcome: Application DB account confirmed scoped to only required tables/views.

steps.title: Enable database query auditing on sensitive tables
steps.desc: Turn on query-level auditing for tables accessed via the UNION injection to detect any future direct data-extraction attempts quickly.
steps.outcome: Auditing active and generating events on test access.

ITID-43423.def: SQL injection in which the attacker submits conditional (boolean) queries and infers data one bit or character at a time from differences in the application's response (e.g. a different page, a present/absent element) rather than from any directly returned data or error message.
ITID-43423.purpose: Captures SQL injection where the attacker infers database content by observing true/false differences in the application's response, with no error messages or direct data returned.
scopeIncludes: Conditional true/false payload injection with inference from response content differences
Automated boolean-based extraction tooling iterating character-by-character
scopeExcludes: Extraction via reflected error messages (ITID-43421)
Extraction via UNION-based direct data return (ITID-43422)
Inference via response-time differences rather than content differences (ITID-43424)
ITID-43423.severity: High, though typically slower to exploit than error-based or UNION-based techniques, extraction is equally complete given enough time.
ITID-43423.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful extraction; P2 for detected probing attempts.
ITID-43423.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately upon confirmation, particularly given the difficulty of detecting this technique in low volumes.
indicators: Repeated near-identical requests differing only in a conditional payload value
High volume of requests from a single source against the same parameter over an extended period
Response content/length varying systematically with injected conditional logic
vectors: Automated blind SQL injection tooling (e.g. sqlmap boolean-based mode) iterating through characters
Manual conditional payload crafting against a vulnerable parameter with no visible error output
rootCauses: Lack of parameterized queries/prepared statements
Generic error handling that inadvertently still allows behavioral inference through content differences
No rate limiting or anomaly detection on repetitive request patterns
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements enforced in application code
Rate limiting and anomaly detection on repetitive request patterns against the same parameter
Web application firewall with blind SQL injection heuristic coverage
ITID-43423.detection: Moderate — requires volumetric/behavioral analysis rather than simple signature matching, since individual payloads may look benign.
ITID-43423.response: Patch the vulnerable query, rate-limit or block the source, and assess how much data was likely inferred given the request volume observed.
metrics: Confirmed boolean-based SQLi incidents per quarter
Coverage of behavioral/volumetric detection rules for blind injection
ITID-43423.notes: Differentiated by inference mechanism: content-based true/false differences rather than error content, direct UNION data, or timing.

playbook.name: Blind/Boolean-Based SQL Injection
playbook.description: An attacker inferred database content by injecting boolean conditions and observing differences in application response (content/behavior) without direct data output.

steps.title: Identify boolean-based injection probing via response-diffing analysis
steps.desc: Analyze application/WAF logs for pairs of nearly-identical requests differing only in an injected boolean condition (e.g. AND 1=1 vs AND 1=2), with correlated differences in response length/status/content.
steps.guidance: Look for a high volume of sequential requests with incrementing substring/ASCII-value guesses characteristic of automated blind SQLi tools (e.g. sqlmap boolean mode).
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and the automated extraction pattern identified.
steps.abort: If pattern volume is too low to be conclusive, monitor before escalating.

steps.title: Deploy WAF virtual patch blocking boolean-injection patterns
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking common boolean/blind injection syntax and rate-limit/block the high-volume automated request pattern from the source.
steps.outcome: Automated extraction traffic blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via parameterized queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to replace the vulnerable dynamic SQL with parameterized queries, verified by retesting representative boolean payloads against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms response no longer varies with injected boolean conditions.

steps.title: Assess and remediate estimated data exposure impact
steps.desc: Based on the estimated scope, reset credentials or notify data subjects as warranted by the worst-case assumption.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per policy.
steps.abort: If estimated scope is negligible, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for blind-injection patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add automated blind-SQLi detection coverage to the pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Estimate what data was inferred through the boolean responses
steps.desc: Given blind extraction is slow and iterative, estimate the volume/scope of data likely inferred based on the number and pattern of requests observed (e.g. character-by-character extraction of a specific column).
steps.guidance: This is an estimate since blind extraction does not appear directly in response content; assume worst-case scope proportional to request volume.
steps.outcome: Estimated exposure scope documented for risk assessment.

steps.title: Block the attacking source IP
steps.desc: Block the source IP(s) conducting the high-volume blind extraction at the perimeter/WAF.
steps.outcome: Source blocked from further probing.

steps.title: Standardize application error handling to prevent response-diffing signals
steps.desc: Ensure the application returns uniform responses regardless of query result truth value, removing the boolean oracle even if a residual injection path is later found.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms uniform response behavior.

ITID-43424.def: SQL injection in which the attacker injects conditional time-delay functions (e.g. database sleep/wait calls) and infers data based on whether the application's response is delayed, requiring no visible content, error, or state difference in the response itself.
ITID-43424.purpose: Captures SQL injection where the attacker infers database content purely from measured response-time differences, used when no content or error differences are observable at all.
scopeIncludes: Conditional time-delay payload injection with inference from measured response latency
Automated time-based blind extraction tooling
scopeExcludes: Extraction via reflected error messages (ITID-43421)
Extraction via UNION-based direct data return (ITID-43422)
Inference via response-content differences rather than timing (ITID-43423)
ITID-43424.severity: High, though the slowest of the SQLi variants to exploit; still results in complete extraction given sufficient time.
ITID-43424.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful extraction; P2 for detected probing.
ITID-43424.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately upon confirmation.
indicators: Requests containing database sleep/wait/delay function calls in parameters
Anomalously long response times correlated with specific injected payload patterns
Sustained slow, repetitive request patterns against the same endpoint
vectors: Automated time-based blind SQL injection tooling (e.g. sqlmap time-based mode)
Manual injection of database-specific delay functions to confirm and exploit the vulnerability
rootCauses: Lack of parameterized queries/prepared statements
Database account permissions allowing execution of delay/wait functions
No anomaly detection on response-time patterns
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements enforced in application code
Database account least-privilege restricting delay/wait function execution where possible
Response-time anomaly monitoring
ITID-43424.detection: Moderate — requires latency-based anomaly detection, which is less commonly instrumented than content-based WAF signatures.
ITID-43424.response: Patch the vulnerable query, restrict database function execution privileges, and assess likely data exposure given the request volume.
metrics: Confirmed time-based SQLi incidents per quarter
Coverage of response-time anomaly detection rules
ITID-43424.notes: Differentiated by inference mechanism: response-timing measurement rather than content, error, or direct data return.

playbook.name: Time-Based Blind SQL Injection
playbook.description: An attacker inferred database content by injecting time-delay functions (e.g. SLEEP/WAITFOR) and measuring response latency, without relying on visible response differences.

steps.title: Identify time-delay injection patterns via timing analysis
steps.desc: Search application/WAF logs and web server response-time metrics for requests containing SLEEP(), WAITFOR DELAY, BENCHMARK(), or pg_sleep() correlated with abnormally long response times for those specific requests.
steps.guidance: Correlate injected payload strings with the actual measured latency spike in APM/web server timing logs to confirm the delay was attacker-triggered rather than backend load.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and the timing-based extraction pattern confirmed.
steps.abort: If latency spikes correlate with unrelated backend load rather than injected delay functions, close as benign.
steps.tool: APM / web server access logs (with response time)

steps.title: Deploy WAF virtual patch blocking time-delay function payloads
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking SLEEP/WAITFOR/BENCHMARK/pg_sleep injection patterns on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via parameterized queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to replace the vulnerable dynamic SQL with parameterized queries, verified by retesting representative time-delay payloads against the patched build showing no latency correlation.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms injected delay functions no longer affect response time.

steps.title: Assess and remediate estimated data exposure impact
steps.desc: Based on the estimated scope, reset credentials or notify data subjects as warranted.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per policy.
steps.abort: If estimated scope is negligible, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for time-based patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add automated time-based-SQLi detection coverage, including APM latency-correlation alerting, to the pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule and APM alert added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Estimate extraction scope from request volume and duration
steps.desc: Estimate the volume/scope of data likely inferred based on the number of timing-based requests observed, since time-based blind extraction is slow (one bit/character per request).
steps.outcome: Estimated exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Rate-limit or block the attacking source
steps.desc: Block or rate-limit the source IP(s) responsible for the sustained timing-based probing to reduce load and stop extraction.
steps.outcome: Source traffic blocked/limited.

steps.title: Apply query execution timeouts at the database layer
steps.desc: Configure a maximum query execution timeout on the application's database connections so any residual time-delay injection cannot be exploited for extended data extraction.
steps.outcome: Timeout enforced and verified against a test long-running query.

ITID-43425.def: SQL injection in which an attacker submits a payload that is safely handled at the point of initial input but is later incorporated, unsanitized, into a different SQL query elsewhere in the application, causing the injection to execute in a delayed and often harder-to-trace context.
ITID-43425.purpose: Captures SQL injection where the malicious payload is stored by the application and only executed later, in a different query context, rather than reflected immediately in the same request/response cycle.
scopeIncludes: Payloads stored via one application function that trigger injection when processed by a separate downstream function/query
Delayed-execution injection discovered through data-flow analysis rather than immediate request/response testing
scopeExcludes: Immediate, single-request/response SQLi variants (error-based, UNION-based, boolean-based, time-based — ITID-43421–43424)
ITID-43425.severity: High — often harder to detect and remediate because the vulnerable sink is decoupled from the original input point.
ITID-43425.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful exploitation; requires broader code review to fully scope.
ITID-43425.escalation: Escalate to application security for full data-flow review across the affected application, given the likelihood of multiple vulnerable sinks.
indicators: Injection payload found stored in application data (e.g. a user profile field) that later causes anomalous query behavior elsewhere
Delayed error/behavior anomalies with no obvious immediate triggering request
vectors: Submitting a malicious payload via a seemingly safe input field that is later reused unsanitized in an administrative or reporting query
Exploiting inconsistent sanitization between an application's write path and its read/report path
rootCauses: Sanitization applied inconsistently across different code paths handling the same stored data
Lack of parameterized queries at every point data is used in a SQL statement, not just at initial input
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements enforced at every query construction point, not just initial input
Application-wide data-flow security review
Output/query-context-aware sanitization
ITID-43425.detection: Weak-Moderate — requires code-level data-flow analysis or careful correlation between storage and later use; not reliably caught by request/response-based WAF signatures alone.
ITID-43425.response: Trace the full data flow from storage to the vulnerable query, remediate all affected sinks, and assess what stored payloads may still be latent elsewhere in the application.
metrics: Confirmed second-order SQLi incidents per quarter
Applications completing a full data-flow security review
detections: Application data-flow/static analysis for stored-input SQL sinks
ITID-43425.notes: Differentiated from the other SQLi siblings by timing/locality: the injection point and execution point are decoupled, requiring code-level rather than request-level detection.

playbook.name: Second-Order SQL Injection
playbook.description: An attacker stored a malicious payload via one application function that was later executed in an unsanitized SQL query by a different, downstream function.

steps.title: Trace the stored-payload path from input to downstream execution
steps.desc: Review application and database audit logs to trace how a value stored via one endpoint (e.g. a profile field) was later read and used unsafely in a SQL query by a separate function, causing delayed injection execution.
steps.guidance: Second-order injection will not show an obvious malicious payload at the point of the vulnerable query — trace back to the original storage point to find the injected string.
steps.outcome: Both the original storage endpoint and the downstream vulnerable query identified.
steps.abort: If the stored value is a false positive (e.g. legitimate special characters), close as benign.

steps.title: Remove or sanitize the stored malicious payload
steps.desc: Locate and remove/sanitize the malicious value at its original storage location to prevent further downstream execution.
steps.outcome: Malicious stored value neutralized.

steps.title: Remediate both the entry point and the downstream sink
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to parameterize the downstream query AND re-validate/sanitize data at the point of storage — second-order flaws require fixing both the sink and, ideally, the source.
steps.guidance: Retest by re-injecting the original payload through the original entry point and confirming the downstream function no longer executes it unsafely.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms both the storage input and downstream query are safe.

steps.title: Audit other downstream consumers of the same stored data
steps.desc: Check for other application functions that may also unsafely consume the same stored field, since second-order flaws often recur across multiple consumers of shared data.
steps.outcome: All consumers of the affected field audited and confirmed safe or remediated.

steps.title: Document the storage-to-execution chain and add data-flow analysis to SAST
steps.desc: Record the full data-flow chain and ensure SAST tooling includes taint-tracking capable of detecting second-order (stored-then-executed) injection paths.
steps.outcome: SAST configuration updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess impact of the downstream execution
steps.desc: Determine what action the second-order injection performed when executed downstream (data extraction, modification, or privilege abuse).
steps.outcome: Scope of impact from the downstream execution documented.

steps.title: Disable or restrict the downstream vulnerable function temporarily
steps.desc: If feasible, temporarily disable or restrict the downstream function that unsafely executes stored values while a fix is developed.
steps.outcome: Further downstream execution prevented.
steps.abort: If disabling breaks critical business function, apply compensating input re-validation instead.

steps.title: Add input re-validation at every downstream consumption point
steps.desc: Given second-order flaws span multiple functions, add defense-in-depth input re-validation immediately before use in any SQL context, not solely at initial intake.
steps.outcome: Re-validation confirmed present at all identified downstream consumers.

ITID-43426.def: General or as-yet-unclassified SQL injection activity, used during initial triage before the specific extraction technique is determined.
ITID-43426.purpose: Intake bucket for SQL injection activity that has not yet been characterized by extraction technique (error-based, UNION-based, boolean-based, time-based, or second-order).
scopeIncludes: Suspected SQL injection reported or detected without a confirmed technique
scopeExcludes: Any SQL injection incident once the technique is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43421 through ITID-43425 at that point
ITID-43426.severity: High pending triage, given SQL injection's typical data-exposure impact.
ITID-43426.priority: P1 while technique is being determined.
ITID-43426.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately in parallel with technique triage.
indicators: WAF or application alert flagging a generic SQL injection payload pattern, technique unconfirmed
vectors: Any SQL injection technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient logging/detail to determine the specific technique at time of detection
controls: Parameterized queries/prepared statements enforced in application code
Web application firewall with SQL injection signature coverage
ITID-43426.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43426.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into the specific sibling leaf; block the source/parameter in the interim.
metrics: Count of general SQLi reports pending reclassification
detections: Generic SQL injection payload signature detection
ITID-43426.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43421 through ITID-43425 once the technique is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General SQL Injection
playbook.description: A generic SQL injection event of unspecified sub-technique (error-based, union-based, blind, time-based, or second-order) exploiting a vulnerable application query.

steps.title: Identify the injection payload and classify its sub-technique
steps.desc: Review WAF/application logs for SQL injection payload patterns and determine which sub-technique was used (error-based, union-based, boolean-blind, time-based, or second-order) to guide the appropriate identification and remediation approach.
steps.outcome: Sub-technique classified and vulnerable endpoint/parameter identified.
steps.abort: If pattern is a false positive, close as benign.

steps.title: Deploy a WAF virtual patch for the identified pattern
steps.desc: Add or tighten a WAF rule blocking the specific injection syntax observed on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via parameterized queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to replace the vulnerable dynamic SQL with parameterized queries or an ORM, verified by retesting the original payload against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms the injection point is closed.

steps.title: Remediate downstream data exposure impact
steps.desc: Reset credentials or notify affected data subjects as warranted by the confirmed scope of exposure.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per policy.
steps.abort: If no sensitive data confirmed exposed, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST regression coverage
steps.desc: Record the confirmed sub-technique and vulnerable pattern, and add regression test/detection coverage to the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess the scope of data accessed or affected
steps.desc: Determine what data was extracted, modified, or inferred through the injection based on the confirmed sub-technique.
steps.outcome: Scope of impact documented.

steps.title: Restrict database account privileges used by the application
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege to the application's database service account to limit further exploitation impact.
steps.outcome: Application DB account confirmed scoped appropriately.

steps.title: Apply least-privilege to the application database account
steps.desc: Restrict the application's database account to only the tables/operations it legitimately requires, limiting the damage of any future injection regardless of sub-technique.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed scoped appropriately.

ITID-43431.def: Exploitation of insufficient input validation on file-path parameters in an HTTP request, allowing an attacker to traverse outside an application's intended directory (e.g. via ../ sequences) and access arbitrary files on the server's filesystem.
ITID-43431.purpose: Provides a general, protocol-level definition of directory traversal exploitation for use at the HTTP/HTTPS protocol-exploitation altitude, cross-referencing the taxonomy's detailed technique breakdown.
scopeIncludes: General directory traversal/path manipulation observations at the HTTP protocol-exploitation level
Cross-references to the detailed technique-specific documentation
scopeExcludes: The detailed technique, tooling, and impact breakdown, tracked at ITID-32234 (Directory Traversal/Path Manipulation Exploitation) under the Exploitation domain
ITID-43431.severity: High — successful traversal can expose credentials, configuration files, or source code, and in some cases enable code execution.
ITID-43431.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful file access outside the intended directory.
ITID-43431.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately; escalate to IR if exposed files include credentials or other sensitive data.
indicators: Requests containing ../ or encoded traversal sequences in file-path parameters
Web server logs showing access attempts to files outside the web root
WAF alerts for path-traversal payload patterns
vectors: Manipulating a file-path or filename parameter to escape the intended directory
URL-encoding or double-encoding traversal sequences to bypass naive filtering
rootCauses: Lack of input validation/canonicalization on file-path parameters
Application code directly concatenating user input into filesystem paths
Web server running with excessive filesystem permissions
controls: Input validation/canonicalization on all file-path parameters
Least-privilege filesystem permissions for the web server process
Web application firewall with path-traversal signature coverage
ITID-43431.detection: Strong — traversal sequences are well signatured by WAFs and web server logs.
ITID-43431.response: Patch the vulnerable path-handling code, review server logs for successful traversal, and assess what files were accessed.
metrics: Confirmed directory traversal incidents per quarter
Applications remediated for path-canonicalization gaps
ITID-43431.notes: This is the general, protocol-exploitation-level definition. For the detailed technique/tooling breakdown see ITID-32234 (Directory Traversal/Path Manipulation Exploitation) under the Exploitation domain.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Directory Traversal Exploit (HTTP/HTTPS Context)
playbook.description: An attacker manipulated file-path parameters in HTTP requests to access files/directories outside the web application's intended root.

steps.title: Identify path-traversal payloads in web access/WAF logs
steps.desc: Search access and WAF logs for requests containing ../, encoded traversal sequences (%2e%2e%2f), or absolute path references in file-parameter values.
steps.guidance: Check response status codes (200 with unexpected content-length) alongside the payload to distinguish blocked from successful attempts.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and payload identified.
steps.abort: If pattern was blocked with no file disclosure, document as attempted-only.
steps.tool: WAF logs / web server access logs

steps.title: Deploy a WAF virtual patch blocking traversal sequences
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking directory-traversal sequences (encoded and raw) on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via path canonicalization and allow-listing
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to fix the vulnerable file-access code using canonicalized path resolution and an allow-list of permitted files/directories, rejecting any resolved path outside the intended root.
steps.guidance: Retest the original payload against the patched build to confirm traversal is blocked at the application layer, not just the WAF.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms traversal attempts are rejected by the application itself.

steps.title: Restrict file system permissions on the web server process
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege file system ACLs to the web server/application process account so even a residual traversal path cannot reach sensitive files.
steps.outcome: Process account confirmed restricted to only required directories.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST regression coverage
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add automated directory-traversal detection to the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine which files were accessed or disclosed
steps.desc: Review the response content/size for the identified requests to determine what files (configuration files, credentials, source code) were successfully read.
steps.guidance: Pay particular attention to attempts targeting /etc/passwd, web.config, .env, or application source files.
steps.outcome: Scope of file disclosure documented.
steps.tool: Web server logs / file integrity monitoring

steps.title: Rotate any credentials/secrets exposed via disclosed files
steps.desc: If configuration files or secrets were disclosed, immediately rotate the exposed credentials/API keys.
steps.outcome: Exposed secrets invalidated.
steps.abort: If no secrets confirmed disclosed, skip.

steps.title: Sandbox or containerize the file-serving component
steps.desc: Where feasible, run the vulnerable file-serving component in a restricted container/chroot so a residual traversal path cannot reach the broader file system.
steps.outcome: Component confirmed running with restricted file system visibility.
steps.abort: If containerization is not feasible for this application, document as a residual-risk exception.

ITID-43441.def: The exploitation of the HTTP protocol's request/response model to overwhelm a web server or application with a high volume of seemingly legitimate requests, exhausting server resources (connections, threads, compute) rather than saturating network bandwidth.
