ITID-43441.purpose: Provides a general, protocol-level definition of HTTP flooding for use at the network-infrastructure/protocol-exploitation altitude, cross-referencing the taxonomy's availability/DoS-focused documentation.
scopeIncludes: General HTTP flooding observations classified at the protocol-exploitation level
Cross-references to the availability-domain flooding documentation
scopeExcludes: The detailed volumetric HTTP flood impact/mitigation documentation, tracked at ITID-41214 (Unclassified/General HTTP Flood) and ITID-41213 (Cache-Busting HTTP Flood) under the Availability/DoS domain
ITID-43441.severity: High — successful flooding directly impacts service availability for legitimate users.
ITID-43441.priority: P1 upon confirmed service degradation or outage.
ITID-43441.escalation: Escalate to network/infrastructure teams and IR immediately upon confirmed service impact.
indicators: Sharp spike in HTTP request volume from a wide or narrow set of sources
Server resource exhaustion (CPU, connection pool, thread pool) correlated with the request spike
Degraded or unavailable service for legitimate users
vectors: Botnet-driven HTTP GET/POST flooding against a target endpoint
Application-layer flooding targeting a specific resource-intensive endpoint (e.g. search, login)
rootCauses: No rate limiting or web application firewall in front of the service
Insufficient auto-scaling or capacity headroom
No CDN/edge caching absorbing request volume
controls: Rate limiting and web application firewall in front of the service
CDN/edge caching and DDoS scrubbing
Auto-scaling and capacity headroom planning
ITID-43441.detection: Strong — volumetric request spikes and resource exhaustion are reliably surfaced by standard infrastructure monitoring.
ITID-43441.response: Engage DDoS mitigation/scrubbing, rate-limit or block offending sources, and restore service capacity.
metrics: Service uptime during flooding events
Mean time to mitigate an active HTTP flood
ITID-43441.notes: This is the general, protocol-exploitation-level definition of HTTP flooding. The detailed volumetric attack and mitigation documentation lives at ITID-41213/41214 under the Availability/DoS domain — reclassify or dual-tag as appropriate once impact is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General HTTP Flooding Attack (Protocol Exploitation Context)
playbook.description: An attacker generated a high volume of application-layer HTTP requests to exhaust server resources and degrade or deny service.

steps.title: Confirm HTTP flood pattern via web server/WAF metrics
steps.desc: Review web server request-rate and WAF metrics for an abnormal spike in request volume, distinguishing legitimate traffic surge from attack traffic by source diversity, user-agent patterns, and request-path repetition.
steps.guidance: Look for a small set of source IPs/ASNs or a botnet-like diverse source pattern generating repeated GET/POST requests to expensive endpoints (search, login, report generation).
steps.outcome: Attack confirmed with source characteristics and targeted endpoint(s) identified.
steps.abort: If the spike correlates with a legitimate traffic event (marketing campaign, viral link), close as benign.
steps.tool: Web server logs / WAF / CDN analytics

steps.title: Enable rate limiting and challenge-based filtering
steps.desc: Apply rate limiting per source IP/session and enable a CAPTCHA/JS-challenge (e.g. via CDN/WAF) on the targeted endpoint(s) to filter automated traffic.
steps.outcome: Request volume from attacking sources drops significantly.

steps.title: Harden expensive endpoints against resource exhaustion
steps.desc: Work with application owners to add caching, query result limits, or backend protections on the specific endpoints targeted, reducing the resource cost per request so future floods have less impact.
steps.outcome: Targeted endpoints confirmed hardened via load testing.

steps.title: Restore normal service levels and monitor traffic patterns
steps.desc: Confirm service has returned to normal responsiveness and continue monitoring for renewed flooding.
steps.outcome: Normal service levels sustained over a 7-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and update DDoS/flood response runbook and capacity planning
steps.desc: Record the attack characteristics and update rate-limiting thresholds, CDN configuration, and capacity planning to better withstand future floods.
steps.outcome: Runbook updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess service impact and resource exhaustion
steps.desc: Check server CPU/memory/connection-pool metrics and application error rates to quantify the degree of service degradation caused by the flood.
steps.outcome: Impact severity documented (partial degradation vs full outage).

steps.title: Block or geo-fence the identified attack sources
steps.desc: Block the specific source IPs/ranges or apply geo-fencing consistent with business rules to further reduce attack traffic.
steps.outcome: Attack traffic reduced to manageable levels; service responsiveness restored.

steps.title: Establish auto-scaling or burst capacity for targeted endpoints
steps.desc: Configure auto-scaling or reserved burst capacity for the targeted endpoints so a future flood degrades gracefully rather than causing full denial of service.
steps.outcome: Auto-scaling verified via load test.

ITID-43511.def: An adversary registers as a legitimate SIP endpoint/extension by authenticating with a weak, default, or easily guessed credential, causing the PBX/softswitch to route that extension's calls to the attacker's device instead of the legitimate user's.
ITID-43511.purpose: Captures SIP registration hijacking achieved because an extension was protected only by a weak or vendor-default credential, as distinct from the broader hijack outcome.
scopeIncludes: Registration achieved via a default or vendor-supplied extension password never changed post-deployment
Registration achieved via a short/simple extension PIN guessed through limited attempts
scopeExcludes: The specific outcome of inbound calls being redirected once registration is hijacked, tracked as its own leaf (ITID-43512)
SIP flooding/DoS against the registration service, tracked separately under Availability (ITID-41431–41433)
ITID-43511.severity: High — a hijacked registration allows the attacker to receive calls, place outbound calls (toll fraud), and eavesdrop on call setup metadata.
ITID-43511.escalation: Escalate to telephony/IT administration immediately; force credential rotation for the affected extension.
indicators: Multiple simultaneous or conflicting registrations for the same extension
Registration from an unexpected source IP/geographic location
PBX logs showing authentication with a known default credential
vectors: Automated scanning tools identifying SIP endpoints with default credentials
Manual guessing of short, weak extension PINs
rootCauses: Vendor-default SIP credentials never rotated post-deployment
Weak PIN/password policy for extension registration
SIP registrar exposed directly to the internet with no additional authentication layer
controls: Mandatory rotation of default SIP credentials at deployment
Strong PIN/password policy for extension registration
SIP registrar access restricted to trusted networks/VPN
ITID-43511.detection: Moderate — depends on PBX/softswitch registration logging and geolocation anomaly detection being in place.
ITID-43511.response: Force re-registration with a new credential, review call detail records for fraudulent usage during the compromise window, and audit all extensions for default credentials.
metrics: Extensions audited and remediated for default credentials
Confirmed weak-credential registration hijacks per quarter
ITID-43511.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43512 by cause versus outcome: this leaf is the credential weakness that enables hijack, not the call-redirection consequence.

playbook.name: SIP Registration Hijack via Weak/Default Extension Credentials
playbook.description: An attacker registered a rogue SIP endpoint using a weak or default extension password, taking control of a legitimate user's SIP registration.

steps.title: Identify anomalous SIP REGISTER activity in PBX logs
steps.desc: Review PBX/softswitch SIP registration logs for an extension re-registering from an unexpected source IP/User-Agent, or multiple simultaneous registrations for the same extension.
steps.guidance: Correlate with call-detail-record (CDR) anomalies such as calls placed from the extension at unusual hours or to unusual destinations (e.g. international toll numbers).
steps.outcome: Compromised extension and rogue registration source identified.
steps.abort: If new registration matches an approved new device enrollment, close as benign.

steps.title: De-register the rogue endpoint and force re-authentication
steps.desc: Immediately terminate the rogue SIP registration and force the extension to re-register only from the legitimate device.
steps.outcome: Rogue endpoint no longer registered; extension controlled by the legitimate user again.

steps.title: Reset extension credentials to strong, unique values
steps.desc: Reset the SIP extension's password to a strong, non-default value and audit all extensions for default/weak credentials.
steps.outcome: Extension secured; org-wide default-credential audit completed.

steps.title: Restore normal extension operation and monitor CDRs
steps.desc: Confirm the legitimate user has normal extension function and monitor CDRs/registration logs for renewed hijack attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and mandate credential hardening across the VoIP estate
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a policy requiring strong unique credentials and TLS for all SIP extensions org-wide.
steps.outcome: Policy updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess toll fraud or eavesdropping impact
steps.desc: Review CDRs for the affected extension to determine whether the attacker placed unauthorized (toll fraud) calls or intercepted inbound calls intended for the legitimate user.
steps.outcome: Financial and confidentiality impact scoped.

steps.title: Block outbound toll/international calling if fraud detected
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict the affected extension/trunk from placing premium/international calls while investigation continues.
steps.outcome: Further toll fraud prevented.
steps.abort: If no toll fraud detected, skip.

steps.title: Enforce SIP over TLS and restrict registration source IPs
steps.desc: Require SIP TLS for registration/signaling and restrict which source IP ranges (VPN/known office egress) may register extensions.
steps.outcome: TLS and source-IP restriction enforced and verified.

ITID-43512.def: Following a successful SIP registration hijack, the PBX/softswitch routes inbound calls for the compromised extension to the attacker's registered endpoint rather than the legitimate user, enabling call interception, toll fraud, or impersonation of the extension's owner.
ITID-43512.purpose: Captures the specific outcome of a SIP registration hijack in which inbound calls intended for a legitimate extension are redirected to the attacker's device, regardless of how the hijack was achieved.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed redirection of inbound calls to an attacker-controlled endpoint following any registration-hijack mechanism
Impersonation of a hijacked extension's identity in subsequent calls
scopeExcludes: The credential-weakness mechanism that enabled the hijack, tracked separately (ITID-43511)
ITID-43512.severity: High — call redirection enables direct interception of sensitive business communications and impersonation of internal staff.
ITID-43512.escalation: Escalate to telephony/IT administration and IR immediately; notify affected business units if sensitive calls may have been intercepted.
indicators: Legitimate user reporting missed calls or an inability to receive calls on their extension
Call detail records showing calls answered from an unexpected endpoint/IP
Complaints from callers reaching an unexpected or suspicious respondent
vectors: Any successful SIP registration hijack mechanism culminating in call redirection
rootCauses: No monitoring of registration state changes or call-routing anomalies on the PBX/softswitch
Lack of alerting when an extension's registration source changes unexpectedly
controls: Registration-state and call-routing anomaly monitoring on the PBX/softswitch
Alerting on unexpected registration source changes for sensitive extensions
ITID-43512.detection: Moderate — relies on PBX-level anomaly monitoring or user reporting; not reliably caught by network-level tooling alone.
ITID-43512.response: Terminate the attacker's registration, restore legitimate routing, and notify affected parties of potential call interception.
metrics: Confirmed call-redirection incidents per quarter
Mean time to restore legitimate routing after hijack detection
ITID-43512.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43511 by cause versus outcome: this leaf is the call-redirection consequence, regardless of the credential mechanism that enabled it.

playbook.name: SIP Registration Hijack Redirecting Inbound Calls to Attacker Extension
playbook.description: An attacker hijacked a SIP registration to redirect inbound calls intended for a legitimate extension to an attacker-controlled endpoint, enabling eavesdropping or social engineering via impersonation.

steps.title: Confirm inbound call redirection via CDR and registration analysis
steps.desc: Review call-detail records for inbound calls to the affected extension that were answered by an unexpected endpoint/device, and correlate with SIP registration logs showing the hijacked registration.
steps.guidance: Interview the legitimate extension holder for reports of missed calls or callers indicating they reached someone else.
steps.outcome: Confirmed redirection with hijacked extension, attacker endpoint, and affected call volume identified.
steps.abort: If redirection matches an approved call-forwarding configuration, close as benign.

steps.title: De-register the hijacked registration and restore correct routing
steps.desc: Terminate the attacker's SIP registration for the extension and force re-registration from the legitimate device, restoring correct call routing immediately.
steps.outcome: Inbound calls now route to the legitimate device.

steps.title: Reset extension credentials and audit for other hijacked extensions
steps.desc: Reset the compromised extension's credentials to a strong unique value and audit other extensions for similar hijack indicators.
steps.outcome: Extension secured; no other hijacked registrations found.

steps.title: Validate correct call routing and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm inbound calls route correctly and monitor CDR/registration logs for renewed hijack attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and update VoIP incident response and customer trust communications
steps.desc: Record the incident, assess reputational/customer-trust impact, and update the VoIP security baseline and customer communication procedures for similar future events.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed; baseline updated.

steps.title: Assess what information was exposed to the attacker via redirected calls
steps.desc: Determine what sensitive information (customer data, credentials via IVR, business communications) callers may have disclosed to the attacker believing they reached the legitimate extension.
steps.outcome: Confidentiality/social-engineering impact documented.

steps.title: Notify recent callers of the potential impersonation
steps.desc: Where feasible, identify and notify callers who reached the attacker-controlled endpoint during the exposure window, particularly if sensitive information may have been disclosed.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with communications/legal for customer-facing notification.
steps.outcome: Affected callers notified where identifiable.

steps.title: Enforce SIP TLS and registration source restriction
steps.desc: Require SIP TLS for signaling and restrict registration to known-good source IP ranges to prevent future unauthorized registration hijacks.
steps.outcome: TLS and source restriction enforced and verified.

ITID-43513.def: General or as-yet-unclassified SIP registration hijacking activity, used during initial triage before the specific cause or outcome is determined.
ITID-43513.purpose: Intake bucket for SIP registration hijacking activity that has not yet been characterized as either the credential-weakness cause or the call-redirection outcome.
scopeIncludes: Suspected SIP registration hijacking reported without confirmed cause or outcome detail
scopeExcludes: Any SIP registration hijacking incident once the cause (ITID-43511) or outcome (ITID-43512) is confirmed — reclassify at that point
ITID-43513.severity: High pending triage, given the toll-fraud and interception risk.
ITID-43513.priority: P1 while cause/outcome is being determined.
ITID-43513.escalation: Escalate to telephony/IT administration immediately in parallel with triage.
indicators: Anomalous SIP registration activity reported without confirmed detail
vectors: Any SIP registration hijacking technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient PBX/softswitch logging to determine cause or outcome at time of detection
controls: PBX/softswitch registration and call-routing logging
Incident triage workflow for suspected SIP hijacking
ITID-43513.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43513.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43511 or ITID-43512; force credential rotation as a precaution.
metrics: Count of general SIP hijacking reports pending reclassification
ITID-43513.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43511 or ITID-43512 once details are known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General SIP Registration Hijacking
playbook.description: A generic SIP registration hijacking event of unspecified downstream effect (credential-based takeover, inbound-call redirection) affecting an extension.

steps.title: Confirm hijacked registration and determine downstream effect
steps.desc: Review PBX registration logs and CDRs to confirm the hijack and determine whether the effect was toll fraud, call redirection, eavesdropping, or another abuse.
steps.outcome: Hijacked extension and abuse type identified.
steps.abort: If registration change was approved, close as benign.

steps.title: De-register the rogue endpoint
steps.desc: Terminate the unauthorized SIP registration and force re-registration from the legitimate device.
steps.outcome: Extension control restored to the legitimate user.

steps.title: Reset credentials and enforce SIP TLS/source restriction
steps.desc: Reset the extension's credentials to a strong unique value and enforce SIP TLS with registration source IP restriction going forward.
steps.outcome: Controls enforced and verified.

steps.title: Restore normal operation and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm normal extension function and monitor for renewed hijack attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and refine classification for future events
steps.desc: Record the confirmed abuse type to refine future classification and detection tuning.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess impact scope
steps.desc: Determine financial, confidentiality, or reputational impact based on the confirmed abuse type.
steps.outcome: Impact documented.

steps.title: Restrict outbound calling or notify affected parties as warranted
steps.desc: Apply toll-fraud restrictions or notify callers/recipients depending on the confirmed abuse type.
steps.outcome: Further abuse prevented; affected parties informed where applicable.

steps.title: Audit all extensions for weak credentials and registration anomalies
steps.desc: Run an org-wide audit of SIP extension credentials and current registrations to catch any other extensions similarly exposed.
steps.outcome: Audit completed with any additional weak/hijacked extensions remediated.

ITID-43521.def: An adversary positioned on the network path captures unencrypted RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) packets carrying voice media and reconstructs the audio, exploiting the absence of SRTP encryption on the call's media path.
ITID-43521.purpose: Captures direct interception of unencrypted RTP media streams on the network, as distinct from eavesdropping achieved through compromising the PBX/softswitch itself.
scopeIncludes: Packet capture and reconstruction of unencrypted RTP voice traffic on a shared or on-path network segment
Exploitation of a network tap, span port, or ARP-spoofed position to intercept media streams
scopeExcludes: Eavesdropping achieved via compromise of the PBX/softswitch call-recording function (ITID-43522)
ITID-43521.severity: High — direct interception of unencrypted voice traffic exposes the full content of calls, including sensitive business or personal conversations.
ITID-43521.priority: P1 upon confirmed interception capability or evidence of active capture.
ITID-43521.escalation: Escalate to network/telephony engineering to enforce SRTP and to IR to determine what calls may have been intercepted.
indicators: Unexpected span/mirror port configuration on VoIP network segments
ARP anomalies on segments carrying voice traffic
Packet capture tools observed on a network segment carrying RTP traffic
vectors: ARP spoofing to position on-path for RTP interception
Physical or logical access to a network tap/span port on the voice VLAN
rootCauses: RTP media not encrypted with SRTP
Voice traffic not segmented onto a dedicated, access-controlled VLAN
No dynamic ARP inspection on voice network segments
controls: SRTP encryption enforcement for all media streams
Voice VLAN segmentation with access control
Dynamic ARP inspection on voice network segments
ITID-43521.detection: Moderate — network anomaly monitoring (ARP, unexpected span configuration) can surface positioning, but passive interception itself is hard to detect without active network monitoring.
ITID-43521.response: Enforce SRTP across the voice environment, remediate the network positioning vector, and assess the scope/sensitivity of intercepted calls.
metrics: Percentage of voice traffic encrypted with SRTP
Confirmed RTP interception incidents per quarter
detections: ARP anomaly detection on voice VLANs
ITID-43521.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43522 by point of interception: the network media path itself, not the call-recording function of the PBX/softswitch.

playbook.name: RTP Media Stream Interception (Unencrypted Voice Traffic)
playbook.description: An attacker on the network path captured unencrypted RTP voice media streams, allowing reconstruction and eavesdropping of call audio.

steps.title: Detect RTP capture activity via network monitoring
steps.desc: Review network packet capture/IDS logs for evidence of a host performing promiscuous-mode packet capture or ARP spoofing on VoIP VLANs, and for unusual RTP flow patterns to unauthorized destinations.
steps.guidance: Look for a host receiving RTP streams it is not a call party to, or ARP anomalies on the voice VLAN.
steps.outcome: Attacker host/position and affected call flows identified.
steps.abort: If activity matches an approved call-recording/QA monitoring system, close as benign.

steps.title: Isolate the intercepting device from the voice VLAN
steps.desc: Shut down or NAC-quarantine the switch port of the device performing the interception/ARP spoofing on the voice VLAN.
steps.outcome: Interception activity stops.

steps.title: Enforce SRTP (encrypted media) org-wide
steps.desc: Enable and mandate SRTP for all RTP media streams across the PBX/SBC and endpoint fleet so future interception yields only encrypted, unusable traffic.
steps.guidance: Phase rollout starting with the affected VLAN, then extend org-wide; validate endpoint compatibility.
steps.outcome: SRTP enforced and verified via test capture showing encrypted media only.

steps.title: Notify affected call participants and monitor the voice VLAN
steps.desc: Notify participants of exposed calls where warranted by content sensitivity, and monitor the voice VLAN for renewed interception attempts.
steps.outcome: Notifications completed where warranted; no recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.
steps.abort: If no sensitive content confirmed exposed, skip notification.

steps.title: Document and codify SRTP as mandatory baseline for VoIP
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize SRTP and voice-VLAN DAI/DHCP snooping as mandatory baseline controls for all VoIP deployments.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine which calls and participants were exposed
steps.desc: Cross-reference the captured RTP flows with CDRs to determine which specific calls, and therefore which participants and conversation content, were exposed.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposed calls documented.

steps.title: Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection and DHCP snooping on the voice VLAN
steps.desc: Apply DAI/DHCP snooping to the voice VLAN as an immediate compensating control against further on-path positioning while SRTP rollout is planned.
steps.outcome: DAI/DHCP snooping active on the voice VLAN.

steps.title: Segment the voice VLAN from general data traffic
steps.desc: Ensure the voice VLAN is properly segmented from general user data VLANs so future on-path positioning requires a separate compromise, not just general network access.
steps.outcome: Segmentation verified via network topology review.

ITID-43522.def: An adversary who has compromised a PBX, softswitch, or unified communications platform abuses its built-in call-recording, live-monitor, or conferencing features to covertly capture or listen to calls in progress.
ITID-43522.purpose: Captures eavesdropping achieved by compromising the PBX/softswitch's call-recording or monitoring function, rather than intercepting media traffic directly on the network.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized use of a compromised PBX/softswitch's legitimate call-recording or silent-monitor feature
Abuse of administrative access to enable recording on extensions without authorization
scopeExcludes: Direct network-level RTP interception with no PBX compromise involved (ITID-43521)
ITID-43522.severity: Critical — administrative compromise of the PBX enables mass, organization-wide call interception rather than a single session.
ITID-43522.priority: P1 upon confirmed unauthorized use of recording/monitoring features.
ITID-43522.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately as a platform-level compromise; treat as organization-wide until scope is established.
indicators: Unexpected enablement of call recording/monitoring on extensions with no legitimate business justification
Administrative account activity on the PBX outside of normal change-management windows
Unusual storage/egress of recorded call files
vectors: Compromise of PBX/softswitch administrative credentials
Exploitation of a vulnerability in the unified communications management interface
rootCauses: Weak or shared PBX administrative credentials
No multi-factor authentication on the PBX management interface
PBX management interface exposed to a broader network than necessary
controls: Multi-factor authentication on PBX/softswitch administrative access
Change-management auditing for recording/monitoring feature enablement
Network segmentation restricting PBX management interface access
ITID-43522.detection: Moderate — dependent on PBX administrative audit logging being enabled and reviewed; often a blind spot in organizations that treat telephony as outside SOC scope.
ITID-43522.response: Revoke compromised administrative access, disable unauthorized recording configurations, and assess which calls/extensions were affected.
metrics: PBX administrative access reviewed for MFA compliance
Confirmed PBX-compromise eavesdropping incidents per quarter
ITID-43522.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43521 by point of compromise: the PBX/softswitch platform itself rather than the network media path.

playbook.name: VoIP Call Recording via Compromised PBX/Softswitch
playbook.description: An attacker gained administrative access to the PBX/softswitch and enabled covert call recording, capturing conversations without authorization.

steps.title: Identify unauthorized administrative changes enabling recording
steps.desc: Review PBX/softswitch admin audit logs for configuration changes enabling call recording features, unauthorized admin logins, or new recording-destination configurations.
steps.guidance: Check for admin logins from unusual source IPs/times and any newly created export/FTP destinations for recorded audio.
steps.outcome: Compromised admin account and unauthorized recording configuration identified.
steps.abort: If recording matches an approved compliance-recording program, close as benign.

steps.title: Disable the unauthorized recording configuration
steps.desc: Immediately disable the malicious recording feature/destination configuration on the PBX.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized recording stops.

steps.title: Rebuild/patch the PBX and rotate all administrative credentials
steps.desc: Apply latest patches to the PBX/softswitch software, rotate all administrative credentials, and verify configuration integrity against a known-good baseline.
steps.outcome: PBX confirmed patched and clean; all admin credentials rotated.

steps.title: Notify affected call participants and legal/compliance
steps.desc: Notify participants of recorded calls and legal/compliance teams given potential wiretapping/privacy regulation implications.
steps.outcome: Notifications completed; legal/compliance engaged.

steps.title: Document and harden PBX administrative access controls
steps.desc: Record the compromise path and formalize MFA and network restriction as mandatory baseline controls for all PBX/softswitch management interfaces.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine scope of calls recorded and exfiltrated
steps.desc: Determine the time window the unauthorized recording was active and whether recorded audio files were exfiltrated to an external destination.
steps.outcome: Scope of recorded/exfiltrated calls documented.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised admin credentials and isolate the PBX management plane
steps.desc: Disable the compromised administrative account and restrict PBX management interface access to a controlled management network.
steps.outcome: Attacker no longer has administrative access.

steps.title: Enforce management-plane MFA and network restriction
steps.desc: Require MFA for PBX administrative access and restrict the management interface to an out-of-band or ACL-restricted network segment going forward.
steps.outcome: MFA and network restriction enforced and verified.

ITID-43523.def: General or as-yet-unclassified VoIP eavesdropping activity, used during initial triage before the specific mechanism is determined.
ITID-43523.purpose: Intake bucket for VoIP eavesdropping activity that has not yet been characterized as network-level RTP interception or PBX/softswitch compromise.
scopeIncludes: Suspected VoIP eavesdropping reported without confirmed mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any VoIP eavesdropping incident once the mechanism is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43521 or ITID-43522 at that point
ITID-43523.severity: High pending triage, given the confidentiality impact of any confirmed call interception.
ITID-43523.priority: P1 while mechanism is being determined.
ITID-43523.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately in parallel with mechanism triage.
indicators: User or business report of a suspected leaked or overheard call, mechanism unconfirmed
vectors: Any VoIP eavesdropping technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient telephony/network logging to determine the specific mechanism at time of detection
controls: Voice network and PBX administrative logging
Incident triage workflow for suspected eavesdropping
ITID-43523.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43523.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43521 or ITID-43522.
metrics: Count of general VoIP eavesdropping reports pending reclassification
ITID-43523.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43521 or ITID-43522 once the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General VoIP Eavesdropping
playbook.description: A generic VoIP eavesdropping event of unspecified mechanism (RTP interception or PBX-based recording) capturing call audio without authorization.

steps.title: Confirm eavesdropping and identify the mechanism
steps.desc: Review network and PBX logs to confirm unauthorized audio capture and determine whether it occurred via network-level RTP interception or PBX/softswitch-based recording.
steps.outcome: Mechanism classified and affected calls/participants identified.
steps.abort: If activity matches an approved recording program, close as benign.

steps.title: Stop the interception/recording mechanism
steps.desc: Isolate the intercepting device (network-based) or disable the unauthorized recording configuration (PBX-based) depending on the confirmed mechanism.
steps.outcome: Eavesdropping stops.
steps.tool: Switch CLI/NAC or PBX admin console

steps.title: Remediate the root cause: enforce SRTP or harden PBX management access
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix based on confirmed mechanism: SRTP enforcement for network interception, or PBX patching/MFA/credential rotation for compromise-based recording.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified.

steps.title: Notify affected participants and monitor
steps.desc: Notify participants where warranted and monitor for renewed eavesdropping activity.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.
steps.abort: If no sensitive content exposed, skip notification.

steps.title: Document mechanism and refine classification/detection
steps.desc: Record the confirmed mechanism to refine future classification and detection tuning.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess scope of exposed conversations
steps.desc: Determine which calls and participants were exposed and the sensitivity of the content.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Revoke any compromised access enabling the eavesdropping
steps.desc: Disable compromised admin credentials or isolate the on-path attacking device as applicable.
steps.outcome: Attacker access removed.

steps.title: Verify SRTP and PBX management hardening are both in place fleet-wide
steps.desc: Since the mechanism could be network-based or PBX-based, confirm both SRTP enforcement and PBX administrative hardening are applied fleet-wide, not just the confirmed vector.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide audit confirms both control families are in place.

ITID-43531.def: An adversary with access to a SIP trunk manipulates the caller identification header fields (e.g. From/P-Asserted-Identity) in outbound call signaling so the displayed caller ID does not match the true originating number.
ITID-43531.purpose: Captures caller ID spoofing performed by directly manipulating SIP header fields on an organization's own or a partner's SIP trunk, as distinct from use of a commercial spoofing service.
scopeIncludes: Direct manipulation of SIP header fields on a trunk the attacker controls or has compromised access to
Abuse of a misconfigured trunk that does not validate/restrict the asserted caller ID
scopeExcludes: Use of a third-party commercial caller ID spoofing app/service with no direct trunk access (ITID-43532)
Spoofing specifically used to impersonate an internal extension to bypass trust-based call screening (ITID-43533)
ITID-43531.severity: Medium-High — depends on the intent of the spoofed calls (fraud, social engineering, harassment).
ITID-43531.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if spoofed calls are used in an active social-engineering or fraud campaign against the organization.
ITID-43531.escalation: Escalate to telephony/IT administration to restrict trunk header manipulation and to IR if spoofed calls are part of a fraud or phishing campaign.
indicators: Outbound SIP signaling showing a From/P-Asserted-Identity header inconsistent with the trunk's assigned number range
Carrier or STIR/SHAKEN attestation failures on outbound calls
vectors: Compromise of trunk credentials to inject arbitrary caller ID values
Misconfigured trunk allowing unrestricted header manipulation by any authenticated device
rootCauses: Trunk configuration not restricting caller ID to the organization's assigned number range
No STIR/SHAKEN attestation enforcement
Weak trunk authentication credentials
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Trunk-level caller ID restriction to assigned number ranges
STIR/SHAKEN attestation enforcement
Strong trunk authentication credential management
ITID-43531.detection: Moderate — carrier-side attestation failure reporting provides some signal; internal detection depends on trunk-level header validation logging.
ITID-43531.response: Restrict trunk header manipulation, rotate trunk credentials if compromise is suspected, and notify affected recipients if spoofed calls targeted them.
metrics: Trunks enforcing caller ID range restriction
Confirmed trunk-level spoofing incidents per quarter
ITID-43531.notes: Caller ID spoofing has no clean ATT&CK Enterprise mapping — this is fundamentally a telephony-signaling/fraud technique rather than an IT-network technique, so mapped MITRE fields are intentionally left empty. Differentiated from siblings by mechanism: direct SIP trunk header manipulation.

playbook.name: Caller ID Spoofing via SIP Trunk Header Manipulation
playbook.description: An attacker manipulated SIP header fields (From/P-Asserted-Identity) on an interconnected trunk to present a falsified caller ID to called parties.

steps.title: Identify SIP header manipulation in trunk signaling logs
steps.desc: Review SBC/trunk signaling logs for mismatches between the authenticated originating trunk identity and the presented From/P-Asserted-Identity header value, or attestation-level (STIR/SHAKEN) verification failures.
steps.guidance: Check for calls failing STIR/SHAKEN attestation or originating from a trunk not authorized to present the claimed number.
steps.outcome: Spoofed call(s), source trunk, and falsified caller ID identified.
steps.abort: If discrepancy is due to legitimate call-forwarding/diversion configuration, close as benign.
steps.tool: SBC/trunk signaling logs, STIR/SHAKEN verification logs

steps.title: Block the abusing trunk/source from placing further calls
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the offending SIP trunk or upstream carrier interconnect responsible for the spoofed header manipulation.
steps.outcome: Further spoofed calls from the source blocked.

steps.title: Enforce STIR/SHAKEN attestation and trunk identity validation
steps.desc: Configure the SBC to enforce STIR/SHAKEN call attestation and reject or flag calls where the presented caller ID does not match the authenticated trunk identity.
steps.outcome: Attestation enforcement verified via test call showing rejection/flagging of a spoofed header.

steps.title: Restore normal trunk operation and monitor attestation failures
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate call traffic flows normally and monitor STIR/SHAKEN attestation failure rates for renewed spoofing attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and formalize trunk hardening requirements
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize STIR/SHAKEN attestation enforcement as a mandatory requirement for all interconnected SIP trunks.
steps.outcome: Policy updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess downstream impact and abuse pattern
steps.desc: Determine whether the spoofed calls were used for social engineering, fraud, or harassment against internal or external call recipients.
steps.outcome: Abuse pattern and impacted recipients documented.

steps.title: Alert affected call recipients if fraud/social engineering suspected
steps.desc: Notify internal recipients or affected external parties who received spoofed calls, particularly where financial or credential fraud was attempted.
steps.outcome: Recipients alerted and advised not to act on the spoofed call's requests.

steps.title: Coordinate with upstream carrier on trunk hardening
steps.desc: Engage the upstream carrier/trunk provider to confirm their own header-validation controls and, if the compromise originated on their side, request remediation.
steps.outcome: Carrier confirms hardening or remediation of the compromised interconnect.

ITID-43532.def: An adversary uses a readily available commercial or free caller ID spoofing service/app to place calls displaying a false caller ID, requiring no access to the target organization's own telephony infrastructure.
ITID-43532.purpose: Captures caller ID spoofing performed using a commercial spoofing application or website, with no direct compromise of organizational SIP infrastructure required.
scopeIncludes: Calls received by the organization where the caller used a known commercial spoofing service
Vishing/social-engineering campaigns using a spoofing app to impersonate a trusted number (e.g. a bank, executive, or vendor)
scopeExcludes: Spoofing via direct manipulation of the organization's own SIP trunk (ITID-43531)
Spoofing specifically impersonating an internal extension to bypass trust-based screening (ITID-43533)
ITID-43532.severity: Medium, escalating to High when used as part of a targeted vishing or business email/voice compromise campaign.
ITID-43532.priority: P2 for isolated reports; P1 if correlated with an active social-engineering campaign against staff.
ITID-43532.escalation: Escalate to security awareness/IR if spoofed calls are part of a coordinated fraud or social-engineering attempt.
indicators: User reports of a call displaying a trusted number that, on callback, does not reach the claimed party
Carrier attestation failure (STIR/SHAKEN) on an inbound call despite a familiar displayed number
vectors: Commercial/consumer caller ID spoofing apps or websites used to impersonate a trusted number for vishing
rootCauses: No inbound call attestation validation at the organization's telephony edge
Staff not trained to independently verify caller identity for sensitive requests
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Inbound STIR/SHAKEN attestation checking where carrier-supported
Staff security-awareness training on independent caller verification
Callback-to-known-number verification procedures for sensitive requests
ITID-43532.detection: Weak — largely reliant on user reporting and carrier attestation signaling, since the spoofing occurs entirely outside the organization's infrastructure.
ITID-43532.response: Advise the reporting user, document the spoofed number and claimed identity, and issue a security-awareness alert if part of a broader campaign.
metrics: Reported commercial-spoofing vishing attempts per quarter
Staff completion of caller-verification awareness training
ITID-43532.notes: No clean ATT&CK Enterprise mapping exists for commercial caller ID spoofing services — this is a telephony-fraud/social-engineering technique outside ATT&CK's network-intrusion scope, so mapped MITRE fields are intentionally left empty.

playbook.name: Caller ID Spoofing Service (Commercial Spoofing App/Website)
playbook.description: An attacker used a commercial caller-ID spoofing app/service to place calls into the organization appearing to originate from a trusted number.

steps.title: Correlate spoofed inbound calls with victim reports
steps.desc: Review PBX/CDR logs and helpdesk/employee reports of suspicious calls claiming to be from a trusted internal or partner number, and check for STIR/SHAKEN attestation-level flags on the inbound trunk.
steps.guidance: Commercial spoofing services typically originate from unattested or low-attestation (gateway) trunks; check the attestation level field on inbound CDRs.
steps.outcome: Spoofed call(s), presented number, and targeted employees/departments identified.
steps.abort: If number match is coincidental and no social-engineering attempt occurred, close as benign.

steps.title: Alert staff and block further calls matching the pattern
steps.desc: Issue an internal advisory warning staff about the spoofed-number social engineering attempt and configure the PBX/SBC to flag or block low-attestation calls presenting the spoofed number.
steps.outcome: Staff alerted; further spoofed calls flagged or blocked.

steps.title: Enforce STIR/SHAKEN attestation checking and low-attestation call flagging
steps.desc: Configure inbound trunk handling to display a warning/flag on the phone display for calls with low or no attestation, and reject or route to voicemail low-attestation calls presenting internal numbers.
steps.outcome: Attestation-based flagging verified via test call.

steps.title: Conduct targeted security awareness refresher
steps.desc: Deliver a targeted awareness refresher to affected staff/department on caller-ID spoofing and verification procedures for sensitive requests.
steps.outcome: Awareness training delivered; no further successful social engineering observed.

steps.title: Document and update call-verification procedures for sensitive requests
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a callback-verification procedure for any sensitive request (financial, credential) received by phone, regardless of displayed caller ID.
steps.outcome: Procedure updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess social engineering/fraud objective of the calls
steps.desc: Interview call recipients to determine what the attacker attempted to elicit (credentials, wire transfer authorization, sensitive data) while impersonating the trusted number.
steps.outcome: Attack objective and any successful compromise or data disclosure documented.

steps.title: Contain any resulting compromise (credentials/fraud)
steps.desc: If the social engineering succeeded, reset any disclosed credentials and place a hold on any fraudulent transaction requested during the call.
steps.outcome: Any resulting compromise contained.
steps.abort: If no successful social engineering occurred, skip.

steps.title: Report the abusing spoofing service/number to carrier and regulatory channels
steps.desc: Report the commercial spoofing service and abused number pattern to the upstream carrier and, where applicable, telecom regulatory reporting channels (e.g. FCC/Ofcom robocall reporting) to support broader takedown efforts.
steps.outcome: Report filed with carrier/regulator.

ITID-43533.def: An adversary spoofs the displayed caller ID to match an internal extension or a known colleague's number, exploiting the organizational trust placed in internal-looking caller ID to bypass normal call-screening skepticism and enable social engineering.
ITID-43533.purpose: Captures caller ID spoofing specifically used to impersonate a trusted internal extension, exploiting staff habits of screening calls by displayed identity rather than authenticating the caller.
scopeIncludes: Spoofed calls displaying an internal extension number or a known internal employee's identity
Vishing/pretexting campaigns specifically leveraging internal-number spoofing to gain victim trust
scopeExcludes: General spoofing via commercial services with no internal-impersonation intent (ITID-43532)
Spoofing via direct trunk manipulation with no internal-impersonation intent (ITID-43531)
ITID-43533.severity: High — internal-number spoofing is a highly effective precursor to social-engineering attacks such as help-desk password resets or wire-transfer fraud.
ITID-43533.priority: P1 given its frequent use as a precursor to a higher-impact social-engineering incident.
ITID-43533.escalation: Escalate to security awareness and IR immediately, especially if the target was a help desk, finance, or executive assistant function.
indicators: User reports a call from what appeared to be an internal extension requesting sensitive action (password reset, fund transfer)
Internal extension displayed for a call that did not actually originate from that extension
vectors: Commercial spoofing services or direct trunk manipulation configured to display an internal extension
Reconnaissance of internal extension numbering schemes (often via org charts or prior social engineering) to select a convincing target identity
rootCauses: Help desk and other sensitive functions relying on caller ID alone for identity verification
Predictable/guessable internal extension numbering exposed externally
No out-of-band verification procedure for sensitive requests received by phone
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: Mandatory out-of-band identity verification for sensitive phone-based requests (e.g. password resets)
Staff security-awareness training specifically covering internal-number spoofing
Restriction/obfuscation of internal extension numbering exposed to outside parties
ITID-43533.detection: Weak — this attack occurs largely outside technical telemetry and depends on staff recognizing and reporting the deception.
ITID-43533.response: Reinforce out-of-band verification procedures with the affected function, document the pretext used, and assess whether any sensitive action was taken as a result.
metrics: Reported internal-impersonation vishing attempts per quarter
Sensitive functions with mandatory out-of-band verification in place
ITID-43533.notes: No clean ATT&CK Enterprise mapping exists — this is a telephony-fraud/social-engineering technique. Differentiated from siblings by target of impersonation: internal identity specifically, to exploit trust-based screening.

playbook.name: Caller ID Spoofing to Impersonate Internal Extension (Bypassing Trust-Based Screening)
playbook.description: An attacker spoofed the caller ID of a trusted internal extension to bypass call-screening trust and social-engineer an employee.

steps.title: Confirm internal-extension spoofing via trunk vs internal registration cross-check
steps.desc: Compare the presented internal extension number against the actual SIP registration/trunk origin to confirm the call did not genuinely originate from that internal extension.
steps.guidance: Internal-extension spoofing typically arrives via an external trunk while presenting an internal number range — cross-reference PBX dial-plan rules that should normally block this.
steps.outcome: Confirmed spoofed internal extension, true external origin, and targeted employee identified.
steps.abort: If call genuinely originated from the internal extension (e.g. call forwarding), close as benign.

steps.title: Contain any resulting compromise from the trust-based bypass
steps.desc: Reset any disclosed credentials or halt any process (approval, transaction, access grant) initiated based on the spoofed call.
steps.outcome: Resulting compromise contained.
steps.abort: If no action was taken by the employee, skip.

steps.title: Audit and harden dial-plan anti-spoofing rules org-wide
steps.desc: Review all SBC/PBX dial-plan configurations org-wide to ensure external-to-internal caller ID spoofing is universally blocked, not just on the affected trunk.
steps.outcome: Org-wide dial-plan audit completed and gaps closed.

steps.title: Brief affected employee and team on the verified control gap and fix
steps.desc: Inform the affected employee and team that the technical control gap has been closed and reinforce verification procedures for trust-based requests.
steps.outcome: Team briefed; no further successful impersonation observed.

steps.title: Document and mandate periodic dial-plan anti-spoofing audits
steps.desc: Record the incident and add anti-spoofing dial-plan validation to periodic PBX/SBC security configuration audits.
steps.outcome: Audit cadence established; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what trust-based action the impersonation elicited
steps.desc: Interview the targeted employee to determine what action they took based on believing the call came from a trusted internal source (e.g. disclosed credentials, bypassed a control, approved a request).
steps.outcome: Impact of the trust-based bypass documented.

steps.title: Block the identified external trunk/source from presenting internal number ranges
steps.desc: Configure the PBX/SBC dial-plan to reject or flag inbound calls from external trunks presenting internal extension number ranges — a control gap that should already exist but evidently failed or was missing.
steps.outcome: Dial-plan rule verified blocking a test call presenting an internal number from an external trunk.

steps.title: Extend anti-spoofing dial-plan rules to all interconnected trunks
steps.desc: Verify every trunk interconnect (not just the one exploited) enforces the internal-number-range anti-spoofing rule.
steps.outcome: All trunks confirmed enforcing the rule.

ITID-43534.def: General or as-yet-unclassified caller ID spoofing activity, used during initial triage before the specific mechanism or intent is determined.
ITID-43534.purpose: Intake bucket for caller ID spoofing activity that has not yet been characterized by mechanism (trunk manipulation, commercial service) or target of impersonation (internal identity).
scopeIncludes: Suspected caller ID spoofing reported without confirmed mechanism or target
scopeExcludes: Any caller ID spoofing incident once the mechanism/target is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43531, ITID-43532, or ITID-43533 at that point
ITID-43534.severity: Medium pending triage; escalate if any sensitive action was taken as a result of the call.
ITID-43534.escalation: Escalate to IR if the spoofed call resulted in any sensitive disclosure or action.
indicators: User report of a suspicious caller ID, mechanism and intent unconfirmed
vectors: Any caller ID spoofing technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient detail available at time of report to determine mechanism or intent
mitreTechniques: T1598.004 Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice
controls: User reporting channel for suspected spoofed calls
ITID-43534.detection: Weak — dependent entirely on user reporting.
ITID-43534.response: Gather additional detail to reclassify into the specific sibling leaf.
metrics: Count of general caller ID spoofing reports pending reclassification
ITID-43534.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; no clean ATT&CK Enterprise mapping exists for caller ID spoofing generally. Reclassify into ITID-43531, ITID-43532, or ITID-43533 once details are known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Caller ID Spoofing
playbook.description: A generic caller-ID spoofing event of unspecified mechanism (SIP header manipulation, commercial spoofing service, or internal-extension impersonation) used to deceive a call recipient.

steps.title: Confirm spoofing and classify the mechanism
steps.desc: Review CDR, SBC signaling, and attestation logs to confirm the caller ID was spoofed and determine the mechanism (trunk header manipulation, commercial spoofing service, or internal-extension impersonation).
steps.outcome: Mechanism classified and targeted recipient(s) identified.
steps.abort: If number match is coincidental, close as benign.

steps.title: Alert affected recipients and block further spoofed calls
steps.desc: Notify targeted staff and apply the appropriate trunk/dial-plan block based on the confirmed mechanism.
steps.outcome: Further spoofed calls blocked or flagged.

steps.title: Remediate the root technical gap enabling spoofing
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix based on the confirmed mechanism: attestation enforcement, dial-plan anti-spoofing rules, or trunk hardening.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified.

steps.title: Brief affected staff and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Brief affected staff on the incident and monitor CDR/attestation logs for renewed spoofing attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document mechanism and refine classification/detection
steps.desc: Record the confirmed mechanism to refine future classification and detection tuning.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess the objective and impact of the spoofed call
steps.desc: Determine what the attacker attempted to achieve and whether the attempt succeeded.
steps.outcome: Impact documented.

steps.title: Contain any resulting compromise
steps.desc: Reset credentials or halt processes initiated based on the spoofed call, if applicable.
steps.outcome: Resulting compromise contained.
steps.abort: If no compromise occurred, skip.

steps.title: Verify STIR/SHAKEN attestation is enforced across all trunks
steps.desc: Confirm attestation enforcement and dial-plan anti-spoofing rules are applied consistently across all SIP trunks regardless of the specific mechanism confirmed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide trunk audit confirms consistent enforcement.

ITID-43611.def: An adversary interferes with the TLS handshake to force a client and server that both still support SSL 3.0 to negotiate down to that protocol version, then exploits SSL 3.0's CBC padding weakness (the POODLE attack) to decrypt portions of the protected traffic.
ITID-43611.purpose: Captures the specific, historically significant downgrade attack that forces a TLS connection to fall back to the fatally weak SSL 3.0 protocol, exploitable via the padding-oracle-based POODLE technique.
scopeIncludes: Forced protocol downgrade from TLS to SSL 3.0 during handshake negotiation
Exploitation of the POODLE padding weakness following a successful downgrade
scopeExcludes: Downgrade to weak export-grade cipher suites rather than protocol version (ITID-43612)
Padding oracle exploitation against a still-supported legacy TLS cipher suite, not SSL 3.0 specifically (ITID-43622)
ITID-43611.severity: High where SSL 3.0 remains enabled — this is a well-understood, reliably exploitable attack class.
ITID-43611.priority: P1 upon confirmed active exploitation; P2 as a standalone finding of SSL 3.0 still being enabled.
ITID-43611.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure/application teams to disable SSL 3.0 immediately; escalate to IR if active exploitation against production traffic is confirmed.
indicators: TLS handshake logs showing negotiation down to SSL 3.0
Vulnerability scan findings confirming SSL 3.0 remains enabled on a service
Anomalous repeated connection attempts consistent with the padding-oracle byte-by-byte decryption pattern
vectors: On-path interference with the TLS handshake to strip supported-protocol options and force SSL 3.0 negotiation
Exploitation of legacy systems/clients still permitting SSL 3.0 fallback
rootCauses: SSL 3.0 left enabled for legacy client compatibility
No enforcement of a minimum TLS version at the server or load balancer
Client software not updated to disable SSL 3.0 fallback
controls: Complete disablement of SSL 3.0 on all servers and load balancers
Minimum TLS version enforcement (TLS 1.2 or higher)
Client software updates removing legacy SSL 3.0 fallback support
ITID-43611.detection: Strong — protocol version negotiation is directly observable in TLS handshake logs and vulnerability scans.
ITID-43611.response: Disable SSL 3.0 immediately across all affected services, confirm no legacy dependency requires it, and assess any traffic that may have been decrypted during active exploitation.
metrics: Services confirmed with SSL 3.0 disabled
Confirmed POODLE exploitation incidents per quarter
ITID-43611.notes: Cross-references the broader TLS exploit documentation at ITID-32531 (TLS Downgrade Attack Exploitation) and ITID-32535 (general TLS/SSL exploit) under the Exploitation domain; this leaf is scoped specifically to the SSL 3.0/POODLE downgrade class.

playbook.name: POODLE-Style SSL 3.0 Downgrade Attack
playbook.description: An attacker forced a TLS connection to downgrade to SSL 3.0, then exploited its CBC padding weakness (POODLE) to decrypt sensitive session data.

steps.title: Identify SSL 3.0 negotiation and downgrade indicators in server/TLS logs
steps.desc: Review TLS termination point (load balancer/web server) logs for connections negotiated at SSL 3.0, and check for a preceding pattern of repeated handshake failures at higher TLS versions from the same client, indicating a forced downgrade attempt.
steps.guidance: Correlate with IDS signatures for POODLE-pattern padding-oracle probing (repeated CBC block manipulation requests).
steps.outcome: Affected connection(s), client, and confirmation of SSL 3.0 usage identified.
steps.abort: If SSL 3.0 negotiation was from a known legacy client with no exploitation pattern, treat as configuration risk rather than active attack.

steps.title: Disable SSL 3.0 on the affected TLS endpoint immediately
steps.desc: Remove SSL 3.0 (and ideally TLS 1.0/1.1) from the supported protocol list on the load balancer/web server to immediately stop further downgrade exploitation.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed rejecting SSL 3.0 handshake attempts.
steps.tool: Load balancer / web server TLS configuration

steps.title: Disable legacy protocol/cipher support org-wide
steps.desc: Audit all TLS termination points org-wide to ensure SSL 3.0 and other legacy protocols/ciphers are disabled, not just on the affected endpoint.
steps.outcome: Org-wide scan confirms no endpoints support SSL 3.0.

steps.title: Validate TLS configuration and monitor for downgrade attempts
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate clients connect successfully at TLS 1.2+ and monitor for renewed downgrade negotiation attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window; no legitimate client connectivity broken.

steps.title: Document and codify minimum TLS version as baseline standard
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a minimum-TLS-version standard (TLS 1.2+) with periodic scanning to prevent legacy protocol regression.
steps.outcome: Standard updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what session data may have been decrypted
steps.desc: Determine what session cookies, credentials, or data were transmitted over the downgraded connection during the suspected exploitation window.
steps.outcome: Scope of potential data exposure documented.

steps.title: Revoke sessions/credentials potentially exposed during the downgrade window
steps.desc: Invalidate session cookies and force credential reset for accounts active on the affected connection during the exploitation window.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed sessions/credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Enable HSTS to prevent future protocol downgrade attempts
steps.desc: Deploy HTTP Strict Transport Security with a long max-age on the affected domain so browsers refuse to negotiate any downgraded connection in the future.
steps.outcome: HSTS header verified present and enforced on subsequent requests.

ITID-43612.def: An adversary interferes with the TLS/SSL handshake to force negotiation down to a legacy export-grade RSA or Diffie-Hellman cipher suite (historically weakened to comply with 1990s-era export control regulations), then breaks the resulting weak key within a practical timeframe to decrypt the session.
ITID-43612.purpose: Captures downgrade attacks that force negotiation to deliberately weakened export-grade cipher suites, exploitable via techniques such as FREAK and Logjam.
scopeIncludes: Forced downgrade to export-grade RSA cipher suites (FREAK-class attacks)
Forced downgrade to weak, commonly-shared Diffie-Hellman parameters (Logjam-class attacks)
scopeExcludes: Downgrade to an entire weak protocol version such as SSL 3.0 (ITID-43611)
Padding oracle attacks exploiting CBC mode weaknesses rather than weak key exchange (ITID-43621/43622)
ITID-43612.severity: High where export-grade cipher suites remain supported — these attacks are well-documented and practically exploitable with modest computing resources.
ITID-43612.priority: P1 upon confirmed active exploitation; P2 as a standalone finding of export-grade cipher support.
ITID-43612.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure teams to remove export-grade cipher support immediately; escalate to IR if active exploitation is confirmed.
indicators: TLS handshake logs showing negotiation to an export-grade or weak DH cipher suite
Vulnerability scan findings confirming export-grade cipher or weak DH parameter support
vectors: On-path interference with cipher-suite negotiation to force a weak export-grade selection
Exploitation of servers sharing common, pre-computable weak Diffie-Hellman parameters
rootCauses: Legacy export-grade cipher suites left enabled for compatibility
Reuse of common, non-unique Diffie-Hellman parameters across many servers
No minimum key-strength enforcement in TLS configuration
controls: Removal of all export-grade cipher suite support
Use of unique, sufficiently large Diffie-Hellman parameters (2048-bit or higher, or ECDHE)
Regular TLS configuration audits against current cryptographic best practice
ITID-43612.detection: Strong — cipher suite negotiation is directly observable in TLS handshake logs and standard vulnerability scanning tools.
ITID-43612.response: Remove export-grade and weak-DH cipher support immediately, regenerate unique DH parameters, and assess any traffic decrypted during active exploitation.
metrics: Services confirmed with export-grade ciphers disabled
Confirmed FREAK/Logjam-class exploitation incidents per quarter
ITID-43612.notes: Cross-references the broader TLS exploit documentation at ITID-32531 and ITID-32535 under the Exploitation domain; this leaf is scoped specifically to the export-grade/weak-key-exchange downgrade class.

playbook.name: FREAK/Logjam-Style Export-Grade Cipher Downgrade Attack
playbook.description: An attacker forced a TLS connection to negotiate a deliberately weak export-grade RSA or Diffie-Hellman cipher, enabling brute-force key recovery and decryption.

steps.title: Identify export-grade cipher negotiation in TLS logs
steps.desc: Review TLS termination logs for connections negotiated using export-grade RSA (512-bit) or DHE_EXPORT cipher suites, which should not normally be offered or accepted.
steps.guidance: Cross-check the server's supported cipher list configuration against the negotiated suite to confirm the server itself still offers export-grade ciphers.
steps.outcome: Affected connection(s) and confirmation of export-grade cipher usage identified.
steps.abort: If no export-grade negotiation occurred and this was a scan-only probe with no successful downgrade, document as attempted-only.

steps.title: Remove export-grade and weak cipher suites from the TLS endpoint immediately
steps.desc: Update the TLS configuration on the affected load balancer/web server to remove all export-grade RSA/DHE cipher suites.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed no longer offering export-grade ciphers.
steps.tool: Load balancer / web server TLS configuration

steps.title: Disable legacy/export cipher support org-wide and enforce strong DH parameters
steps.desc: Audit all TLS endpoints org-wide to remove export-grade ciphers and ensure Diffie-Hellman parameters use sufficiently strong (2048-bit+) groups to prevent Logjam-style downgrade.
steps.outcome: Org-wide scan confirms no export-grade ciphers or weak DH parameters remain.

steps.title: Validate configuration and monitor for downgrade attempts
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate client connectivity is unaffected and monitor for renewed downgrade negotiation attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and codify cipher suite hardening as baseline standard
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a hardened cipher suite standard with periodic scanning to prevent regression to weak/export ciphers.
steps.outcome: Standard updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess exposure window and potential key recovery risk
steps.desc: Determine the duration export-grade ciphers were exposed and whether captured traffic could be feasibly brute-forced to recover session keys and decrypt captured data.
steps.outcome: Risk of retroactive decryption of captured traffic documented.

steps.title: Rotate TLS private keys if compromise of session keys is plausible
steps.desc: If retroactive decryption risk is significant, rotate the server's TLS private key and certificate to invalidate any long-term key material that could aid decryption of captured historical traffic.
steps.outcome: TLS key/certificate rotated.
steps.abort: If risk assessment concludes negligible retroactive decryption risk, skip.

steps.title: Enable HSTS and disable TLS renegotiation where not required
steps.desc: Deploy HSTS and disable insecure TLS renegotiation on the affected endpoint to further reduce the downgrade attack surface beyond cipher suite removal alone.
steps.outcome: HSTS active; renegotiation disabled and verified.

ITID-43613.def: General or as-yet-unclassified SSL/TLS downgrade attack activity, used during initial triage before the specific downgrade class is determined.
ITID-43613.purpose: Intake bucket for SSL/TLS downgrade attacks that have not yet been characterized as a protocol-version downgrade or a cipher-suite downgrade.
scopeIncludes: Suspected TLS downgrade activity reported without confirmed downgrade class
scopeExcludes: Any downgrade incident once the class is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43611 or ITID-43612 at that point
ITID-43613.severity: High pending triage, given the confidentiality impact of any successful downgrade.
ITID-43613.priority: P1 while class is being determined.
ITID-43613.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure teams immediately in parallel with triage.
indicators: Vulnerability scan or handshake log flagging weak negotiation, class unconfirmed
vectors: Any TLS downgrade technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient detail to determine the specific downgrade class at time of detection
controls: TLS handshake and cipher-suite negotiation logging
ITID-43613.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43613.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43611 or ITID-43612.
metrics: Count of general downgrade reports pending reclassification
ITID-43613.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43611 or ITID-43612 once the downgrade class is known. Cross-references ITID-32531/32535 under the Exploitation domain.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General SSL/TLS Downgrade Attack
playbook.description: A generic SSL/TLS downgrade event of unspecified sub-technique (SSL 3.0/POODLE-style or export-cipher/FREAK-Logjam-style) forcing weaker cryptography onto a connection.

steps.title: Identify the downgrade and classify its sub-technique
steps.desc: Review TLS termination logs to confirm a downgrade occurred and determine whether it targeted the protocol version (e.g. SSL 3.0) or the cipher suite (e.g. export-grade), guiding the specific remediation path.
steps.outcome: Sub-technique classified and affected connection(s) identified.
steps.abort: If no actual downgrade occurred, close as benign.

steps.title: Remove the weak protocol/cipher from the affected TLS endpoint
steps.desc: Update TLS configuration to remove the specific weak protocol version or cipher suite that enabled the downgrade.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed rejecting the weak configuration.
steps.tool: Load balancer / web server TLS configuration

steps.title: Disable legacy protocol/cipher support org-wide
steps.desc: Audit all TLS endpoints org-wide to eliminate legacy protocols and weak cipher suites consistent with current hardening standards.
steps.outcome: Org-wide scan confirms hardened TLS configuration.

steps.title: Validate configuration and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate connectivity is unaffected and monitor for renewed downgrade attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document sub-technique and refine classification/detection
steps.desc: Record the confirmed sub-technique to refine future classification, and ensure the TLS hardening standard covers the identified gap.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed; standard reviewed.

steps.title: Assess data exposure risk from the downgraded connection
steps.desc: Determine what data was transmitted over the weakened connection and the feasibility of an attacker having decrypted it.
steps.outcome: Exposure risk documented.

steps.title: Revoke potentially exposed sessions/credentials
steps.desc: Invalidate sessions and reset credentials for accounts active during the exposure window if data exposure is plausible.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.
steps.abort: If exposure risk is negligible, skip.

steps.title: Enable HSTS on the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Deploy HTTP Strict Transport Security to prevent browsers from ever negotiating a downgraded connection to this domain in the future, regardless of which specific downgrade technique was used.
steps.outcome: HSTS header verified present and enforced.

ITID-43621.def: An adversary exploits a web application's use of CBC-mode block cipher encryption with detectable padding-validation error behavior, submitting crafted ciphertexts and observing error responses to decrypt or forge encrypted application data without knowing the key.
ITID-43621.purpose: Captures padding oracle attacks against a web application's own CBC-mode encryption implementation (e.g. encrypted cookies, viewstate, or tokens), as distinct from exploitation of the TLS protocol itself.
scopeIncludes: Padding oracle exploitation against application-layer encrypted objects (cookies, viewstate, tokens, encrypted parameters)
Forgery of application-encrypted data enabled by a padding oracle
scopeExcludes: Padding oracle exploitation against the TLS transport layer's legacy cipher suite (ITID-43622)
ITID-43621.severity: High — successful exploitation can allow decryption or forgery of session tokens, authentication data, or other sensitive application state.
ITID-43621.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately; escalate to IR if forged tokens were used to gain unauthorized access.
indicators: Distinctive error-response differences correlated with crafted ciphertext padding manipulation
Automated padding-oracle tooling (e.g. PadBuster-class tools) signatures in web logs
Unexpected successful authentication using a forged or decrypted token
vectors: Automated padding-oracle attack tooling targeting an application's CBC-encrypted cookie or parameter
Manual crafting of ciphertext to distinguish valid from invalid padding via application error behavior
rootCauses: Application using CBC-mode encryption without authenticated encryption (no MAC/AEAD)
Distinct error messages/behavior revealing padding-validation state to the client
Custom cryptographic implementation rather than a vetted, standard library
controls: Migration to authenticated encryption (AEAD) for all application-layer encrypted objects
Uniform, generic error responses regardless of padding validity
Use of vetted cryptographic libraries rather than custom implementations
ITID-43621.detection: Moderate — requires WAF or application-log analysis tuned to detect the characteristic high-volume, incrementally-varying ciphertext submission pattern.
ITID-43621.response: Migrate the affected encryption scheme to an authenticated mode, invalidate all potentially forgeable tokens, and assess what data may have been decrypted.
metrics: Applications migrated to authenticated encryption (AEAD)
Confirmed application-layer padding oracle incidents per quarter
ITID-43621.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43622 by layer: this leaf covers application-implemented CBC encryption, not the TLS transport protocol itself. Cross-references the general TLS/SSL exploit documentation at ITID-32535.

playbook.name: CBC Padding Oracle Attack Against Web Application Encryption
playbook.description: An attacker exploited a web application's use of CBC-mode encryption with a detectable padding-validation oracle (e.g. in a ViewState/token) to decrypt or forge encrypted data.

steps.title: Identify padding-oracle probing pattern in application logs
steps.desc: Review application/WAF logs for a high volume of requests with systematically manipulated ciphertext (e.g. modified ViewState, encrypted cookie, or token parameter) and observe differing error responses (padding-valid vs padding-invalid) — the signature of automated padding-oracle tooling (e.g. PadBuster).
steps.guidance: Look for sequential byte-by-byte manipulation of a specific encrypted parameter correlated with distinct error/response-time signatures.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and the oracle-exploitation pattern identified.
steps.abort: If pattern was blocked by WAF with no successful decryption, document as attempted-only.

steps.title: Deploy a WAF virtual patch blocking the oracle-probing pattern
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking the high-volume systematic ciphertext manipulation pattern against the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Further oracle-probing traffic blocked.

steps.title: Remediate by eliminating the padding oracle and using authenticated encryption
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to replace the vulnerable CBC-with-separate-MAC (or unauthenticated CBC) scheme with an authenticated encryption mode (e.g. AES-GCM) and ensure uniform, generic error responses regardless of padding validity.
steps.guidance: Retest the original oracle-exploitation technique against the patched build to confirm no distinguishable error/timing signal remains.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms the oracle no longer distinguishes valid from invalid padding.

steps.title: Force re-authentication and notify affected users if privilege escalation occurred
steps.desc: Require affected users to re-authenticate under the new key/scheme and notify them if the forged token was used to escalate privileges or access unauthorized data.
steps.outcome: Users re-authenticated; notifications completed where warranted.
steps.abort: If no privilege escalation confirmed, skip notification.

steps.title: Document and add cryptographic review to the SDLC
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable cryptographic pattern and add a mandatory cryptographic design review step to the SDLC for any custom encryption implementation.
steps.outcome: SDLC process updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what was decrypted or forged via the oracle
steps.desc: Determine whether the attacker successfully decrypted sensitive data or forged a valid encrypted token (e.g. to escalate privileges or bypass authentication) using the oracle.
steps.outcome: Scope of decryption/forgery impact documented.

steps.title: Invalidate any forged tokens/sessions and rotate the encryption key
steps.desc: Revoke any session/token confirmed forged via the oracle and rotate the underlying encryption key used for the vulnerable data (e.g. machine key for ASP.NET ViewState) to invalidate all existing tokens.
steps.outcome: Forged tokens invalidated; new key in use.

steps.title: Audit other application components for the same unauthenticated-encryption pattern
steps.desc: Search the codebase for other uses of the vulnerable CBC-without-authentication pattern (e.g. other encrypted cookies/tokens) and remediate each instance found.
steps.outcome: Codebase audit completed with all instances remediated or ticketed.
