ITID-43622.def: An adversary exploits a padding-validation timing or error-behavior difference in a server's legacy TLS CBC-mode cipher suite implementation to decrypt portions of protected traffic without knowledge of the session key.
ITID-43622.purpose: Captures padding oracle attacks against the TLS protocol itself via a still-supported legacy CBC-mode cipher suite, distinct from application-layer encryption weaknesses.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a legacy CBC-mode TLS cipher suite's padding-validation weakness (e.g. Lucky 13-class timing attacks)
Exploitation requiring the target to still support vulnerable CBC-mode TLS cipher suites
scopeExcludes: Padding oracle exploitation against application-implemented CBC encryption unrelated to the TLS transport itself (ITID-43621)
Protocol-version downgrade to SSL 3.0 (ITID-43611), which is a distinct though related attack class
ITID-43622.severity: High where vulnerable legacy CBC-mode cipher suites remain enabled.
ITID-43622.priority: P1 upon confirmed active exploitation; P2 as a standalone finding of vulnerable cipher suite support.
ITID-43622.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure teams to remove vulnerable CBC-mode cipher suite support immediately; escalate to IR if active exploitation is confirmed.
indicators: Vulnerability scan findings confirming support for vulnerable legacy CBC-mode TLS cipher suites
Anomalous, high-volume, timing-sensitive connection patterns consistent with a timing-based padding oracle attack
vectors: Automated timing-analysis tooling exploiting a legacy CBC-mode cipher suite's padding validation
rootCauses: Legacy CBC-mode TLS cipher suites left enabled for compatibility
TLS implementation not patched against known timing-attack mitigations
No preference given to AEAD cipher suites (e.g. AES-GCM) in server configuration
controls: Preference for AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305) over legacy CBC-mode suites
Removal of vulnerable legacy CBC-mode cipher suite support
TLS stack patching to current, timing-attack-hardened implementations
ITID-43622.detection: Moderate — vulnerable cipher suite support is easily scanned for; active timing-based exploitation is harder to detect without specialized network timing analysis.
ITID-43622.response: Remove vulnerable cipher suite support, prefer AEAD suites, and assess any traffic decrypted during active exploitation.
metrics: Services confirmed with vulnerable legacy CBC cipher suites disabled
Confirmed TLS padding oracle incidents per quarter
detections: Vulnerable cipher suite support vulnerability scanning
ITID-43622.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43621 by layer: this leaf covers the TLS transport protocol's own CBC-mode cipher suites, not application-implemented encryption. Cross-references ITID-32531/32535 under the Exploitation domain.

playbook.name: Padding Oracle Attack Exploiting Legacy TLS Cipher Suite
playbook.description: An attacker exploited a legacy CBC-mode TLS cipher suite's padding validation timing/error behavior (e.g. Lucky 13-style) to decrypt portions of TLS-protected traffic.

steps.title: Identify legacy CBC TLS cipher suite usage and oracle-probing traffic
steps.desc: Review TLS termination logs for connections negotiated with legacy CBC-mode cipher suites and correlate with an unusually high volume of connection attempts/resets from a single client, consistent with automated padding-oracle timing analysis.
steps.outcome: Affected cipher suite, endpoint, and probing source identified.
steps.abort: If cipher suite usage is legitimate legacy client compatibility with no probing pattern, treat as configuration risk rather than active attack.

steps.title: Disable the vulnerable legacy CBC cipher suite immediately
steps.desc: Remove the affected legacy CBC-mode cipher suite from the TLS endpoint's supported list.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed no longer negotiating the vulnerable cipher suite.
steps.tool: Load balancer / web server TLS configuration

steps.title: Disable all legacy CBC cipher suites org-wide and prefer AEAD ciphers
steps.desc: Audit all TLS endpoints org-wide to remove legacy CBC-mode cipher suites and prioritize AEAD cipher suites (e.g. AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) that are not vulnerable to padding-oracle timing attacks.
steps.outcome: Org-wide scan confirms hardened cipher suite configuration.

steps.title: Validate configuration and monitor connectivity
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate client connectivity is unaffected and monitor for renewed oracle-probing patterns.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and codify AEAD cipher preference as baseline standard
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a cipher suite standard prioritizing AEAD ciphers with periodic scanning to prevent regression to vulnerable CBC suites.
steps.outcome: Standard updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what data may have been exposed via the timing side-channel
steps.desc: Determine the sensitivity of data transmitted over the targeted connection(s) during the suspected exploitation window.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Revoke potentially exposed sessions/credentials
steps.desc: Invalidate sessions and reset credentials for accounts active during the exposure window if data exposure is plausible.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.
steps.abort: If exposure risk is negligible, skip.

steps.title: Enable HSTS on the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Deploy HTTP Strict Transport Security to reduce the chance of any client negotiating a legacy cipher suite in the future.
steps.outcome: HSTS header verified present and enforced.

ITID-43623.def: General or as-yet-unclassified padding oracle exploitation activity, used during initial triage before the specific target layer is determined.
ITID-43623.purpose: Intake bucket for padding oracle exploitation activity that has not yet been characterized as targeting application-layer encryption or the TLS transport protocol itself.
scopeIncludes: Suspected padding oracle exploitation reported without confirmed target layer
scopeExcludes: Any padding oracle incident once the target layer is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43621 or ITID-43622 at that point
ITID-43623.priority: P1 while target layer is being determined.
ITID-43623.escalation: Escalate to application/infrastructure security immediately in parallel with triage.
indicators: WAF or scanner alert flagging padding-oracle-consistent behavior, layer unconfirmed
vectors: Any padding oracle technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient detail to determine the target layer at time of detection
controls: Application and TLS-layer logging sufficient to distinguish target
ITID-43623.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43623.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43621 or ITID-43622.
metrics: Count of general padding oracle reports pending reclassification
ITID-43623.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43621 or ITID-43622 once the target layer is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Padding Oracle Exploit
playbook.description: A generic padding-oracle exploitation event of unspecified target (application-layer CBC encryption or legacy TLS cipher suite) used to decrypt or forge encrypted data.

steps.title: Identify the oracle-probing pattern and classify its target
steps.desc: Review application and TLS logs to confirm a padding-oracle exploitation pattern and determine whether the target was application-layer encryption (e.g. a token/ViewState) or the TLS cipher suite itself.
steps.outcome: Target classified and affected endpoint/connection identified.
steps.abort: If pattern was blocked with no successful exploitation, document as attempted-only.

steps.title: Block the oracle-probing traffic and disable the vulnerable configuration
steps.desc: Deploy a WAF rule or TLS configuration change to block the specific probing pattern based on the confirmed target.
steps.outcome: Further probing blocked.

steps.title: Remediate the root cryptographic weakness
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix based on the confirmed target: authenticated encryption for application-layer tokens, or AEAD cipher suite enforcement for TLS.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified via retest.

steps.title: Validate remediation and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Confirm the fix is effective and monitor for renewed oracle-probing attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document target and refine classification/detection
steps.desc: Record the confirmed target to refine future classification and detection tuning.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what was decrypted or forged
steps.desc: Determine the scope of data decrypted or tokens forged via the oracle.
steps.outcome: Impact scope documented.

steps.title: Invalidate potentially compromised tokens/sessions and rotate keys
steps.desc: Revoke affected sessions/tokens and rotate encryption keys as warranted by the confirmed impact.
steps.outcome: Exposure contained.
steps.abort: If no compromise confirmed, skip.

steps.title: Audit for other instances of unauthenticated-encryption/legacy-cipher patterns
steps.desc: Depending on the confirmed target, search for other application encryption uses or TLS endpoints exhibiting the same weakness and remediate each instance found.
steps.outcome: Audit completed with all instances remediated or ticketed.

ITID-43631.def: An adversary who has compromised a Certificate Authority's infrastructure or issuance workflow obtains a fraudulently issued certificate for a domain or identity they do not legitimately control, which is nonetheless trusted by default because it was issued by a trusted CA.
ITID-43631.purpose: Captures certificate forgery achieved through compromise of a Certificate Authority's issuance process, enabling fraudulently issued certificates trusted by default.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent certificates traced to a compromised CA's issuance process for domains this organization owns
Confirmed misissuance events reported via Certificate Transparency logs
scopeExcludes: A self-signed certificate socially engineered into acceptance, with no CA compromise involved (ITID-43632)
A forged certificate created using a stolen private signing key rather than CA process compromise (ITID-43633)
The organization-level CA compromise incident itself, tracked separately (ITID-64312/64313/64314) — this leaf covers the downstream fraudulent-certificate impact
ITID-43631.severity: Critical — a fraudulently issued, CA-trusted certificate can enable undetectable TLS interception or impersonation against any client trusting that CA.
ITID-43631.priority: P1 immediate upon confirmed misissuance for an organization-owned domain.
ITID-43631.escalation: Escalate to IR and the affected CA immediately for revocation; notify browser/OS trust-store maintainers if the scope is broad.
indicators: Certificate Transparency log entries showing an unexpected certificate issued for an organization-owned domain
Unexpected certificate serial number/issuer combination observed in client connections
vectors: Compromise of a CA's issuance system or validation process
Exploitation of a domain-validation weakness allowing fraudulent proof of control
rootCauses: CA-side process or infrastructure weakness (outside the organization's direct control)
No Certificate Transparency monitoring in place for the organization's own domains
No Certificate Authority Authorization (CAA) DNS records restricting which CAs may issue for the domain
controls: Certificate Transparency log monitoring for organization-owned domains
CAA DNS records restricting authorized issuing CAs
Rapid revocation procedures coordinated with the CA upon misissuance discovery
ITID-43631.detection: Moderate-Strong where Certificate Transparency monitoring is actively deployed; weak otherwise, since misissuance may go unnoticed until abused.
ITID-43631.response: Coordinate immediate revocation with the issuing CA, notify affected relying parties where feasible, and implement CAA restrictions to prevent recurrence.
metrics: Organization domains under active Certificate Transparency monitoring
Confirmed CA-compromise misissuance incidents per quarter
detections: Unexpected certificate serial/issuer detection on client connections
ITID-43631.notes: Differentiated from siblings by mechanism: CA-side issuance-process compromise rather than social engineering or stolen key material. Cross-references the CA compromise incident leaves at ITID-64312–64314.

playbook.name: Fraudulently Issued Certificate via Compromised Certificate Authority
playbook.description: A trusted Certificate Authority (internal or public) was compromised and used to issue a fraudulent certificate for one of the organization's domains, enabling impersonation or MITM.

steps.title: Confirm the fraudulent certificate via Certificate Transparency log monitoring
steps.desc: Review Certificate Transparency (CT) log monitoring alerts or manually query CT logs (crt.sh) for unauthorized certificates issued for the organization's domains that were not requested through the approved issuance process.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the certificate's issuing CA, serial number, and validity period against the organization's certificate inventory.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent certificate identified with issuing CA and affected domain confirmed.
steps.abort: If certificate matches an approved but undocumented issuance, close as benign and update inventory.
steps.tool: Certificate Transparency monitoring (crt.sh, CT log search)

steps.title: Request emergency revocation of the fraudulent certificate
steps.desc: Immediately request revocation of the fraudulent certificate from the issuing CA and confirm it is added to the CA's CRL/OCSP responder.
steps.guidance: Escalate directly with the CA's security/abuse team; reference the CT log entry as evidence.
steps.outcome: Certificate revoked and confirmed via OCSP/CRL check.

steps.title: Deploy certificate pinning and CT log monitoring going forward
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen certificate pinning for critical applications/clients and set up continuous automated CT log monitoring for all organizational domains to catch future fraudulent issuance quickly.
steps.outcome: CT monitoring active and alerting verified via a test scenario.
steps.tool: CT monitoring service, certificate pinning configuration

steps.title: Verify legitimate certificate is in use and monitor for further fraudulent issuance
steps.desc: Confirm the organization's legitimate certificate is correctly deployed and monitor CT logs for any further unauthorized issuance attempts.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent issuance observed over a 30-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document the CA compromise incident and update PKI trust policy
steps.desc: Record the full incident including CA coordination outcomes, and update the organization's PKI trust policy (CAA restrictions, pinning, CT monitoring) as a permanent baseline control.
steps.outcome: PKI policy updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine whether the fraudulent certificate was used in an active MITM/impersonation attack
steps.desc: Check network/DNS logs and user reports for evidence the fraudulent certificate was actively deployed (e.g. on a rogue server intercepting traffic to the domain).
steps.outcome: Active exploitation confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Coordinate external CA-incident response
steps.desc: Formally engage the compromised CA's incident response team to understand the scope of the CA compromise (whether other certificates were also fraudulently issued) and track their remediation.
steps.guidance: This is an external coordination step distinct from internal IR — the CA itself must investigate its issuance systems.
steps.outcome: CA incident response engaged and providing scope updates.

steps.title: Evaluate trust in the compromised CA and consider CAA policy restriction
steps.desc: Based on the CA's incident findings, evaluate whether to restrict future certificate issuance to specific trusted CAs via DNS CAA records, reducing the risk of unauthorized issuance from any other CA.
steps.outcome: CAA records updated to restrict issuance to approved CAs.

ITID-43632.def: An adversary presents a self-signed or otherwise non-CA-trusted certificate to a victim and, through social engineering (instructing the user to click through a warning, or via a compromised endpoint's trust-store manipulation), induces acceptance of that certificate as if it were legitimate.
ITID-43632.purpose: Captures certificate forgery where a self-signed or otherwise untrusted certificate is accepted by a victim through social engineering rather than any compromise of CA infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: Victim instructed or tricked into accepting/clicking through a browser or client certificate-warning prompt
A self-signed certificate manually installed into a victim's trust store via social engineering or physical/remote access
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent issuance via CA compromise (ITID-43631)
Forgery using a stolen legitimate private signing key (ITID-43633)
ITID-43632.severity: Medium-High — effective only where the victim's browser/client warns and is bypassed by social engineering, but can enable full TLS interception once accepted.
ITID-43632.priority: P1 upon confirmed acceptance of a rogue certificate on a production endpoint.
ITID-43632.escalation: Escalate to IR and endpoint security immediately; remove the rogue certificate from all affected trust stores.
indicators: Rogue self-signed certificate found installed in a client's trust store with no legitimate business justification
User reports of being instructed to bypass a certificate warning by an unfamiliar or suspicious source
Endpoint security alert on an unexpected root/intermediate certificate installation
vectors: Phishing or vishing pretext instructing the victim to install a certificate or bypass a warning
Malicious software installer bundling a rogue root certificate with social-engineering consent prompts
rootCauses: Staff not trained to recognize and refuse certificate-warning bypass requests
Endpoints permitting unrestricted installation of root/intermediate certificates by standard users
No monitoring of trust-store changes on managed endpoints
mitreTechniques: T1553.004 Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate
controls: Restriction of trust-store modification privileges on managed endpoints
Trust-store change monitoring and alerting
Staff security-awareness training on certificate-warning bypass social engineering
ITID-43632.detection: Moderate — endpoint trust-store monitoring reliably catches this where deployed; otherwise depends on user reporting.
ITID-43632.response: Remove the rogue certificate from all affected endpoints, assess what traffic may have been intercepted, and reinforce awareness training.
metrics: Endpoints with trust-store modification restricted to administrators
Confirmed rogue-certificate acceptance incidents per quarter
ITID-43632.notes: Differentiated from siblings by mechanism: social-engineering-driven acceptance of an untrusted certificate, not CA compromise or stolen key material.

playbook.name: Self-Signed Certificate Presented as Trusted (Social Engineering Acceptance)
playbook.description: An attacker presented a self-signed certificate to users, who were socially engineered into accepting the browser's trust warning, enabling MITM interception.

steps.title: Identify the self-signed certificate acceptance incident
steps.desc: Review endpoint browser/EDR telemetry and user reports for instances where a certificate warning was displayed and clicked through (accepted) for a domain that should present a valid CA-issued certificate.
steps.guidance: Check browser certificate exception stores/logs where available for manually added exceptions.
steps.outcome: Affected user(s), domain, and the rogue self-signed certificate details identified.
steps.abort: If the warning was correctly rejected with no acceptance, close as attempted-only.

steps.title: Remove the accepted certificate exception and block the rogue server
steps.desc: Remove the manually accepted certificate trust exception on the affected browser/endpoint and block network access to the rogue server's IP.
steps.outcome: Endpoint no longer trusts the rogue certificate; rogue server blocked.

steps.title: Deploy centralized certificate-warning enforcement policy
steps.desc: Configure browser management policy (e.g. via GPO/MDM) to prevent users from overriding certificate trust warnings for organizational domains, closing the social-engineering acceptance path.
steps.outcome: Policy verified preventing warning override in a test scenario.

steps.title: Conduct targeted awareness training on certificate warnings
steps.desc: Deliver awareness training to the affected user(s)/team on the danger of overriding browser certificate warnings.
steps.outcome: Training delivered.

steps.title: Document and update browser security baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize certificate-warning override prevention as a mandatory baseline browser management control.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what data was exposed during the accepted MITM session
steps.desc: Determine what credentials or data were transmitted while the user's browser trusted the rogue certificate.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposure documented.

steps.title: Reset credentials exposed during the MITM session
steps.desc: Force password reset and session revocation for accounts whose credentials may have been captured.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Deploy trusted internal CA-issued certificates to eliminate legitimate self-signed usage
steps.desc: Replace any remaining legitimate self-signed certificates on internal services with certificates from the trusted internal CA, removing situations where users are conditioned to expect and accept warnings.
steps.outcome: Internal services confirmed presenting trusted certificates.

ITID-43633.def: An adversary who has stolen an organization's or CA's private signing key uses it to sign a new certificate for a domain or identity they do not control, producing a certificate that is technically valid and fully trusted because it carries a legitimate signature chain.
ITID-43633.purpose: Captures certificate forgery where an adversary uses a legitimately trusted organization's stolen private signing key to sign a new, fraudulent certificate that inherits full trust.
scopeIncludes: Certificates signed using a stolen intermediate or organizational private key
Confirmed use of an exfiltrated signing key to produce fraudulent certificates for phishing or interception infrastructure
scopeExcludes: Fraudulent issuance via CA process compromise with no key theft involved (ITID-43631)
Social-engineering acceptance of a self-signed certificate (ITID-43632)
The private key theft event itself when tracked as a standalone credential-theft incident (ITID-12633, ITID-64211/64212)
ITID-43633.severity: Critical — a certificate signed with a stolen legitimate key is indistinguishable from a genuine one until the key is revoked.
ITID-43633.priority: P1 immediate upon confirmed use of a stolen key to sign a certificate.
ITID-43633.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; revoke the compromised key and all certificates it signed, and notify affected relying parties.
indicators: Certificate signed by a key known or suspected to have been stolen/exfiltrated
Unexpected certificate issuance activity correlated with a prior key-theft incident
Certificate Transparency log entries for an unauthorized domain signed with the organization's key
vectors: Exfiltration of a private signing key from a poorly secured key store or HSM-bypassing system
Insider misuse of legitimate signing-key access
rootCauses: Private signing keys stored without hardware security module (HSM) protection
Insufficient access controls/audit logging on signing-key usage
No key-usage monitoring to detect anomalous signing activity
controls: Hardware security module (HSM) protection for all private signing keys
Signing-key usage audit logging and anomaly monitoring
Rapid key revocation and re-issuance procedures
ITID-43633.detection: Moderate — depends on signing-key usage audit logging and Certificate Transparency monitoring; weak where keys are managed outside a controlled, logged system.
ITID-43633.response: Revoke the compromised key and every certificate it signed, re-key using an HSM-protected key, and notify all relying parties of the compromise.
metrics: Signing keys protected by HSM
Confirmed stolen-key certificate forgery incidents per quarter
ITID-43633.notes: Differentiated from siblings by mechanism: use of legitimately stolen key material rather than CA process compromise or social engineering. Cross-references the underlying key/certificate theft leaves at ITID-12633, ITID-64211, and ITID-64212.

playbook.name: Forged Certificate Using Stolen Private Signing Key
playbook.description: An attacker stole an organization's private code-signing or TLS signing key and used it to forge valid-looking certificates or signed artifacts.

steps.title: Confirm private key theft and identify forged certificates/artifacts
steps.desc: Investigate how the private key was exfiltrated (e.g. compromised build server, key vault breach) and search Certificate Transparency logs / software repositories for certificates or signed binaries using the stolen key that the organization did not issue.
steps.guidance: Correlate key-store access logs with the suspected compromise timeframe.
steps.outcome: Confirmed key theft vector and list of fraudulently signed certificates/artifacts identified.
steps.tool: Key vault/HSM access logs, CT log search

steps.title: Revoke the compromised private key's certificate(s) immediately
steps.desc: Request emergency revocation of all certificates tied to the stolen private key from the issuing CA, and publish to CRL/OCSP.
steps.outcome: Certificate(s) revoked and confirmed via OCSP/CRL check.

steps.title: Generate and deploy a new signing key with hardened storage
steps.desc: Generate a new private signing key stored in a hardware security module (HSM) or equivalent hardened key vault with strict access controls, and re-sign/re-issue legitimate certificates/artifacts under the new key.
steps.outcome: New key deployed and confirmed in HSM-backed storage with restricted access.

steps.title: Validate new key deployment and monitor for further forged artifacts
steps.desc: Confirm all systems trust the new key and monitor CT logs/software repositories for further use of the stolen key.
steps.outcome: No further fraudulent use observed over a 30-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and mandate HSM-backed key storage as baseline control
steps.desc: Record the key-theft incident and formalize HSM-backed storage and strict access control as a mandatory baseline for all signing keys.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess the scope of trust abuse enabled by the stolen key
steps.desc: Determine what systems/users trust certificates or signatures from this key and therefore what could be impersonated or what malware could be signed as trusted.
steps.outcome: Trust-abuse blast radius documented.

steps.title: Isolate and remediate the key-theft vector
steps.desc: Isolate the compromised system (build server, key vault, HSM interface) used to exfiltrate the key and remove attacker access.
steps.outcome: Key-theft vector closed.

steps.title: Coordinate with CA and software distribution partners on forged artifact takedown
steps.desc: Notify the issuing CA and any software distribution/app-store partners of the forged certificates/signed artifacts so they can be blocklisted or removed.
steps.outcome: Forged artifacts blocklisted/removed by partners.

ITID-43634.def: General or as-yet-unclassified certificate forgery activity, used during initial triage before the specific mechanism is determined.
ITID-43634.purpose: Intake bucket for certificate forgery activity that has not yet been characterized by mechanism (CA compromise, social-engineered self-signed acceptance, or stolen signing key).
scopeIncludes: Suspected certificate forgery reported without confirmed mechanism
scopeExcludes: Any certificate forgery incident once the mechanism is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43631, ITID-43632, or ITID-43633 at that point
ITID-43634.severity: High pending triage, given the trust-model impact of any confirmed forged certificate.
ITID-43634.priority: P1 while mechanism is being determined.
ITID-43634.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately in parallel with mechanism triage.
indicators: Certificate anomaly reported without confirmed mechanism
vectors: Any certificate forgery technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient detail to determine the specific mechanism at time of detection
controls: Certificate Transparency log monitoring
Trust-store change monitoring
ITID-43634.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43634.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43631, ITID-43632, or ITID-43633.
metrics: Count of general certificate forgery reports pending reclassification
ITID-43634.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43631, ITID-43632, or ITID-43633 once the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Certificate Forgery
playbook.description: A generic certificate forgery event of unspecified mechanism (compromised CA issuance, accepted self-signed certificate, or stolen signing key) enabling impersonation or MITM.

steps.title: Confirm the forged certificate and classify its origin mechanism
steps.desc: Investigate the certificate's issuance chain, trust acceptance path, and signing key to determine whether it originated from a compromised CA, a socially-engineered self-signed acceptance, or a stolen private key.
steps.outcome: Mechanism classified and affected domain/system identified.
steps.abort: If certificate is legitimate/approved, close as benign.
steps.tool: CT log search, certificate chain analysis

steps.title: Revoke the forged certificate
steps.desc: Request revocation of the forged certificate from the issuing CA (or remove the accepted trust exception if self-signed).
steps.outcome: Certificate revoked/untrusted.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause per confirmed mechanism
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix: CAA restriction/CT monitoring, browser trust-warning enforcement policy, or new HSM-backed signing key, depending on the confirmed forgery mechanism.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified.

steps.title: Validate remediation and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Confirm the fix is effective and monitor CT logs/endpoint telemetry for renewed forgery attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 30-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document mechanism and refine classification/PKI policy
steps.desc: Record the confirmed mechanism to refine future classification and ensure the PKI trust policy addresses the identified gap.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed; policy reviewed.

steps.title: Assess exploitation impact
steps.desc: Determine whether the forged certificate was actively used for MITM interception or impersonation and what data was exposed.
steps.outcome: Impact documented.

steps.title: Contain the underlying compromise (CA, endpoint, or key)
steps.desc: Based on the confirmed mechanism, contain the relevant compromise: engage CA incident response, remediate the endpoint accepting the exception, or isolate the key-theft vector.
steps.outcome: Underlying compromise contained.

steps.title: Establish continuous CT log monitoring regardless of confirmed mechanism
steps.desc: Set up ongoing Certificate Transparency log monitoring for all organizational domains as a standing detective control, independent of which specific forgery mechanism was confirmed this time.
steps.outcome: CT monitoring active and alerting verified.

ITID-43711.def: An adversary sends a spoofed-source NTP monlist request to a misconfigured NTP server that still supports the deprecated monlist command, causing the server to send a disproportionately large response to the spoofed victim address, amplifying the attacker's traffic volume.
ITID-43711.purpose: Captures abuse of the legacy NTP monlist command on a misconfigured server, historically the primary vector for large-scale NTP amplification DDoS attacks.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of the monlist command specifically to generate amplified traffic toward a spoofed victim
NTP servers found responding to monlist requests during scanning/audit
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of other unpatched NTP daemon vulnerabilities not related to monlist (ITID-43712)
ITID-43711.severity: High — this technique has historically produced amplification factors in the hundreds, enabling significant DDoS impact from modest attacker bandwidth.
ITID-43711.priority: P1 if the organization's NTP infrastructure is identified as being used as an amplification source (reputational/abuse risk); P2 for standalone audit findings.
ITID-43711.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure teams to disable monlist immediately; escalate to IR/abuse-desk coordination if the organization's server was used to attack a third party.
indicators: Outbound NTP traffic volume far exceeding the inbound request volume from a single internal server
Vulnerability scan confirming monlist command still enabled
Abuse reports from third parties citing the organization's NTP server as an attack source
vectors: Spoofed-source UDP request to a monlist-enabled NTP server, directing the amplified response at a victim
rootCauses: Legacy NTP daemon versions with monlist enabled by default
No egress filtering preventing spoofed-source traffic amplification
NTP service exposed to the internet with no access restriction
controls: Disablement of the monlist command / upgrade to a modern NTP daemon
Egress filtering (BCP38) preventing spoofed-source traffic from leaving the network
Restriction of NTP service exposure to only required clients
ITID-43711.detection: Strong — amplification traffic patterns and monlist-enabled server scans are well established detection points.
ITID-43711.response: Disable monlist or upgrade the NTP daemon immediately, implement egress filtering, and coordinate with any third-party abuse reports.
metrics: NTP servers confirmed with monlist disabled
Confirmed amplification-source incidents per quarter
detections: Outbound amplification traffic volume anomaly detection
ITID-43711.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43712 by specificity: this leaf is scoped to the well-known monlist amplification technique specifically, not general daemon vulnerabilities.

playbook.name: NTP Monlist Command Abuse on Misconfigured Server
playbook.description: An attacker abused the legacy NTP monlist command on a misconfigured, internet-reachable NTP server to conduct a reflected/amplified DDoS attack, or to enumerate client history.

steps.title: Confirm monlist abuse via NTP server and network flow logs
steps.desc: Review the NTP server's query logs and network flow data for a high volume of monlist (mode 7) requests from spoofed source IPs, and check for outbound amplified response traffic characteristic of reflection/amplification abuse.
steps.guidance: Amplification factor for monlist can exceed 200x; check for disproportionately large outbound response volume relative to inbound query size.
steps.outcome: Confirmed monlist abuse with source pattern and amplification target(s) identified.
steps.abort: If volume is within normal operational parameters, close as benign.

steps.title: Disable the monlist command on the NTP server immediately
steps.desc: Disable the legacy monlist/mode 7 query functionality on the NTP daemon to immediately stop the abuse.
steps.outcome: Server confirmed no longer responding to monlist queries.

steps.title: Upgrade NTP daemon and apply reflector-hardening configuration org-wide
steps.desc: Upgrade to a patched NTP daemon version with monlist disabled by default, and audit all NTP servers org-wide for similar reflector-hardening (disable monlist, restrict query source, rate-limit responses), consistent with prior amplification-abuse remediation conventions.
steps.outcome: Org-wide NTP server audit confirms hardened configuration across the fleet.

steps.title: Notify the amplification victim if identified and monitor server traffic
steps.desc: Notify the identified reflected-DDoS victim organization where feasible, and monitor the NTP server's traffic for renewed abuse attempts.
steps.outcome: Victim notified where identifiable; no recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.
steps.abort: If victim cannot be identified/contacted, skip notification.

steps.title: Document and codify NTP reflector-hardening as baseline standard
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize NTP reflector-hardening (monlist disabled, query source restriction, rate limiting) as a mandatory baseline for all NTP infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Baseline updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Identify the ultimate DDoS victim (spoofed target) if amplification occurred
steps.desc: Determine the spoofed destination IP(s) that received the amplified reflected traffic, as the organization's server was used as an unwitting reflector against a third party.
steps.outcome: Victim identified for potential notification/coordination.

steps.title: Restrict NTP query source access at the firewall
steps.desc: Apply firewall rules restricting which source IPs/ranges may query the NTP server, removing unrestricted internet reachability.
steps.outcome: NTP server no longer reachable from arbitrary internet sources.

steps.title: Deploy rate limiting on remaining permitted NTP query sources
steps.desc: Apply response rate-limiting on the NTP daemon to cap the amplification factor even for legitimately permitted query sources, as defense-in-depth beyond disabling monlist alone.
steps.outcome: Rate limiting verified active via test query burst.

ITID-43712.def: An adversary exploits a known vulnerability (other than the monlist amplification issue) in an unpatched or legacy NTP daemon implementation, potentially achieving remote code execution, information disclosure, or other daemon-specific impact.
ITID-43712.purpose: Captures exploitation of unpatched or legacy NTP daemon vulnerabilities generally, distinct from the specific and well-known monlist amplification technique.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a CVE-tracked NTP daemon vulnerability unrelated to monlist
Compromise of an NTP service via an unpatched software flaw
scopeExcludes: The specific, well-known monlist amplification technique (ITID-43711)
ITID-43712.severity: High — depends on the specific vulnerability's impact, ranging from denial of service to remote code execution.
ITID-43712.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure teams for emergency patching and to IR if code execution or data exposure is confirmed.
indicators: Vulnerability scan findings confirming an unpatched, CVE-affected NTP daemon version
Exploit-framework signatures matching a known NTP daemon vulnerability
Anomalous process behavior on a host running an outdated NTP service
vectors: Direct exploitation of a known, unpatched NTP daemon CVE
Automated vulnerability scanning followed by targeted exploitation
rootCauses: NTP daemon not included in routine patch management scope
Legacy/unsupported NTP daemon version still in production use
NTP service exposed to untrusted networks
controls: Inclusion of NTP daemons in routine patch management scope
Upgrade from legacy/unsupported NTP daemon versions
Network restriction of NTP service exposure to trusted sources
ITID-43712.detection: Moderate — dependent on vulnerability scanning coverage extending to NTP infrastructure, which is often overlooked relative to core application servers.
ITID-43712.response: Patch or upgrade the affected daemon immediately, and assess for signs of compromise if the vulnerability allows code execution.
metrics: NTP daemons confirmed patched/upgraded
Confirmed daemon-vulnerability exploitation incidents per quarter
ITID-43712.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43711 by scope: general daemon vulnerabilities rather than the specific, well-known monlist amplification technique.

playbook.name: Unpatched/Legacy NTP Daemon Vulnerability Exploitation
playbook.description: An attacker exploited a known vulnerability in an unpatched or legacy NTP daemon version to achieve remote code execution, denial of service, or information disclosure.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation via IDS/EDR and NTP daemon version check
steps.desc: Correlate IDS/IPS alerts for known NTP CVE exploit signatures with the target server's actual NTP daemon version to confirm it is vulnerable and was exploited.
steps.guidance: Check for crash/restart events in the NTP daemon logs correlating with the alert timing.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploited host, NTP daemon version, and specific CVE identified.
steps.abort: If daemon version is not vulnerable to the alerted CVE, close as false positive.

steps.title: Isolate the affected NTP server
steps.desc: Network-isolate the exploited NTP server to prevent further exploitation or, if RCE occurred, lateral movement from the compromised host.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.
steps.abort: If host is critical time-sync infrastructure, apply restrictive ACLs instead of full isolation with compensating monitoring.

steps.title: Patch or replace the vulnerable NTP daemon
steps.desc: Apply the vendor patch for the exploited CVE or upgrade to a current, actively maintained NTP implementation (e.g. chrony) if the legacy daemon is no longer supported.
steps.outcome: Patched/upgraded daemon confirmed not vulnerable to the exploited CVE.

steps.title: Restore the primary NTP server to service and validate time sync integrity
steps.desc: Return the patched server to service and confirm dependent systems resume accurate time synchronization without disruption.
steps.outcome: Time sync confirmed accurate across dependent systems; no recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and tighten patch SLA for critical infrastructure services
steps.desc: Record the incident and tighten patch-compliance SLA enforcement for time-synchronization and other critical infrastructure services.
steps.outcome: SLA policy updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess impact: RCE, DoS, or information disclosure
steps.desc: Determine which impact class resulted from the exploitation (remote code execution, service crash/DoS, or information disclosure) via EDR telemetry and service availability logs.
steps.outcome: Impact class and downstream effects documented.

steps.title: Fail over to a redundant/backup NTP source
steps.desc: Redirect dependent systems to a redundant or backup NTP source to maintain accurate time synchronization while the primary server is remediated.
steps.guidance: Time synchronization is critical infrastructure for logging/certificate validation — avoid extended outages.
steps.outcome: Dependent systems maintain accurate time sync via the backup source.

steps.title: Audit fleet-wide NTP daemon versions for the same vulnerability
steps.desc: Scan all NTP servers/services org-wide for the same vulnerable daemon version and remediate to close the exposure window everywhere.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide scan confirms no remaining vulnerable instances.

ITID-43713.def: General or as-yet-unclassified NTP protocol exploitation activity, used during initial triage before the specific technique is determined.
ITID-43713.purpose: Intake bucket for NTP protocol exploitation activity that has not yet been characterized as monlist amplification abuse or a general daemon vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Suspected NTP exploitation reported without a confirmed technique
scopeExcludes: Any NTP exploitation incident once the technique is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43711 or ITID-43712 at that point
Volumetric NTP amplification DDoS impact already tracked under the general Availability domain (ITID-41131 NTP Amplification Attack)
ITID-43713.priority: P2 during triage; P1 if code execution or active amplification abuse is confirmed.
ITID-43713.escalation: Escalate to infrastructure teams immediately in parallel with triage.
indicators: NTP-related alert or scan finding flagged without confirmed technique
vectors: Any NTP exploitation technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient detail to determine the specific technique at time of detection
controls: NTP service logging and vulnerability scanning
ITID-43713.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43713.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43711 or ITID-43712.
metrics: Count of general NTP exploitation reports pending reclassification
ITID-43713.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43711 or ITID-43712 once the technique is known. Cross-references ITID-41131 for the general volumetric-DDoS-impact perspective on NTP amplification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General NTP Protocol Exploitation
playbook.description: A generic NTP protocol exploitation event of unspecified sub-technique (monlist amplification abuse or daemon vulnerability exploitation) affecting an NTP server.

steps.title: Confirm the exploitation and classify its sub-technique
steps.desc: Review NTP server logs, network flow data, and IDS alerts to confirm exploitation and determine whether it was reflection/amplification abuse (e.g. monlist) or a daemon vulnerability exploit.
steps.outcome: Sub-technique classified and affected server identified.
steps.abort: If volume/alert is within normal parameters, close as benign.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict the affected NTP server
steps.desc: Restrict query access or isolate the server depending on the confirmed sub-technique, and fail over dependent systems to a backup time source if needed.
steps.outcome: Abuse/exploitation stopped; time sync maintained via backup.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause per confirmed sub-technique
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate fix: disable monlist and restrict query sources, or patch/upgrade the vulnerable daemon, and audit the fleet for the same gap.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and verified fleet-wide.

steps.title: Validate remediation and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Confirm the fix is effective and monitor for renewed abuse/exploitation attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document sub-technique and refine classification/hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the confirmed sub-technique to refine future classification and ensure NTP hardening baseline addresses the identified gap.
steps.outcome: After-action report filed; baseline reviewed.

steps.title: Assess impact scope
steps.desc: Determine the impact: amplified DDoS against a third party, service disruption, or compromise of the NTP server itself.
steps.outcome: Impact documented.

steps.title: Notify third-party victim if amplification abuse occurred
steps.desc: If reflection/amplification abuse against a third party is confirmed, notify the victim where identifiable.
steps.outcome: Victim notified where applicable.
steps.abort: If not an amplification scenario, skip.

steps.title: Establish a redundant/backup NTP source for critical dependent systems
steps.desc: Ensure critical systems depending on this NTP server have a configured secondary time source to maintain resilience against future NTP-targeted incidents of either sub-technique.
steps.outcome: Redundant source configured and verified for critical dependents.

ITID-43721.def: An adversary injects unsanitized input into an LDAP filter or query to retrieve directory attributes and records beyond what the application intended to expose, exploiting insufficient input validation on LDAP-bound query parameters.
ITID-43721.purpose: Captures LDAP injection used specifically to extract data from the directory (e.g. user attributes, group membership) rather than to enumerate object existence or bypass authentication.
scopeIncludes: Injected LDAP filter syntax used to broaden a search and return additional directory attributes/records
Confirmed extraction of sensitive directory data (e.g. email addresses, group memberships, organizational data) via LDAP injection
scopeExcludes: LDAP injection used specifically for authentication bypass, tracked separately (ITID-12835)
LDAP injection used purely for object/attribute enumeration without bulk data extraction (ITID-43722)
Blind LDAP injection with no direct data returned in the response (ITID-43723)
ITID-43721.severity: High — directory data often includes information useful for further social engineering or lateral movement (org structure, group membership, contact details).
ITID-43721.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful data extraction.
ITID-43721.escalation: Escalate to application security and directory-services teams immediately.
indicators: Application logs showing LDAP special characters (*, (, ), \, NUL) in input fields
LDAP server logs showing unusually broad or malformed filter queries
Application response containing more directory data than the intended use case
vectors: Injecting LDAP filter metacharacters into a search or login field to broaden query scope
Automated LDAP injection tooling against a vulnerable application endpoint
rootCauses: Lack of input sanitization/escaping for LDAP special characters
Application constructing LDAP filters via direct string concatenation of user input
Directory service accounts used by the application granted excessive read scope
controls: Input sanitization/escaping for all LDAP special characters
Parameterized LDAP query construction (avoiding direct string concatenation)
Least-privilege scoping of the directory service account used by the application
ITID-43721.detection: Moderate — application and LDAP server logging can surface this where filter-syntax anomaly detection is configured; often under-monitored relative to SQL injection.
ITID-43721.response: Patch the vulnerable query construction, restrict the application's directory read scope, and assess what data was extracted.
metrics: Applications remediated for LDAP filter injection
Confirmed data-extraction LDAP injection incidents per quarter
ITID-43721.notes: Differentiated from siblings by objective: bulk data extraction, distinct from enumeration (ITID-43722), blind inference (ITID-43723), or authentication bypass (ITID-12835).

playbook.name: LDAP Injection for Directory Data Extraction
playbook.description: An attacker injected malicious LDAP filter syntax into an application's directory search input to extract unauthorized directory data (user attributes, group memberships, etc).

steps.title: Identify LDAP injection payloads in application/directory logs
steps.desc: Review application and LDAP/AD server logs for search filter parameters containing injected LDAP metacharacters (*, (, ), \, NUL) or filter-manipulation strings targeting the application's directory-search functionality.
steps.guidance: Correlate application requests with corresponding LDAP query logs on the directory server to see the actual filter that was executed.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and injected filter syntax identified.
steps.abort: If special characters are part of a legitimate user search (e.g. a name containing a parenthesis), close as benign.
steps.tool: Application logs / LDAP server audit logs

steps.title: Deploy a WAF virtual patch blocking LDAP injection patterns
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule blocking LDAP metacharacter injection patterns on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via input validation and parameterized LDAP queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to implement proper LDAP special-character escaping/encoding and parameterized filter construction at the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.guidance: Retest the original payload against the patched build to confirm the injection point is closed.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms LDAP metacharacters are properly escaped and no longer alter query logic.

steps.title: Assess and remediate downstream data exposure impact
steps.desc: If sensitive directory data (e.g. privileged group membership) was disclosed, assess whether follow-on targeted attacks are likely and notify affected data subjects if warranted.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per policy.
steps.abort: If no sensitive data confirmed disclosed, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for LDAP injection patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add automated LDAP-injection detection to the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine what directory data was extracted
steps.desc: Reconstruct the sequence of injected queries and corresponding application responses to determine what user attributes, group memberships, or other directory data was disclosed.
steps.outcome: Scope of directory data disclosure documented.

steps.title: Restrict the application's directory-bind account privileges
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege to the LDAP bind account used by the application so even a successful injection can only read the minimum required attributes/OUs.
steps.outcome: Bind account confirmed scoped appropriately.

steps.title: Enable LDAP query auditing for the affected bind account
steps.desc: Turn on detailed query auditing for the application's LDAP bind account to detect any future anomalous directory-search activity quickly.
steps.outcome: Auditing active and generating events on test queries.

ITID-43722.def: An adversary injects LDAP filter syntax to systematically probe for the existence of specific usernames, groups, or attributes in the directory, using the application's differing responses (found/not-found) to build a map of valid directory objects.
ITID-43722.purpose: Captures LDAP injection used to enumerate the existence of directory objects or attributes, rather than to extract bulk data or bypass authentication.
scopeIncludes: Systematic probing of username/object existence via crafted LDAP filter injection
Directory reconnaissance enabled by an LDAP-injection-vulnerable application endpoint
scopeExcludes: Bulk extraction of directory attribute data (ITID-43721)
Blind injection relying on true/false inference with no visible found/not-found distinction (ITID-43723)
ITID-43722.severity: Medium-High — enumeration is a reconnaissance precursor to more targeted attacks such as password spraying against confirmed valid usernames.
ITID-43722.priority: P2 for detected enumeration attempts; P1 if correlated with a subsequent credential-based attack against enumerated accounts.
ITID-43722.escalation: Escalate to application security; escalate to IR if enumeration is followed by a targeted credential attack.
indicators: Repeated requests systematically varying a username/object parameter with LDAP injection syntax
Application response timing or content differences correlated with object existence
High volume of enumeration-pattern requests from a single source
vectors: Automated enumeration scripts exploiting an LDAP-injection-vulnerable login or search field
Manual probing of a small set of high-value usernames via crafted filter injection
rootCauses: Lack of input sanitization/escaping for LDAP special characters
Application response distinguishing found/not-found states in a way that leaks object existence
No rate limiting on directory-query-backed endpoints
controls: Input sanitization/escaping for all LDAP special characters
Uniform application responses regardless of object existence
Rate limiting on directory-query-backed endpoints
ITID-43722.detection: Moderate — volumetric/pattern-based detection of systematic enumeration requests is achievable but often not specifically tuned for LDAP.
ITID-43722.response: Patch the vulnerable query construction, rate-limit or block the source, and monitor enumerated accounts for follow-on attack attempts.
metrics: Applications remediated for enumeration-enabling response differences
Confirmed enumeration incidents per quarter
ITID-43722.notes: Differentiated from siblings by objective: object-existence enumeration/reconnaissance rather than bulk data extraction or blind inference.

playbook.name: LDAP Injection for Unauthorized Object/Attribute Enumeration
playbook.description: An attacker used LDAP injection to enumerate directory objects and attributes beyond the application's intended scope, mapping the organization's identity structure.

steps.title: Identify enumeration-pattern LDAP injection activity
steps.desc: Review application and LDAP server logs for a high volume of sequential/iterative injected filter queries characteristic of automated object/attribute enumeration (e.g. wildcard-based iteration across the directory tree).
steps.guidance: Correlate request volume and pattern with LDAP query logs showing broad OU/attribute traversal beyond the application's intended search scope.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and enumeration pattern identified.
steps.abort: If pattern volume is too low to be conclusive, monitor before escalating.
steps.tool: Application logs / LDAP server audit logs

steps.title: Block the enumerating source and deploy a WAF virtual patch
steps.desc: Block the source IP conducting the enumeration and add a WAF rule blocking the injection pattern on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Enumeration traffic stopped.

steps.title: Remediate via input validation and parameterized LDAP queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to implement proper LDAP special-character escaping and parameterized filter construction, verified by retesting the enumeration payload against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms enumeration is no longer possible via the endpoint.

steps.title: Assess risk of follow-on targeted attacks using the mapped structure
steps.desc: Given the attacker now has a map of the identity structure, assess and brief the SOC on elevated risk of targeted phishing/password-spray attacks against enumerated accounts.
steps.outcome: SOC briefed; elevated monitoring applied to high-value enumerated accounts.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for LDAP enumeration patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add automated detection for LDAP injection/enumeration to the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine the scope of the directory structure mapped
steps.desc: Reconstruct which objects/OUs/attributes were enumerated to assess how much of the organization's identity structure (users, groups, service accounts) was exposed to the attacker.
steps.outcome: Scope of directory structure exposure documented.

steps.title: Restrict the application's directory-bind account scope
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege to the LDAP bind account so future injection attempts cannot enumerate beyond the application's legitimate OU scope.
steps.outcome: Bind account confirmed scoped appropriately.

steps.title: Enable LDAP query auditing for the affected bind account
steps.desc: Turn on detailed query auditing for the application's LDAP bind account to detect any future anomalous enumeration activity quickly.
steps.outcome: Auditing active and generating events on test queries.

ITID-43723.def: LDAP injection in which the attacker submits conditional filter payloads and infers directory attribute values character-by-character from indirect differences in the application's behavior (e.g. response content, timing), rather than from any directly returned data.
ITID-43723.purpose: Captures blind LDAP injection where the attacker infers directory content through true/false response differences, with no data or existence result directly returned.
scopeIncludes: Conditional true/false LDAP filter payload injection with inference from indirect behavioral differences
Automated blind LDAP injection tooling iterating through characters
scopeExcludes: Direct data extraction with visible results (ITID-43721)
Object-existence enumeration with a clear found/not-found signal (ITID-43722)
ITID-43723.severity: High, though slower to exploit than direct extraction; still results in complete attribute extraction given sufficient time.
ITID-43723.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful extraction; P2 for detected probing.
ITID-43723.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately upon confirmation, given the difficulty of detecting this technique at low volume.
indicators: Repeated near-identical requests differing only in a conditional LDAP filter payload value
High volume of requests from a single source against the same parameter over an extended period
vectors: Automated blind LDAP injection tooling iterating through characters using conditional filter logic
Manual conditional payload crafting against a vulnerable parameter with no visible direct output
rootCauses: Lack of input sanitization/escaping for LDAP special characters
No rate limiting or anomaly detection on repetitive request patterns
controls: Input sanitization/escaping for all LDAP special characters
Rate limiting and anomaly detection on repetitive request patterns
Parameterized LDAP query construction
ITID-43723.detection: Weak-Moderate — requires volumetric/behavioral analysis rather than simple signature matching.
ITID-43723.response: Patch the vulnerable query construction, rate-limit or block the source, and assess how much data was likely inferred given the request volume observed.
metrics: Confirmed blind LDAP injection incidents per quarter
Coverage of behavioral/volumetric detection rules for blind injection
ITID-43723.notes: Differentiated from siblings by inference mechanism: indirect true/false behavioral inference rather than direct data return or a clear existence signal.

playbook.name: Blind LDAP Injection Exploitation
playbook.description: An attacker inferred directory data by injecting boolean/timing-based LDAP filter conditions and observing response differences, without direct data output.

steps.title: Identify blind LDAP injection probing via response-diffing analysis
steps.desc: Review application/LDAP logs for pairs of near-identical requests differing only in an injected boolean LDAP filter condition, with correlated differences in application response (content/status/timing).
steps.guidance: Look for a high volume of sequential automated requests characteristic of blind extraction tooling iterating character-by-character.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint/parameter and the blind extraction pattern identified.
steps.abort: If pattern volume is too low to be conclusive, monitor before escalating.
steps.tool: Application logs / LDAP server audit logs

steps.title: Block the enumerating source and deploy a WAF virtual patch
steps.desc: Block the source IP conducting the blind extraction and add a WAF rule blocking boolean/timing-based LDAP injection patterns on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Automated extraction traffic blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via input validation and parameterized LDAP queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to implement proper LDAP special-character escaping and parameterized filter construction, verified by retesting representative boolean payloads against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms response no longer varies with injected LDAP filter conditions.

steps.title: Assess and remediate estimated data exposure impact
steps.desc: Based on the estimated scope, notify affected data subjects or reset credentials as warranted by the worst-case assumption.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per policy.
steps.abort: If estimated scope is negligible, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST rule for blind LDAP injection patterns
steps.desc: Record the vulnerable pattern and add automated blind-LDAP-injection detection to the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Estimate scope of data inferred through blind extraction
steps.desc: Estimate the volume/scope of directory data likely inferred based on the number and pattern of requests observed, since blind extraction does not appear directly in response content.
steps.outcome: Estimated exposure scope documented.

steps.title: Restrict the application's directory-bind account privileges
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege to the LDAP bind account used by the application to limit the scope of what any successful blind extraction could infer.
steps.outcome: Bind account confirmed scoped appropriately.

steps.title: Standardize application error handling to prevent response-diffing signals
steps.desc: Ensure the application returns uniform responses regardless of the LDAP filter's truth value, removing the boolean oracle even if a residual injection path is later found.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms uniform response behavior.

ITID-43724.def: General or as-yet-unclassified LDAP injection activity, used during initial triage before the specific technique is determined.
ITID-43724.purpose: Intake bucket for LDAP injection activity that has not yet been characterized by objective (data extraction, enumeration, or blind inference).
scopeIncludes: Suspected LDAP injection reported without a confirmed technique
scopeExcludes: Any LDAP injection incident once the technique is confirmed — reclassify to ITID-43721, ITID-43722, or ITID-43723 at that point
LDAP injection used for authentication bypass, tracked separately (ITID-12835)
ITID-43724.severity: High pending triage, given LDAP injection's typical data-exposure impact.
ITID-43724.priority: P1 while technique is being determined.
ITID-43724.escalation: Escalate to application security immediately in parallel with technique triage.
indicators: WAF or application alert flagging a generic LDAP injection payload pattern, technique unconfirmed
vectors: Any LDAP injection technique, not yet attributed
rootCauses: Insufficient logging/detail to determine the specific technique at time of detection
controls: Input sanitization/escaping for all LDAP special characters
Web application firewall with LDAP injection signature coverage
ITID-43724.detection: Variable — dependent on available logging at time of report.
ITID-43724.response: Gather additional telemetry to reclassify into ITID-43721, ITID-43722, or ITID-43723.
metrics: Count of general LDAP injection reports pending reclassification
detections: Generic LDAP injection payload signature detection
ITID-43724.notes: Catch-all triage leaf; reclassify into ITID-43721, ITID-43722, or ITID-43723 once the technique is known. Cross-references the authentication-bypass-specific leaf at ITID-12835.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General LDAP Injection
playbook.description: A generic LDAP injection event of unspecified sub-technique (direct data extraction, enumeration, or blind extraction) exploiting a vulnerable directory-search endpoint.

steps.title: Identify the injection payload and classify its sub-technique
steps.desc: Review application and LDAP server logs for injected filter syntax and determine which sub-technique was used (direct data extraction, object/attribute enumeration, or blind boolean-based).
steps.outcome: Sub-technique classified and vulnerable endpoint/parameter identified.
steps.abort: If pattern is a false positive, close as benign.
steps.tool: Application logs / LDAP server audit logs

steps.title: Deploy a WAF virtual patch for the identified pattern
steps.desc: Add or tighten a WAF rule blocking the specific LDAP injection syntax observed on the vulnerable endpoint.
steps.outcome: Repeat/variant payloads blocked.

steps.title: Remediate via input validation and parameterized LDAP queries
steps.desc: File and track an AppSec/developer ticket to implement proper LDAP special-character escaping and parameterized filter construction, verified by retesting the original payload against the patched build.
steps.outcome: Retest confirms the injection point is closed.

steps.title: Remediate downstream data exposure impact
steps.desc: Notify affected data subjects or reset credentials as warranted by the confirmed scope of exposure.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure remediated per policy.
steps.abort: If no sensitive data confirmed exposed, skip.

steps.title: Document and add SAST/DAST regression coverage
steps.desc: Record the confirmed sub-technique and vulnerable pattern, and add regression test/detection coverage to the CI/CD pipeline.
steps.outcome: Pipeline rule added; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess the scope of directory data accessed or inferred
steps.desc: Determine what data was extracted or inferred through the injection based on the confirmed sub-technique.
steps.outcome: Scope of impact documented.

steps.title: Restrict the application's directory-bind account privileges
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege to the LDAP bind account used by the application to limit further exploitation impact.
steps.outcome: Bind account confirmed scoped appropriately.

steps.title: Enable LDAP query auditing for the affected bind account
steps.desc: Turn on detailed query auditing for the application's LDAP bind account to detect any future anomalous directory activity regardless of sub-technique.
steps.outcome: Auditing active and generating events on test queries.

ITID-43731.def: An adversary positioned to observe network traffic captures usernames and passwords transmitted in the clear during a Telnet session, exploiting the protocol's complete lack of transport encryption.
ITID-43731.purpose: Captures passive interception of Telnet's inherently cleartext credential exchange, as distinct from actively exploiting weak/default credentials on a Telnet service.
scopeIncludes: Passive network capture of Telnet session traffic revealing plaintext credentials
On-path positioning specifically to intercept Telnet authentication exchanges
scopeExcludes: Active exploitation of a default or weak Telnet credential without interception being the mechanism (ITID-43732)
ITID-43731.severity: High — any successful interception yields immediately usable, plaintext credentials.
ITID-43731.priority: P1 upon confirmed interception capability or evidence of active capture.
ITID-43731.escalation: Escalate to network engineering to eliminate Telnet use and to IR to determine what credentials may have been exposed.
indicators: Telnet traffic observed on the network (port 23 or equivalent)
Packet capture tooling observed on a segment carrying Telnet traffic
Credentials later found in use that match a known Telnet-exposed account
vectors: Passive packet capture on a shared network segment carrying Telnet traffic
ARP spoofing or span-port access specifically to intercept Telnet sessions
rootCauses: Telnet still in use for device/system administration instead of SSH
Network devices retaining Telnet management access enabled by default
No network segmentation isolating legacy management traffic
controls: Replacement of Telnet with SSH for all administrative access
Network segmentation isolating any remaining legacy management traffic
Network monitoring alerting on any Telnet traffic detected
ITID-43731.detection: Strong — Telnet traffic itself is trivially detectable by any network monitoring tool once looked for; the challenge is organizational will to eliminate it.
ITID-43731.response: Disable Telnet and migrate to SSH immediately, rotate any credentials that may have traversed the network in cleartext, and audit for other legacy cleartext protocols.
metrics: Devices/systems migrated from Telnet to SSH
Telnet traffic instances detected per quarter
ITID-43731.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43732 by mechanism: passive credential interception, not active exploitation of a weak/default credential.

playbook.name: Telnet Cleartext Credential Interception
playbook.description: An attacker on the network path captured cleartext Telnet session traffic, harvesting login credentials transmitted unencrypted.

steps.title: Detect Telnet interception activity via network monitoring
steps.desc: Review network IDS/packet capture logs for evidence of a host performing packet capture or ARP spoofing positioned to intercept Telnet (TCP 23) traffic, and identify affected Telnet sessions.
steps.guidance: Look for ARP anomalies on segments carrying Telnet traffic to network devices.
steps.outcome: Attacker host/position and affected Telnet session(s)/device(s) identified.
steps.abort: If activity matches an approved network monitoring/packet capture tool, close as benign.

steps.title: Isolate the intercepting device from the network
steps.desc: Shut down or NAC-quarantine the switch port of the device performing the interception.
steps.outcome: Interception activity stops.

steps.title: Replace Telnet with SSH on all affected devices
steps.desc: Disable the Telnet service and enable SSH (with key-based or strong password authentication) as the actual protocol-level fix, since Telnet's cleartext design is the root cause, not merely a configuration issue.
steps.guidance: Verify device support for SSH; for legacy devices without SSH support, plan replacement or isolate to a dedicated management VLAN as a compensating control.
steps.outcome: Telnet disabled and SSH confirmed active on the affected device(s).

steps.title: Validate SSH access and monitor for renewed interception attempts
steps.desc: Confirm administrators can manage the device via SSH and monitor the segment for renewed interception activity.
steps.outcome: No recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and mandate Telnet deprecation as baseline policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a policy prohibiting Telnet for device management, requiring SSH or equivalent encrypted management protocols org-wide.
steps.outcome: Policy updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Determine which credentials were exposed
steps.desc: Identify which device/system credentials were transmitted in cleartext during the intercepted session(s).
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials/devices documented.

steps.title: Reset exposed device credentials immediately
steps.desc: Rotate the credentials for any device/system whose Telnet session was intercepted.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Audit fleet-wide for remaining Telnet-enabled devices
steps.desc: Scan the network for all devices still running Telnet and prioritize migration to SSH org-wide.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide Telnet inventory produced with remediation plan.

ITID-43732.def: An adversary directly authenticates to a Telnet-exposed network device or system using a default, vendor-supplied, or easily guessed credential, gaining administrative access without needing to intercept any traffic.
ITID-43732.purpose: Captures active exploitation of default or weak credentials on a Telnet-exposed network device, as distinct from passive interception of a legitimate credential exchange.
scopeIncludes: Successful authentication to a Telnet service using a default or well-known weak credential
Automated scanning tools identifying and exploiting Telnet-exposed devices with default credentials (e.g. IoT/router botnet-style compromise)
scopeExcludes: Passive interception of a legitimate credential exchange over Telnet (ITID-43731)
ITID-43732.severity: Critical — this is a common vector for large-scale device compromise (e.g. IoT botnet recruitment) and grants direct administrative access.
ITID-43732.priority: P1 upon confirmed unauthorized administrative access.
ITID-43732.escalation: Escalate to IR and infrastructure teams immediately; treat the device as compromised and isolate it.
indicators: Successful Telnet authentication using a known default credential
Device configuration changes inconsistent with authorized change management
Device exhibiting botnet-recruitment behavior (outbound scanning, C2 beaconing) following Telnet compromise
vectors: Automated scanning/exploitation tools cycling through known default credential lists against exposed Telnet services
Manual exploitation of a device left on factory-default credentials
rootCauses: Default credentials never changed on network devices
Telnet management interface exposed to the internet or an untrusted network
No device credential audit/rotation program
controls: Mandatory credential rotation from vendor defaults at deployment
Removal of internet exposure for Telnet management interfaces
Replacement of Telnet with SSH wherever supported
ITID-43732.detection: Strong — default-credential authentication attempts and subsequent anomalous device behavior are well signatured.
ITID-43732.response: Isolate and rebuild/reconfigure the compromised device, rotate all credentials, and migrate management access to SSH.
metrics: Devices audited and remediated for default Telnet credentials
Confirmed default-credential Telnet compromises per quarter
ITID-43732.notes: Differentiated from ITID-43731 by mechanism: active credential exploitation rather than passive interception.

playbook.name: Telnet Default/Weak Credential Exploitation on Network Device
playbook.description: An attacker accessed a network device via Telnet using default or weak vendor-supplied credentials that were never changed.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized Telnet access via default/weak credentials
steps.desc: Review the device's authentication logs for successful login using a known default username/password, and correlate with an unexpected source IP/time.
steps.guidance: Check vendor default-credential lists against what was used to authenticate.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access via default/weak credential, with device and source identified.
steps.abort: If login matches an approved admin action, close as benign.

steps.title: Terminate the attacker session and reset device credentials
steps.desc: Force-terminate any active attacker session and immediately change the device's credentials to a strong, non-default value.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated; device secured with new credentials.

steps.title: Replace Telnet with SSH and audit fleet-wide for default credentials
steps.desc: Disable Telnet and enable SSH on the device, and scan all network devices org-wide for default/weak credentials, remediating each one found.
steps.outcome: SSH active on the device; fleet-wide default-credential audit completed and remediated.

steps.title: Verify device configuration integrity and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm the device configuration matches the known-good baseline (no attacker-planted changes remain) and monitor for renewed unauthorized access attempts.
steps.outcome: Configuration confirmed clean; no recurrence over a 14-day monitoring window.

steps.title: Document and mandate default-credential elimination as onboarding standard
steps.desc: Record the incident and formalize a requirement that all network devices have default credentials changed as part of the device onboarding/provisioning checklist.
steps.outcome: Onboarding standard updated; after-action report filed.

steps.title: Assess what configuration changes or data access occurred
steps.desc: Review the device configuration change log for any unauthorized modifications made during the attacker's session.
