ITID-44921.def: A defensive/response action classification (not an adversary technique) in which the SOC or network operations team adds a firewall or web-proxy block rule against a confirmed C2 IP address, preventing further outbound (and, where relevant, inbound) traffic to that address from the organization's network as part of active incident containment.
ITID-44921.purpose: Captures the organization's deliberate firewall or proxy block applied against a known malicious C2 IP address during incident response.
scopeIncludes: Perimeter firewall rule added to drop/deny traffic to a confirmed C2 IP
Web proxy block rule added against a confirmed C2 IP where traffic is proxied rather than routed directly
Emergency/out-of-cycle block rule deployment during active incident response
scopeExcludes: DNS-layer blocking of the associated domain rather than direct IP blocking (ITID-44922)
Threat-intel-feed-driven automated blocklist updates at scale rather than a single incident-driven manual block (ITID-44923)
ITID-44921.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf classifies the organization's own disruption action; document the severity of the underlying C2 incident separately.
ITID-44921.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes: IP blocking is typically one of the fastest available containment actions and is applied promptly once a C2 IP is confirmed.
ITID-44921.escalation: Coordinate with legal/threat intel before any external-facing blocklist action affecting shared or third-party infrastructure; notify network operations to avoid unintended impact on legitimate services sharing the same IP (e.g., cloud/CDN-hosted C2).
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs a defender action; associated evidence is the firewall/proxy rule change record
Post-block traffic logs showing attempted (and now denied) connections from internal hosts to the blocked IP, useful for identifying additional infected hosts
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents a defensive action taken in response to an identified C2 IP
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf; document root causes under the originating C2 incident's own ITID classification
controls: Emergency change-management process for expedited firewall/proxy rule deployment during active incidents
Firewall/proxy rule change auditing and periodic cleanup of stale block entries
ITID-44921.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity; post-block denied-connection logs become a detection source for identifying additional infected hosts.
ITID-44921.response: Validate the block rule is functioning (test/verify denial), monitor denied-connection logs to identify additional infected hosts, and monitor for the adversary's fallback C2 mechanism (e.g., a new IP or domain) that may activate once the block takes effect.
metrics: Count of C2 IPs blocked per year
Mean time from C2 IP confirmation to block deployment
Count of additional infected hosts identified via denied-connection logs
detections: Post-block denied-connection log monitoring for infected-host identification
ITID-44921.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty for this leaf and its siblings in the C2 Disruption and Takedown Methods branch.

playbook.name: Firewall/Proxy Block Applied Against Known C2 IP Address
playbook.description: The organization needs to apply a firewall/proxy block against a known-malicious C2 IP address as a defensive disruption action, ensuring the block is correctly scoped so it does not inadvertently impact legitimate traffic sharing the same IP or address range.

steps.title: Confirm the IP is malicious and assess shared-infrastructure risk
steps.desc: Validate the IP against threat intelligence and check whether it is dedicated malicious infrastructure or shared/cloud infrastructure that may also host legitimate co-tenants.
steps.guidance: Check ASN, hosting provider, and reverse DNS to assess how narrowly the block must be scoped.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment informing the appropriate block scope (single IP vs. range).
steps.abort: If the IP cannot be confirmed malicious, do not proceed with blocking.

steps.title: Apply the block and validate it takes effect
steps.desc: Implement the firewall/proxy deny rule for the target IP and validate via test traffic that it is being blocked as expected.
steps.outcome: Outbound connections to the C2 IP are confirmed blocked.
steps.abort: If the block does not take effect as expected, troubleshoot rule ordering/precedence before proceeding.

steps.title: Remediate hosts previously observed communicating with the blocked IP
steps.desc: Identify and remediate any internal hosts that were communicating with the now-blocked IP prior to the block, since the block alone does not remove existing infections.
steps.outcome: Previously affected hosts are remediated.

steps.title: Maintain the block as a standing control and monitor
steps.desc: Keep the block in place as a durable control and monitor for continued blocked-attempt logs indicating lingering infection or actor persistence.
steps.outcome: Blocked-attempt logs decline to zero, confirming successful remediation.

steps.title: Document the block and outcomes
steps.desc: Record the IP, block scope decision, and remediation outcomes for future reference and to inform blocklist management processes.
steps.outcome: A documented blocking record supporting future similar actions and blocklist governance.

steps.title: Determine the correct block placement and scope
steps.desc: Decide whether the block should be applied at the perimeter firewall, web proxy, or both, and at what granularity (exact IP, small CIDR, or ASN), based on the risk assessment.
steps.guidance: Prefer the narrowest scope that reliably blocks the malicious traffic.
steps.outcome: A documented block placement and scope decision.

steps.title: Verify no legitimate traffic is impacted by the block
steps.desc: Monitor for any help desk tickets, application errors, or business complaints indicating the block has disrupted legitimate services sharing the IP/range.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of no legitimate service disruption from the block.
steps.abort: If legitimate disruption is found, narrow the block scope or add a documented exception.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains
steps.desc: Re-scan remediated hosts for scheduled tasks, startup items, or registry run-keys the malware may have used for persistence.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.

ITID-44922.def: A defensive/response action classification (not an adversary technique) in which the SOC or network operations team adds a DNS-layer block (via a DNS firewall, RPZ deny rule, or secure-web-gateway DNS filtering policy) against a confirmed C2 domain, preventing resolution of that domain from the organization's network as part of active incident containment.
ITID-44922.purpose: Captures the organization's deliberate DNS-layer block applied against a known malicious C2 domain during incident response.
scopeIncludes: DNS firewall/RPZ deny rule added for a confirmed C2 domain
Secure web gateway DNS-category or explicit-domain block deployed against a confirmed C2 domain
Emergency/out-of-cycle DNS block deployment during active incident response
scopeExcludes: Direct IP address blocking at the firewall/proxy layer (ITID-44921)
Threat-intel-feed-driven automated blocklist updates at scale rather than a single incident-driven manual block (ITID-44923)
DNS sinkholing that redirects (rather than simply denies) resolution (ITID-44911/44912)
ITID-44922.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf classifies the organization's own disruption action; document the severity of the underlying C2 incident separately.
ITID-44922.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes: DNS blocking is typically applied promptly once a C2 domain is confirmed, as a fast and low-risk containment action.
ITID-44922.escalation: Coordinate with legal/threat intel before any external-facing blocklist action affecting shared or third-party domains (e.g., a compromised legitimate service used as C2 infrastructure); notify network operations to avoid unintended impact.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs a defender action; associated evidence is the DNS block rule change record
Post-block DNS query logs showing attempted (and now blocked) resolution requests from internal hosts, useful for identifying additional infected hosts
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents a defensive action taken in response to an identified C2 domain
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf; document root causes under the originating C2 incident's own ITID classification
mitreTechniques: T1568.002 Dynamic Resolution: Domain Generation Algorithms
controls: DNS firewall/RPZ or secure web gateway DNS filtering capability
Emergency change-management process for expedited DNS block deployment during active incidents
ITID-44922.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity; post-block DNS query logs become a detection source for identifying additional infected hosts.
ITID-44922.response: Validate the DNS block is functioning (test/verify resolution failure), monitor blocked-query logs to identify additional infected hosts, and monitor for the adversary's fallback C2 mechanism.
metrics: Count of C2 domains blocked at the DNS layer per year
Mean time from C2 domain confirmation to block deployment
Count of additional infected hosts identified via blocked-query logs
detections: Post-block DNS query log monitoring for infected-host identification
ITID-44922.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty for this leaf and its siblings in the C2 Disruption and Takedown Methods branch.

playbook.name: DNS-Layer Block Applied Against Known C2 Domain
playbook.description: The organization needs to apply a DNS-layer block against a known-malicious C2 domain as a defensive disruption action, ensuring the block is scoped correctly so it does not break legitimate services that may share the parent domain or DNS infrastructure.

steps.title: Confirm the domain is malicious and assess shared-infrastructure risk
steps.desc: Validate the domain against threat intelligence and check whether it is dedicated malicious infrastructure or a compromised legitimate domain/subdomain with ongoing legitimate use.
steps.guidance: Check current content, WHOIS history, and any legitimate subdomains sharing the parent zone to assess how narrowly the block must be scoped.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment informing the appropriate block scope (full domain vs. specific subdomain/record).
steps.abort: If the domain cannot be confirmed malicious, do not proceed with blocking.
steps.tool: WHOIS / passive DNS / threat intel platform

steps.title: Apply the DNS block and validate it takes effect
steps.desc: Implement the DNS firewall/RPZ entry for the target domain and validate via test resolution that it correctly resolves to a blocked/null response.
steps.outcome: DNS resolution of the malicious domain is confirmed blocked for internal clients.
steps.abort: If the block does not take effect as expected, troubleshoot DNS forwarding/caching before proceeding.

steps.title: Remediate hosts previously observed resolving the blocked domain
steps.desc: Identify and remediate any internal hosts that were resolving/connecting to the domain prior to the block, since the block alone does not remove existing infections.
steps.outcome: Previously affected hosts are remediated.

steps.title: Maintain the block as a standing control and monitor
steps.desc: Keep the DNS block in place as a durable control and monitor blocked-query logs for continued attempts indicating lingering infection or actor persistence.
steps.outcome: Blocked-query logs decline to zero, confirming successful remediation.

steps.title: Document the block and outcomes
steps.desc: Record the domain, block scope decision, and remediation outcomes for future reference and to inform blocklist governance.
steps.outcome: A documented blocking record supporting future similar actions.

steps.title: Determine the correct DNS block mechanism and scope
steps.desc: Decide whether to implement the block via DNS firewall/RPZ, internal authoritative override, or upstream resolver policy, and at what granularity (exact FQDN vs. wildcard).
steps.guidance: Prefer the narrowest scope (exact FQDN) unless the DGA/fast-flux nature of the threat requires wildcard coverage.
steps.outcome: A documented block mechanism and scope decision.

steps.title: Verify no legitimate traffic is impacted by the block
steps.desc: Monitor for help desk tickets, application errors, or business complaints indicating the block has disrupted legitimate services sharing the domain.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of no legitimate service disruption from the block.
steps.abort: If legitimate disruption is found, narrow the block scope (subdomain-specific) or add a documented exception.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains
steps.desc: Re-scan remediated hosts for scheduled tasks, startup items, or registry run-keys the malware may have used for persistence.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.

ITID-44923.def: A defensive/response action classification (not an adversary technique) describing the organization's automated ingestion of a threat-intelligence feed's C2 indicator list into firewall, proxy, or DNS blocking infrastructure on a recurring basis, enabling proactive blocking of newly-published C2 indicators without requiring a manual, per-incident block action.
ITID-44923.purpose: Captures the organization's use of an automated, threat-intelligence-feed-driven pipeline to update C2 IP/domain blocklists at scale, distinct from a single manual incident-driven block.
scopeIncludes: Scheduled/automated ingestion of a threat-intel feed's C2 IP/domain indicators into blocking infrastructure
Bulk blocklist update applied as part of a subscription/feed integration rather than a single confirmed-incident block
Automated removal/expiry of stale indicators as part of the feed-driven pipeline
scopeExcludes: A single, manually-applied firewall/proxy IP block tied to a specific confirmed incident (ITID-44921)
A single, manually-applied DNS-layer domain block tied to a specific confirmed incident (ITID-44922)
ITID-44923.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf classifies the organization's own proactive defensive process, not a specific incident's severity.
ITID-44923.priority: P3 for routine feed updates; escalate to P1 handling if an automated update is later found to correspond to indicators actively impacting the organization.
ITID-44923.escalation: Escalate to threat intel/detection engineering if a feed-driven block causes an unexpected business impact (false positive) or if automated blocking reveals indicators matching an active internal incident.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs a defender process; associated evidence is the feed-ingestion pipeline's update logs
Blocklist update logs showing indicator additions/removals correlated with feed publication timestamps
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents a proactive defensive process
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf
controls: Threat-intel feed integration with automated blocklist update pipeline
False-positive review/exception process for automated blocklist updates
Periodic validation that the feed-driven pipeline is functioning and current
ITID-44923.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity directly; the pipeline's effectiveness is measured by how many subsequent internal-host connection attempts it successfully denies.
ITID-44923.response: Monitor pipeline health and false-positive rate, and periodically validate that feed-driven blocks are current and effective; investigate any case where an automated block corresponds to activity also seen in an active internal incident.
metrics: Count of indicators ingested/blocked via the automated pipeline per period
False-positive rate of automated blocklist updates
Pipeline update latency versus feed publication time
detections: Pipeline health monitoring: feed ingestion/update failure alert
ITID-44923.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty. Differentiates from ITID-44921/44922 by scale/automation: this leaf covers the ongoing, feed-driven bulk process, not a single incident-driven manual block.

playbook.name: Threat Intelligence Feed-Driven Automated C2 Blocklist Update
playbook.description: An automated threat intelligence feed integration has pushed new C2 indicators into the organization's blocklists, and the organization needs to validate the automated update was applied correctly and did not introduce false positives that break legitimate traffic.

steps.title: Review the automated feed update for scope and volume anomalies
steps.desc: Review the specific batch of indicators pushed by the automated threat intel feed integration, checking for unusually large volume, overly broad entries (e.g., wildcard/CIDR ranges), or entries from a feed source with a history of false positives.
steps.guidance: Automated feed pushes can occasionally include mis-scoped or erroneous entries (e.g., a popular CDN IP mistakenly flagged); flag any suspicious entries for manual review before or immediately after they take effect.
steps.outcome: The update batch is reviewed, with any suspicious/overly broad entries flagged for manual verification.
steps.abort: If the entire batch appears anomalous (e.g., feed source compromise or integration malfunction), pause the automated push pending investigation.

steps.title: Confirm the blocklist update has been correctly applied across enforcement points
steps.desc: Verify the new C2 indicators are active across all relevant enforcement points (DNS firewall, perimeter firewall, secure web gateway) consistent with the automation's intended scope.
steps.outcome: Confirmed consistent enforcement of the new indicators across all intended control points.
steps.tool: DNS firewall / firewall / secure web gateway consoles

steps.title: Investigate and remediate any hosts flagged as communicating with the newly blocked indicators
steps.desc: Review logs for any internal hosts that were communicating with the newly added (and confirmed malicious) indicators prior to the block, and remediate accordingly.
steps.outcome: Any previously undetected infections surfaced by the new indicators are remediated.

steps.title: Confirm normal business operations and monitor blocklist health
steps.desc: Confirm no ongoing legitimate service disruption from the update and monitor the automated feed integration's future pushes with the same review process.
steps.outcome: Normal operations continue with no residual false-positive impact.

steps.title: Document the feed performance and refine automation safeguards
steps.desc: Record any false positives, feed source reliability observations, and refine the automation's safeguards (e.g., staged rollout, confidence-score thresholds, human-review gates for broad entries) to reduce future risk.
steps.outcome: Improved automated blocklist update process with reduced false-positive risk.

steps.title: Cross-check flagged entries against internal traffic and business context
steps.desc: For any flagged entries, check whether they correspond to legitimate infrastructure the organization or its partners use, before or shortly after they go live.
steps.outcome: Flagged entries are confirmed as either correctly malicious or identified as false positives requiring an exception.

steps.title: Remove or except any confirmed false-positive entries
steps.desc: For any entries confirmed as false positives, remove them from the blocklist or add a documented exception, and provide feedback to the feed provider where a feedback mechanism exists.
steps.outcome: False-positive entries are excepted and legitimate traffic is restored.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains on remediated hosts
steps.desc: Re-scan remediated hosts for scheduled tasks, startup items, or registry run-keys the malware may have used for persistence.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General IP and Domain Blocking Action
playbook.description: The organization needs to execute an IP or domain blocking action against C2 infrastructure that does not fit a more specific blocking subtype, ensuring it is correctly scoped to avoid disrupting legitimate traffic.

steps.title: Confirm the indicator is malicious and assess shared-infrastructure risk
steps.desc: Validate the IP/domain against threat intelligence and assess whether it is dedicated malicious infrastructure or shared infrastructure with legitimate co-tenants.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment informing appropriate block scope.
steps.abort: If the indicator cannot be confirmed malicious, do not proceed with blocking.

steps.title: Apply the block and validate it takes effect
steps.desc: Implement the block and validate via test traffic that it functions as expected.
steps.outcome: The indicator is confirmed blocked.
steps.abort: If the block does not take effect, troubleshoot before proceeding.
steps.tool: DNS firewall / perimeter firewall / secure web gateway

steps.title: Remediate hosts previously observed communicating with the blocked indicator
steps.desc: Identify and remediate any internal hosts that were communicating with the indicator prior to the block.
steps.outcome: Previously affected hosts are remediated.

steps.title: Maintain the block as a standing control and monitor
steps.desc: Keep the block in place and monitor for continued blocked-attempt logs.
steps.outcome: Blocked-attempt logs decline to zero.

steps.title: Document the block and outcomes
steps.desc: Record the indicator, scope decision, and remediation outcomes.
steps.outcome: A documented blocking record for future reference.

steps.title: Determine the correct block mechanism and scope
steps.desc: Decide the appropriate enforcement point (DNS firewall, perimeter firewall, secure web gateway) and granularity for the block.
steps.outcome: A documented block mechanism and scope decision.

steps.title: Verify no legitimate traffic is impacted
steps.desc: Monitor for signs of legitimate service disruption from the block.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of no legitimate service disruption.
steps.abort: If disruption is found, narrow scope or add an exception.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains
steps.desc: Re-scan remediated hosts for persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.

ITID-44931.def: A defensive/response action classification (not an adversary technique) in which the organization's EDR platform, either through automated policy or analyst-initiated response, terminates a process identified as a C2 implant on a host, immediately stopping that specific execution instance as an endpoint-level disruption action.
ITID-44931.purpose: Captures the organization's EDR-triggered (automated or analyst-initiated) termination of a process confirmed to be a C2 implant on an endpoint.
scopeIncludes: Automated EDR policy killing a process matching a known-malicious C2 implant signature/behavior
Analyst-initiated manual process termination via the EDR console during active investigation
Process termination as a first-response action pending fuller host containment
scopeExcludes: Full network isolation of the host (ITID-44932), a broader containment action than single-process termination
Sinkholing or blocking actions targeting the C2 infrastructure rather than the endpoint process (ITID-44911/44921/44922)
ITID-44931.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf classifies the organization's own disruption action; document the severity of the underlying C2 incident separately.
ITID-44931.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes: process termination is typically one of the fastest available endpoint-level containment actions once a C2 implant is confirmed.
ITID-44931.escalation: Coordinate with IR before termination where forensic memory capture is needed first, since killing the process may lose volatile evidence; for automated EDR-policy terminations, ensure the resulting alert routes to IR for follow-up investigation.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs a defender action; associated evidence is the EDR termination event record
EDR alert/log confirming successful process termination and any persistence mechanism that subsequently attempts to relaunch it
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents a defensive action taken in response to an identified C2 implant process
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf; document root causes under the originating C2 incident's own ITID classification
mitreTechniques: T1543 Create or Modify System Process
controls: EDR platform with automated response/kill-process policy capability
Analyst runbook for manual process termination during active investigation
Memory-capture-before-kill procedure for cases requiring forensic preservation
ITID-44931.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity; the termination event itself, combined with monitoring for relaunch/persistence attempts, is useful for confirming whether a persistence mechanism remains active.
ITID-44931.response: Validate the process does not relaunch via an undiscovered persistence mechanism, capture memory forensics beforehand where feasible, and proceed to full host containment/eradication rather than treating process termination alone as resolution.
metrics: Count of EDR-triggered C2 process terminations per year
Rate of relaunch/persistence-mechanism detection following termination
detections: EDR: process relaunch attempt following termination (indicates undiscovered persistence)
ITID-44931.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty for this leaf and its siblings in the C2 Disruption and Takedown Methods branch.

playbook.name: EDR-Triggered Process Termination of C2 Implant
playbook.description: The organization's EDR platform has automatically or manually terminated a process identified as a C2 implant, and the response team must validate the termination was effective, safe, and did not miss any secondary/persistent components.

steps.title: Confirm the terminated process was correctly identified as the C2 implant
steps.desc: Review the EDR alert and process tree to confirm the terminated process was indeed the malicious C2 implant and not a legitimate process incorrectly flagged.
steps.guidance: Check process hash, parent-child relationships, and behavioral indicators (network connections, file writes) that triggered the EDR detection.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that the terminated process was correctly identified as malicious.
steps.abort: If the terminated process appears to be a legitimate application, restore it and investigate the EDR detection logic for a false positive.

steps.title: Isolate the host pending full remediation
steps.desc: Isolate the host via EDR/NAC to prevent any respawned implant or watchdog process from re-establishing C2 communication while eradication is completed.
steps.outcome: The host is fully isolated from the network.

steps.title: Remove all persistence mechanisms and the implant's on-disk artifacts
steps.desc: Remove the implant binary, any watchdog/persistence processes, and associated on-disk artifacts identified during the identification phase.
steps.outcome: The host is confirmed clean via a full EDR scan with no remaining implant artifacts.
steps.abort: If persistence is deeply embedded (bootkit/firmware), reimage the host instead.

steps.title: Restore the host to production and monitor for respawn attempts
steps.desc: Return the remediated host to the network with EDR monitoring for any attempt to relaunch the terminated process or re-establish C2 communication.
steps.outcome: No recurrence of the implant or C2 communication.

steps.title: Document the EDR detection and termination effectiveness
steps.desc: Record the implant details, EDR detection logic effectiveness, and any gaps (e.g., missed persistence mechanism) for detection content improvement.
steps.outcome: Updated EDR detection/response playbook content based on findings.

steps.title: Determine whether termination fully stopped C2 communication or only the visible process
steps.desc: Check network telemetry to confirm the C2 beaconing actually stopped after process termination, since some malware maintains a separate watchdog or persistence process that can respawn the implant.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of whether C2 communication has fully ceased or is continuing via a secondary process.

steps.title: Block the C2 infrastructure the terminated process was communicating with
steps.desc: Block the associated C2 IP/domain at the perimeter as a defense-in-depth measure in case the implant respawns before eradication is complete.
steps.outcome: Even if the implant respawns, it cannot reach its C2 destination.

steps.title: Identify persistence mechanisms that could respawn the implant
steps.desc: Review scheduled tasks, services, startup items, and registry run-keys on the host for any mechanism that could relaunch the terminated process.
steps.outcome: Any persistence mechanisms are identified for removal.

ITID-44932.def: A defensive/response action classification (not an adversary technique) in which the organization's EDR platform or network access control isolates an endpoint from the network (allowing only management-plane connectivity to the security tooling) to immediately sever any active C2 connection from that host, used when broader containment is warranted beyond terminating a single process.
ITID-44932.purpose: Captures the organization's use of host network isolation to sever an active C2 connection, cutting the endpoint off from the network rather than only terminating the offending process.
scopeIncludes: EDR-initiated host isolation (network quarantine) applied to a host with confirmed active C2 communication
NAC-driven VLAN quarantine achieving equivalent isolation
Isolation applied as a precautionary measure pending full investigation of a suspected C2-communicating host
scopeExcludes: Termination of the specific C2 implant process without full network isolation (ITID-44931)
Blocking of the C2 infrastructure itself (IP/domain) rather than isolating the affected endpoint (ITID-44921/44922)
ITID-44932.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf classifies the organization's own disruption action; document the severity of the underlying C2 incident separately.
ITID-44932.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes: host isolation is typically applied promptly once active C2 communication is confirmed, especially where lateral movement risk is present.
ITID-44932.escalation: Coordinate with business/asset owners before isolating a production-critical host, since isolation halts all normal host function; for less time-critical cases, brief the affected team before isolating to manage business impact.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs a defender action; associated evidence is the isolation event record from the EDR/NAC platform
Post-isolation telemetry confirming the host's C2 connection has been severed and no further outbound C2 traffic is observed
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents a defensive action taken in response to an identified active C2 connection
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf; document root causes under the originating C2 incident's own ITID classification
controls: EDR platform with host isolation/network quarantine capability
NAC-driven VLAN quarantine as an equivalent/backup isolation mechanism
Business-impact notification process for production-host isolation
ITID-44932.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity; the isolation event and subsequent telemetry confirm containment effectiveness.
ITID-44932.response: Validate the sinkhole/isolation is functioning and monitor for the adversary's fallback C2 mechanism, since the implant may still be resident on the host and attempt reconnection once isolation is lifted; proceed to full eradication before returning the host to the network.
metrics: Count of hosts isolated for confirmed C2 activity per year
Mean time from C2 detection to host isolation
Mean isolation duration before eradication and return to service
detections: Post-isolation telemetry: confirmation of severed C2 connection
ITID-44932.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty for this leaf and its siblings in the C2 Disruption and Takedown Methods branch. Differentiates from ITID-44931 by scope: this leaf is full network isolation, not single-process termination.

playbook.name: Host Isolation to Sever Active C2 Connection
playbook.description: The response team needs to isolate a host from the network to sever an active C2 connection, ensuring the isolation is applied correctly and does not disrupt investigation capability or unrelated legitimate business processes running on the host.

steps.title: Confirm the host and active C2 session requiring isolation
steps.desc: Confirm the specific host and the active C2 session/connection that isolation is intended to sever, and assess any business-critical processes running on the host that isolation might impact.
steps.guidance: Check whether the host runs any shared services (e.g., a file server or application backend) whose sudden isolation could cause broader business disruption, informing whether isolation should be immediate or coordinated.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the host's role and the urgency/coordination needs for isolation.

steps.title: Apply isolation and validate the C2 connection is severed
steps.desc: Execute the isolation action and validate via network telemetry that the active C2 connection has been terminated and no further C2 traffic is flowing from the host.
steps.outcome: Confirmed severance of the C2 connection with the host otherwise isolated from the network.
steps.abort: If isolation fails to take effect (e.g., EDR agent unresponsive), escalate to NAC/switch-port isolation immediately.

steps.title: Remove the C2 implant from the isolated host
steps.desc: While the host remains isolated, identify and remove the malware/implant responsible for the C2 connection.
steps.outcome: The host is confirmed clean via EDR scan while still isolated.
steps.abort: If persistence is deeply embedded, reimage the host instead.

steps.title: Lift isolation and restore the host to production with monitoring
steps.desc: Once eradication is confirmed complete, remove the isolation and return the host to normal network operation with heightened monitoring for any recurrence.
steps.outcome: The host resumes normal operation with no recurrence of C2 activity.

steps.title: Document the isolation action and effectiveness
steps.desc: Record the isolation method used, its effectiveness, and any business impact experienced, refining the isolation procedure/runbook accordingly.
steps.outcome: An improved isolation runbook informed by this incident's outcome.

steps.title: Select the appropriate isolation method
steps.desc: Decide between EDR-based host isolation (agent-enforced network lockdown while preserving remote forensic access) versus NAC/switch-port-based isolation (physical network cutoff), based on the urgency and forensic needs of the case.
steps.guidance: EDR-based isolation is generally preferred where available since it preserves remote investigative access; NAC-based isolation may be necessary if the EDR agent itself may be compromised/disabled.
steps.outcome: An isolation method is selected appropriate to the situation.

steps.title: Preserve remote forensic access where the isolation method allows it
steps.desc: Confirm that, despite network isolation, the response team retains the ability to remotely collect forensic artifacts (memory, disk, process list) from the host via the EDR's isolated-mode channel.
steps.outcome: Forensic collection capability is confirmed intact despite isolation.
steps.abort: If remote access is lost, plan for physical/on-site forensic collection instead.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains
steps.desc: Re-scan the host for scheduled tasks, startup items, or registry run-keys the malware may have used for persistence, prior to lifting isolation.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.

ITID-44933.def: A catch-all classification for the organization's own endpoint-level C2 disruption action where the specific mechanism (process termination or network isolation) has not been characterized, or does not match an existing sibling leaf.
ITID-44933.purpose: Intake bucket for a confirmed endpoint C2 disruption action that does not fit the process-termination or host-isolation leaves.
scopeIncludes: Endpoint C2 disruption actions pending further characterization of mechanism
Endpoint disruption actions using a mechanism other than process termination or network isolation
scopeExcludes: EDR-triggered process termination of C2 implant (ITID-44931)
Host isolation to sever active C2 connection (ITID-44932)
ITID-44933.severity: Not applicable — this leaf classifies the organization's own response action.
ITID-44933.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes, consistent with the sibling leaves.
ITID-44933.escalation: Coordinate with IR per standard endpoint disruption handling; reclassify once the specific mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs a defender action
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf
controls: EDR platform response capability consistent with the sibling leaves
ITID-44933.response: Identify the specific endpoint disruption mechanism used and reclassify to a specific sibling ITID where possible.
metrics: Count of incidents initially filed here later reclassified
detections: N/A — this leaf documents a response action
ITID-44933.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty. Use sparingly; prefer ITID-44931 or ITID-44932 whenever the mechanism is known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Endpoint C2 Disruption
playbook.description: The response team needs to execute an endpoint-level action to disrupt an active C2 connection that does not fit a more specific endpoint C2 disruption subtype, ensuring the action is effective without unnecessary business disruption.

steps.title: Confirm the host and C2 activity requiring disruption
steps.desc: Confirm the specific host and C2 activity, and assess the host's role and any business-critical processes that the disruption action might impact.
steps.outcome: A documented assessment of the host's role and the appropriate disruption approach.

steps.title: Apply the disruption action and validate effectiveness
steps.desc: Execute the selected action and validate via network/endpoint telemetry that the C2 activity has been disrupted.
steps.outcome: Confirmed disruption of the C2 activity.
steps.abort: If the action fails to take effect, escalate to a more forceful containment method.

steps.title: Remove the C2 implant from the affected host
steps.desc: Identify and remove the malware/implant responsible for the C2 activity.
steps.outcome: The host is confirmed clean via EDR scan.
steps.abort: If persistence is deeply embedded, reimage the host instead.

steps.title: Restore the host to production with monitoring
steps.desc: Return the remediated host to normal operation with heightened monitoring for recurrence.
steps.outcome: The host resumes normal operation with no recurrence of C2 activity.

steps.title: Document the disruption action and effectiveness
steps.desc: Record the action taken, its effectiveness, and any business impact, refining response procedures accordingly.
steps.outcome: Improved endpoint disruption procedures informed by this incident.

steps.title: Select the appropriate endpoint disruption method
steps.desc: Decide on the appropriate endpoint-level action (process termination, network isolation, or other EDR-driven response) based on the situation.
steps.outcome: An appropriate disruption method is selected.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence during the disruption action
steps.desc: Ensure forensic artifacts are captured before or during the disruption action to support eradication and root-cause analysis.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence is preserved.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains
steps.desc: Re-scan the host for scheduled tasks, startup items, or registry run-keys the malware may have used for persistence.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.

ITID-44941.def: A defensive/response event classification (not an adversary technique) documenting that law enforcement (domestic or international) seized, disabled, or took legal control of C2 infrastructure relevant to an incident the organization is actively responding to, which may abruptly change the state of the incident (e.g., C2 traffic stops, notification arrives from law enforcement about victim status) independent of the organization's own containment actions.
ITID-44941.purpose: Captures a law-enforcement-led seizure of C2 infrastructure that materially affects an organization's active incident, whether or not the organization initiated the law enforcement engagement.
scopeIncludes: Law enforcement seizure of a C2 server/domain that the organization was actively investigating or had already contained
Organization notified by law enforcement that it was identified as a victim via seized C2 infrastructure (e.g., victim data found on a seized server)
Change in incident status (e.g., C2 traffic ceasing) attributable to a law enforcement action rather than the organization's own disruption
scopeExcludes: A coordinated multi-vendor industry botnet takedown not specifically led by law enforcement (ITID-44942)
The organization's own DNS/IP/domain blocking or sinkholing actions (ITID-449xx blocking/sinkholing leaves), which are separate from law enforcement action
ITID-44941.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf documents an external event affecting the organization's incident; document the severity of the underlying C2 incident separately.
ITID-44941.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes when it materially changes an active incident's status; P2 for purely informational notifications about historical/closed incidents.
ITID-44941.escalation: Escalate to legal and executive leadership immediately upon any law enforcement contact regarding the organization's status as a victim; coordinate all further communication with law enforcement through legal counsel.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs an external event; associated evidence is the law enforcement notification/seizure order and any resulting change in observed C2 activity
Abrupt cessation of previously-observed C2 traffic correlating with public reporting of a law enforcement takedown
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents a law enforcement disruption event affecting the organization's incident
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf; document root causes under the originating C2 incident's own ITID classification
controls: Legal/law-enforcement liaison process for receiving and validating victim notifications
Incident status re-assessment procedure triggered by external takedown events
ITID-44941.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity directly; detection here is of the law enforcement action's effect on the organization's own incident (e.g., traffic cessation, formal notification).
ITID-44941.response: Validate the authenticity of any law enforcement notification through official channels before acting on it, reassess the incident's containment/eradication status in light of the takedown, and continue monitoring for the adversary's fallback infrastructure.
metrics: Count of incidents affected by a law enforcement C2 infrastructure seizure per year
Mean time from seizure event to organizational incident status reassessment
detections: Traffic-cessation correlation: C2 activity stopping in alignment with public takedown reporting
ITID-44941.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive/law-enforcement takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty for this leaf and its siblings.

playbook.name: Law Enforcement-Led C2 Infrastructure Seizure Affecting Active Incident
playbook.description: Law enforcement has seized or disrupted C2 infrastructure that the organization's active incident depends on for tracking/analysis, requiring the response team to adapt its incident handling to the sudden loss of that infrastructure and coordinate evidence sharing with the seizing authority.

steps.title: Confirm the seizure and assess impact on the active incident
steps.desc: Confirm reports (via threat intel, public reporting, or direct law enforcement contact) that the C2 infrastructure relevant to the organization's active incident has been seized or disrupted, and assess how this affects the organization's ongoing investigation and containment posture.
steps.guidance: A sudden C2 outage from external causes can be mistaken for a self-inflicted control failure or an actor going dark voluntarily — confirm the law enforcement cause before assuming resolution.
steps.outcome: Confirmation that the C2 infrastructure was law-enforcement-seized, with an assessment of the impact on the organization's incident (e.g., is the threat now neutralized, or might the actor pivot to backup infrastructure).
steps.tool: Public reporting / threat intel platform / law enforcement liaison

steps.title: Preserve and continue internal containment regardless of the external takedown
steps.desc: Do not treat the external takedown as a substitute for internal containment — continue or complete isolation of any internal hosts still exhibiting the implant, since a seized C2 domain does not remove the implant from internal systems.
steps.outcome: Internal containment proceeds unaffected by the external infrastructure change.

steps.title: Complete eradication of the implant regardless of C2 availability
steps.desc: Remove the malware implant and any persistence mechanisms from affected internal hosts, since the implant remains a risk even with its C2 seized (it could still execute local malicious functionality or be reactivated via a fallback channel).
steps.outcome: All affected hosts are confirmed clean of the implant.

steps.title: Restore operations and monitor for fallback infrastructure activation
steps.desc: Return remediated hosts to production with monitoring focused on any fallback/backup C2 mechanisms identified during risk assessment, in case the actor pivots following the takedown.
steps.outcome: No recurrence of C2 activity via primary or fallback infrastructure.

steps.title: Document the incident outcome and law enforcement coordination
steps.desc: Record the incident timeline, the law enforcement action's effect on the case, and any coordination/evidence-sharing outcome for the incident report and future reference.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive incident report capturing the external takedown's role in incident resolution.

steps.title: Determine whether the organization is a known victim in the law enforcement action
steps.desc: Determine whether the seizing law enforcement/agency is aware the organization was a victim of the infrastructure taken down, and whether the organization should proactively reach out.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal counsel on the approach to law enforcement contact.
steps.outcome: Clarity on the organization's status relative to the law enforcement action and next engagement steps.

steps.title: Preserve evidence for coordination with the seizing authority
steps.desc: Preserve logs, samples, and indicators related to the organization's exposure to the seized infrastructure in a manner suitable for sharing with law enforcement if requested, following legal counsel's guidance on format and chain of custody.
steps.outcome: Evidence is preserved in a legally sound format for potential law enforcement coordination.

steps.title: Assess risk of actor pivot to backup/alternative infrastructure
steps.desc: Given that sophisticated actors often maintain backup C2 infrastructure, assess whether the affected implant(s) in the organization's environment have known fallback mechanisms that could reactivate the incident via new infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Reverse-engineer or check threat intel for known fallback C2 mechanisms of the specific malware family involved.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment of potential actor pivot to new infrastructure.

ITID-44942.def: A defensive/response event classification (not an adversary technique) documenting that a coordinated, multi-vendor industry effort (security vendors, cloud providers, registrars acting in concert, with or without law enforcement participation) disrupted botnet C2 infrastructure relevant to an incident the organization is actively responding to, changing the state of that incident independent of the organization's own containment actions.
ITID-44942.purpose: Captures a coordinated, multi-vendor (industry-led, not necessarily law-enforcement-led) botnet takedown that materially affects an organization's active incident.
scopeIncludes: Coordinated sinkholing/seizure of botnet C2 infrastructure by a multi-vendor industry coalition affecting hosts within the organization
Organization notified by a security vendor/CERT that its IP space was identified within a botnet population as part of a coordinated takedown effort
Change in incident status attributable to an industry-coordinated takedown rather than the organization's own disruption
scopeExcludes: A takedown specifically led and legally executed by law enforcement (ITID-44941)
The organization's own DNS/IP/domain blocking or sinkholing actions (ITID-449xx blocking/sinkholing leaves)
ITID-44942.severity: Not applicable in the traditional threat-severity sense — this leaf documents an external event affecting the organization's incident; document the severity of the underlying botnet-related incident separately.
ITID-44942.priority: P1 for IR-process purposes when it materially changes an active incident's status; P2 for purely informational notifications.
ITID-44942.escalation: Escalate to IR leadership to reassess remediation status for any internal hosts identified as bots via the coordinated takedown; coordinate with the notifying vendor/CERT for indicator sharing.
indicators: N/A — this leaf logs an external event; associated evidence is the vendor/CERT notification and any resulting change in observed C2 activity
Abrupt cessation of previously-observed botnet C2 traffic correlating with public reporting of a coordinated takedown
vectors: N/A — not an attack vector; this leaf documents an industry-coordinated disruption event affecting the organization's incident
rootCauses: N/A — not a root-cause-bearing leaf; document root causes under the originating botnet incident's own ITID classification (see ITID-317xx and ITID-4473x)
controls: Threat-intel/CERT liaison process for receiving and validating takedown-related victim notifications
Incident status re-assessment procedure triggered by external takedown events
ITID-44942.detection: N/A for detecting adversary activity directly; detection here is of the takedown's effect on the organization's own incident (e.g., traffic cessation, formal notification).
ITID-44942.response: Validate the notification through official channels, remediate any confirmed internal bot hosts identified through the coordinated effort, and continue monitoring for the botnet operator's fallback infrastructure or re-recruitment attempts.
metrics: Count of incidents affected by a coordinated botnet takedown per year
Count of internal hosts remediated as a result of takedown-driven notification
detections: Traffic-cessation correlation: botnet C2 activity stopping in alignment with public takedown reporting
ITID-44942.notes: ATT&CK documents attacker behavior, not defensive/industry takedown actions, so mapped_mitre_tactics/techniques are intentionally left empty. Differentiates from ITID-44941 by leading party: this leaf covers industry/multi-vendor-coordinated efforts, which may or may not include law enforcement, versus a takedown specifically led by law enforcement.

playbook.name: Coordinated Multi-Vendor Botnet Takedown Impacting Organization's Incident
playbook.description: A coordinated multi-vendor/multi-agency botnet takedown operation has disrupted botnet infrastructure that overlaps with the organization's active incident, requiring the response team to reconcile the takedown's effects with ongoing internal remediation and assess any residual risk from partial takedown coverage.

steps.title: Confirm the takedown scope and its relevance to the organization's incident
steps.desc: Review public reporting, vendor advisories, or direct notification from participating organizations (security vendors, ISACs, law enforcement) about the takedown's scope, and determine whether the botnet infrastructure the organization's incident involves was fully covered.
steps.guidance: Multi-vendor takedowns often only disrupt a portion of a botnet's total infrastructure (e.g., primary C2 servers but not all fallback DGA domains) — do not assume complete neutralization.
steps.outcome: A documented understanding of what was and was not covered by the takedown, relative to the organization's specific incident.
steps.tool: Public reporting / vendor advisories / threat intel platform

steps.title: Continue internal containment independent of the takedown's status
steps.desc: Isolate all confirmed internal bot hosts regardless of the external takedown's progress, since internal remediation remains necessary even with external infrastructure disrupted.
steps.outcome: Internal containment proceeds and is not delayed pending confirmation of the takedown's completeness.

steps.title: Remove the bot implant from all confirmed internal hosts
steps.desc: Remove the malicious payload and persistence mechanisms from all confirmed bot hosts, independent of the takedown's external effects.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean via EDR scan.

steps.title: Restore hosts and monitor for reconstitution of the botnet
steps.desc: Return remediated hosts to production with monitoring for any signs the botnet operators have reconstituted infrastructure following the takedown.
steps.guidance: Botnet operators sometimes rebuild infrastructure weeks after a takedown; maintain a longer monitoring window than typical.
steps.outcome: No recurrence of botnet check-in activity during the extended monitoring window.

steps.title: Document the takedown's effect on the organization's incident
steps.desc: Record how the coordinated takedown intersected with the organization's internal response, including any gaps in coverage and lessons for engaging with future coordinated takedown efforts.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive incident report capturing the interaction between the external takedown and internal remediation.

steps.title: Assess residual risk from infrastructure not covered by the takedown
steps.desc: Identify any fallback mechanisms (DGA, backup C2 lists, alternative protocols) the botnet malware possesses that may not have been addressed by the takedown, using reverse engineering or threat intel on the specific malware family.
steps.outcome: A documented residual risk assessment informing whether internal remediation must proceed independent of the takedown's effects.

steps.title: Apply internal blocking for any residual/fallback infrastructure
steps.desc: Block any fallback C2 mechanisms identified during the residual risk assessment that the coordinated takedown did not address.
steps.outcome: Residual C2 pathways not covered by the external takedown are blocked internally.

steps.title: Reconcile internal host inventory against the takedown's published indicators
steps.desc: Cross-reference the organization's internal hunt for infected hosts against any indicators/sinkhole data shared as part of the coordinated takedown (some takedowns include victim notification via sinkhole telemetry).
steps.guidance: Check whether the organization received or should proactively request victim notification data from the takedown coordinators.
steps.outcome: A complete, reconciled list of internal hosts confirmed part of the botnet.

ITID-44943.def: A catch-all classification for an external C2 infrastructure takedown event affecting an organization's active incident where the specific leading party (law enforcement or a multi-vendor industry coalition) has not been characterized, or does not match an existing sibling leaf.
ITID-44943.purpose: Intake bucket for a confirmed law-enforcement or industry-coordinated C2 takedown event that does not fit the law-enforcement-led or multi-vendor-coordinated leaves.
scopeIncludes: Takedown events pending further characterization of the leading party
Takedown events led by a party other than law enforcement or a multi-vendor industry coalition (e.g., a single vendor acting unilaterally)
scopeExcludes: Law enforcement-led C2 infrastructure seizure affecting active incident (ITID-44941)
Coordinated multi-vendor botnet takedown impacting organization's incident (ITID-44942)

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Law Enforcement C2 Takedown
playbook.description: An external law enforcement or coordinated takedown action has disrupted C2 infrastructure relevant to the organization's incident in a manner that does not fit a more specific takedown subtype, requiring the response team to adapt internal handling and coordinate evidence sharing as appropriate.

steps.title: Confirm the takedown and assess impact on the organization's incident
steps.desc: Confirm reports of the external takedown action and assess how it affects the organization's ongoing investigation and containment posture.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of the takedown's cause and an assessment of its impact on the incident.

steps.title: Continue internal containment independent of the external takedown
steps.desc: Proceed with or complete isolation of internal hosts still exhibiting the implant, since the external takedown does not remove the implant from internal systems.
steps.outcome: Internal containment proceeds unaffected by the external infrastructure change.

steps.title: Complete eradication of the implant regardless of C2 availability
steps.desc: Remove the malware implant and persistence mechanisms from affected internal hosts.
steps.outcome: All affected hosts are confirmed clean of the implant.

steps.title: Restore operations and monitor for fallback infrastructure activation
steps.desc: Return remediated hosts to production with monitoring for any fallback C2 mechanisms in case the actor pivots.
steps.outcome: No recurrence of C2 activity via primary or fallback infrastructure.

steps.title: Document the incident outcome and coordination
steps.desc: Record the incident timeline, the external action's effect on the case, and any coordination outcome for future reference.
steps.outcome: A comprehensive incident report capturing the external action's role in incident resolution.

steps.title: Assess risk of actor pivot to alternative infrastructure
steps.desc: Determine whether the affected implant(s) have known fallback mechanisms that could reactivate the incident via new infrastructure.
steps.outcome: A documented risk assessment of potential actor pivot.

steps.title: Preserve evidence for potential law enforcement coordination
steps.desc: Preserve logs, samples, and indicators related to the organization's exposure in a manner suitable for sharing with law enforcement if requested.
steps.outcome: Evidence is preserved in a legally sound format.

steps.title: Verify no residual persistence remains
steps.desc: Re-scan remediated hosts for scheduled tasks, startup items, or registry run-keys the malware may have used for persistence.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence artifacts remain.
